notes.text: Design refined through further discussion (2026-07-25), before any architect review: (1) two distinct kinds of 'bulk' identified — author-written batch-shaped operations (e.g. batchCreateItems(items[])) need ZERO apigen changes, they're just ordinary Operations; the real generic gap is N-way fan-out of an EXISTING unmodified single-item operation, which is what DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001 actually needs. (2) Corrected an earlier wrong assumption: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts does NOT use createApiPackage or the v2 --use MountCapability loader — it hand-wires extract()/composeSchemas()/plugin.run() directly (v1 OutputPlugin contract). (3) Confirmed --use IS real, load-bearing machinery elsewhere (apigen serve's health plugin: serve.ts pushes '--use','health' to spawn the CLI pipeline) — so batch should be modeled as a genuine MountCapability plugin loaded via --use, consistent with the openapi/health precedent, while consumers on the hand-wired pattern (backlog-style) invoke the same plugin's capabilities.mount.operations() directly rather than going through the CLI loader. (4) Streaming inclusion (not exclusion) resolved via a two-tier design: Tier 1 (day-1, universal) reuses the EXISTING collectWithPhase/ApiStream machinery (already used by apigen-plugin-mcp's single-op streaming path) to give every batch item - unary or streaming - one uniform terminal BatchItemResult shape, working on all four transports today without requiring any transport to gain new streaming capability. Tier 2 (capability-gated, not deferred) lets transports with true live single-op streaming (HTTP/SSE today) project a live tagged-multiplexed batch stream instead of collecting - see the cross-linked note on FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000 for how that epic's landing automatically upgrades Tier 2 per-transport. Next step: architect review of this design, scoped explicitly to apigen-core-client/apigen-engine-runtime + the consumer-authoring experience only (not the pre-existing per-plugin implementation gaps tracked by FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000's children, which are out of scope for this item's review).

Architect review (2026-07-25), scoped explicitly to apigen-core-client/apigen-engine-runtime + consumer-authoring experience only (current per-plugin implementation gaps under FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000 were explicitly out of scope for this review).

VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES. Core insight (batch-shaped ops vs. generic fan-out are different problems) is correct; orchestrating fan-out as pure composition over the existing invoke()/Layer stack is sound. Several parts are under-specified in ways that will force breaking changes as new hosts/transports/consumers arrive.

F1 — _batch's single static Operation cannot represent a polymorphic fan-out target. Operation.kind/safe are per-op static classifications transports read to make wire decisions (safe drives HTTP verb/cacheability, kind distinguishes action/query), but _batch's actual behavior varies per-request based on the runtime `operation` string selected in call.data - no static Operation object can carry that. Required change: mount one synthetic op PER DISTINCT KIND present in the batchable set (_batch/query, _batch/action), each with truthful static kind/safe and an operation enum restricted to ids of that kind - keeps the common single-kind case (e.g. agent-mcp's task) at exactly one extra tool/route/command.

F2 — The proposal's example code calls syntheticOp(id, descriptor) which does not exist anywhere as real, exported code - it appears exactly once, in a JSDoc example comment on MountCapability (apigen-core-client/src/lib/plugin.ts:452), never exported. The one real shipped MountCapability (apigen-plugin-health) hand-builds the full ~10-field Operation literal itself, including a locally-reimplemented seg() helper to avoid a cross-package dependency. Required change: extract and ship a REAL syntheticOp(id, descriptor, fields) helper in apigen-core-client as part of this work, and retrofit apigen-plugin-health onto it in the same change so there is exactly one implementation, not two independently-maintained ones.

F3 — No cross-host contract; invokeBatch/MountCapability is TS-only today with nothing to port. PluginLanguage already includes py/rust/go/java, and a Python runtime already exists (packages/apigen/python/apigen_python/runtime.py, its own invoke/invoke_sync) entirely separate from the TS createInvoker/Layer/MountCapability types. MountedOperation.handler's signature is a TS closure type, not expressible in the Python runtime's model at all. Required change: specify BatchOptions/BatchItemResult as a wire-level JSON-Schema IR independent of the TS invokeBatch function signature (the same separation apigen already uses for Operation's type IR generally) so each host runtime implements fan-out against that wire contract, none depending on the TS implementation.

F4 — BatchOptions is missing per-item cancellation/timeout, will force a breaking change. Call.signal is whole-request cancellation already wired per single op; invokeBatch fans out N invoke() calls but never states whether an individual item's failure/timeout can be cancelled independently of the batch, or whether whole-batch abort propagates to in-flight items. Given onItemError:'continue' is the stated default, 'bound one slow item without killing the whole batch' is near-certain to be requested immediately after ship (it's close to the exact motivating scenario - agent-mcp dispatching to a slow external service per call). Required change: state explicitly whether each fanned-out item gets its own signal derived/linked from the batch's signal, and add itemTimeoutMs?: number to BatchOptions now (even as a stub) so the shape doesn't need a breaking revision on first request.

F5 — Two consumption paths (--use loader vs. hand-wired capabilities.mount.operations()) need an explicit equivalence guarantee. Both paths are legitimate but only acceptable if guaranteed to produce IDENTICAL MountedOperation[] output for the same (descriptor, opts) - otherwise a hand-wiring consumer (like backlog) silently forks from CLI behavior as the plugin evolves. Nothing in the current proposal states or tests this. Required change: state it as an explicit invariant and add a conformance test (analogous to apigen-engine-conformance's existing role) that drives both paths against a fixture descriptor and diffs the output.

F6 (non-blocking, just record it) — Tenet 1 compliance (never derive behavior from source annotations) is already satisfied by the exclude opt-out and dynamic per-item validation reuse; worth stating explicitly in the eventual design doc so a future reviewer doesn't re-litigate it.

Reviewer's summary: ship this, but close F1-F4 before the shape hardens into public API. F1 and F3 are the two most consequential for surviving contact with a second host language and a second transport family; F2 and F5 are cheap to fix now and expensive to retrofit later.

apigen-plugin-cli-output cannot render an operation whose top-level input schema is a discriminated union (oneOf at the schema root) - generates zero flags

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, while designing generic bulk/batch operation support for apigen (FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001) and checking whether apigen's own established discriminated-union convention (`oneOf` + `discriminator`, per `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts`, DESIGN §4.1 `docs/plan/apigen-logical-types`) can be used as an OPERATION's top-level input shape.

**Root cause (traced to real code, not guessed):** `apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts`'s per-operation flag emission (lines ~110-155) calls `dataSchemaProps(fnSchema)`/`dataParamNames(fnSchema)`, both of which read `fnSchema.input.properties` directly and iterate that flat map to emit one `--flag` per property. `schema-introspect.ts`'s existing `oneOf` handling (`FlagProp.oneOf`, per `BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001`) is narrowly scoped to detecting a NESTED optional field's nullable-union shape (`T | undefined` → `oneOf: [{type:'null'},{type:X}]` as `ts-json-schema-generator` renders it) - it is not, and was never meant to be, a mechanism for a top-level discriminated union covering the WHOLE operation input.

**Impact:** if any operation's top-level `input` schema is `{oneOf: [...], discriminator: {...}}` (apigen's own canonical shape for a tagged/variant value, already used elsewhere in the system for field-level unions) rather than a flat `{type:'object', properties:{...}}`, `dataSchemaProps`/`dataParamNames` find no top-level `properties` to iterate at all. The generated CLI command for that operation would have ZERO flags - not degraded, genuinely unusable via CLI. This affects ANY future operation whose input is inherently a top-level union, not just batch (batch is simply the first concrete case that surfaced it).

**Fix direction:** teach `apigen-plugin-cli-output`'s codegen to recognize a root-level `oneOf`+`discriminator` operation input and render it as N Commander subcommands, one per discriminator branch (e.g. a hypothetical `batch` operation would render as `<cli> batch create-item --items ...` / `<cli> batch task --items ...`), with each branch's own flat `properties` rendered via the EXISTING flag-generation logic unchanged (once inside one branch, it's a flat object again - no new logic needed there). MCP (`apigen-plugin-mcp`) and HTTP/runtime validation are unaffected by this gap - MCP passes the raw JSON schema through to the client/LLM as `inputSchema` with no per-property decomposition, and the existing validate-layer already evaluates `oneOf` correctly at dispatch time.

**Explicitly non-blocking:** this does NOT gate or need to be resolved as a prerequisite for any consumer of the `oneOf`+`discriminator` convention (e.g. FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001's batch operation) to ship for MCP/HTTP first - CLI catches up independently on its own timeline, the same pattern this repo already uses for `apigen-plugin-cli-output`'s existing streaming-rejection gap (`FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-008`/`DEBT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-002`'s cli half) not blocking HTTP/MCP streaming support.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, apigen-batch-design-2026-07-25, 1: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts:110-155 (dataSchemaProps/dataParamNames property-iteration, no oneOf-root handling); 2: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/schema-introspect.ts:29-54 (FlagProp.oneOf scoped to nested nullable-field detection only, BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001); 3: packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts (apigen's own canonical oneOf+discriminator convention for tagged unions); 4: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-mcp/src/lib/generate.ts (contrast - no per-property decomposition, unaffected)]

meta_parsed.title: apigen-plugin-cli-output cannot render an operation whose top-level input schema is a discriminated union (oneOf at the schema root) - generates zero flags
meta_parsed.body:
**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, while designing generic bulk/batch operation support for apigen (FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001) and checking whether apigen's own established discriminated-union convention (`oneOf` + `discriminator`, per `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts`, DESIGN §4.1 `docs/plan/apigen-logical-types`) can be used as an OPERATION's top-level input shape.

**Root cause (traced to real code, not guessed):** `apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts`'s per-operation flag emission (lines ~110-155) calls `dataSchemaProps(fnSchema)`/`dataParamNames(fnSchema)`, both of which read `fnSchema.input.properties` directly and iterate that flat map to emit one `--flag` per property. `schema-introspect.ts`'s existing `oneOf` handling (`FlagProp.oneOf`, per `BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001`) is narrowly scoped to detecting a NESTED optional field's nullable-union shape (`T | undefined` → `oneOf: [{type:'null'},{type:X}]` as `ts-json-schema-generator` renders it) - it is not, and was never meant to be, a mechanism for a top-level discriminated union covering the WHOLE operation input.

**Impact:** if any operation's top-level `input` schema is `{oneOf: [...], discriminator: {...}}` (apigen's own canonical shape for a tagged/variant value, already used elsewhere in the system for field-level unions) rather than a flat `{type:'object', properties:{...}}`, `dataSchemaProps`/`dataParamNames` find no top-level `properties` to iterate at all. The generated CLI command for that operation would have ZERO flags - not degraded, genuinely unusable via CLI. This affects ANY future operation whose input is inherently a top-level union, not just batch (batch is simply the first concrete case that surfaced it).

**Fix direction:** teach `apigen-plugin-cli-output`'s codegen to recognize a root-level `oneOf`+`discriminator` operation input and render it as N Commander subcommands, one per discriminator branch (e.g. a hypothetical `batch` operation would render as `<cli> batch create-item --items ...` / `<cli> batch task --items ...`), with each branch's own flat `properties` rendered via the EXISTING flag-generation logic unchanged (once inside one branch, it's a flat object again - no new logic needed there). MCP (`apigen-plugin-mcp`) and HTTP/runtime validation are unaffected by this gap - MCP passes the raw JSON schema through to the client/LLM as `inputSchema` with no per-property decomposition, and the existing validate-layer already evaluates `oneOf` correctly at dispatch time.

**Explicitly non-blocking:** this does NOT gate or need to be resolved as a prerequisite for any consumer of the `oneOf`+`discriminator` convention (e.g. FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001's batch operation) to ship for MCP/HTTP first - CLI catches up independently on its own timeline, the same pattern this repo already uses for `apigen-plugin-cli-output`'s existing streaming-rejection gap (`FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-008`/`DEBT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-002`'s cli half) not blocking HTTP/MCP streaming support.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, apigen-batch-design-2026-07-25, 1: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts:110-155 (dataSchemaProps/dataParamNames property-iteration, no oneOf-root handling); 2: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/schema-introspect.ts:29-54 (FlagProp.oneOf scoped to nested nullable-field detection only, BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001); 3: packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts (apigen's own canonical oneOf+discriminator convention for tagged unions); 4: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-mcp/src/lib/generate.ts (contrast - no per-property decomposition, unaffected)]

notes.text: CORRECTION (2026-07-27): this item's own body claims "MCP ... unaffected by this gap - MCP passes the raw JSON schema through to the client/LLM as inputSchema with no per-property decomposition." That claim is WRONG, disproven by direct testing against a real external MCP consumer (agent-browser's search-mcp-source.ts, via opencode's actual production config) after FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001's batch plugin shipped: apigen-plugin-mcp/src/lib/run.ts:471-481 has its own pre-existing fallback that substitutes an EMPTY {type:'object',properties:{}} schema whenever a mount op's input isn't already top-level {type:'object'} - it does NOT pass oneOf schemas through raw. Filed the MCP-specific analog as BUG-APIGEN-MCP-ROOT-ONEOF-001 (cross-linked) rather than editing this item's scope, since the fix lives in a different package with a different mechanism.

FIXED. apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/schema-introspect.ts: added resolveRootUnion() (new export, ~lines 138-232) which detects a root-level oneOf+discriminator domain schema (schema.input.properties.data.{oneOf,discriminator}) and decomposes it into per-branch {value, commandName, props, required} data — deliberately separate from the existing FlagProp.oneOf (BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001, nested nullable-field detection only, left untouched).

apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts: refactored the per-operation flag/action emission into shared helpers (emitEnvelopeFlags, emitParamFlags, emitDispatchAction) reused by both the existing flat path (byte-for-byte unchanged output — regression-tested) and a new emitDiscriminatedCommand() that renders one parent Command + N Commander subcommands (one per discriminator branch, e.g. `<cli> batchAction create-item --items ...` / `<cli> batchAction send-task --items ...`), reusing the exact same flag-typing logic per branch. The discriminator's own literal field (e.g. "operation") is bound automatically per branch (not exposed as a flag). Each branch also gets its own synthesized flat per-branch dispatch schema (registered under a codegen-internal `pkgId:fnName::branchCommandName` key in the emitted `schemas` const) so the existing, unmodified dispatch()/dataParamNames() (@adhd/apigen-engine-runtime, not touched) resolve domainArgs correctly for a branch without dispatch() itself needing any oneOf-awareness.

Real tests added: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/test/root-oneof-branch.spec.ts (12 tests) — unit coverage for resolveRootUnion + generate()'s subcommand codegen using the REAL buildBatchMountedOperations/buildBatchKindSchema output from @adhd/apigen-core-client (not an invented oneOf shape) as the fixture, a regression guard proving the flat non-union path is unaffected, plus 2 real end-to-end tests that write the generated cli.ts + a real target module to disk and drive them as REAL spawned `node -r @swc-node/register` child processes — proving both discriminator branches ("create-item", "send-task") are genuinely invokable and dispatch real args to a real function. A negative-control test reproduces the exact pre-fix symptom (dataSchemaProps finds zero properties) against the same real schema.

Verified: npx nx test apigen-plugin-cli-output — 6 files, 82 tests passed (was 70 pre-fix, +12 new). npx nx lint apigen-plugin-cli-output — clean. npx nx test apigen-cli (real dependent, per AGENTS.md affected-test guidance) — 21 files, 163 tests passed, unaffected.

Scope note (transparency, not a new backlog item): apigen-plugin-cli-output's generate() (the static codegen path this bug is scoped to) has NO mount-capability collection at all today — --use batch's real _batch/<kind> mounted operations never reach generate()'s PluginInput.packages (only run.ts's live dispatch path collects MountedOperations, via buildOpPlan in apigen-engine-runtime). This fix makes generate() correctly render ANY ComposedSchemas entry shaped with a root-level oneOf+discriminator domain schema (proven against the real batch schema shape) — but wiring batch's mount ops INTO generate()'s package set is a separate, pre-existing architectural gap, out of this bug's scope (and out of apigen-plugin-cli-output's file boundary in the constraints I was given this session). Did not file a new backlog item per instruction to report rather than expand scope; flagging here for whoever owns that follow-up.

apigen has no JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration codegen path for any operation - a real gap in the core value proposition, not just a batch-spec detail

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, during an architect revision pass on `docs/spec/apigen/BATCH_0.0.1.md` (FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001), while resolving whether `oneOf`+`discriminator` schemas degrade to a looser type when consumed by this repo's JSON-Schema→TS codegen.

**Finding:** the premise didn't hold - **there is no JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration codegen path anywhere in this repo**, for `_batch` or any other operation (verified via `grep -rn "json-schema-to-typescript|jsonSchemaToTs|generateTypes" packages/apigen`, zero hits outside node_modules/dist). `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/ts-json-schema.ts` runs the OPPOSITE direction (TS source → JSON Schema, via `ts-json-schema-generator`+`ts-morph`) and has zero references to `oneOf`/`discriminator`/`union`.

What DOES exist, all real and already correctly handling `oneOf`+`discriminator`: the JSON-Schema wire shape itself (`union.ts` nominal/$ref, `morph-walk.ts` inline/advisory), OpenAPI emission (`packages/apigen/codegen/openapi`, which just passes oneOf/discriminator through since OpenAPI 3.1 natively supports it), runtime encode/decode transcoding (`apigen-base-logical/src/lib/emit.ts`'s `emitOneOf`), runtime validation (`apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/validate-layer.ts`, which deliberately does NOT use Ajv's built-in `discriminator:true` for compatibility reasons), and runtime dispatch (`union-codec.ts` routing by `discriminator.propertyName`/`.mapping`).

**Why this matters beyond batch:** apigen's stated purpose (per `docs/apigen/SPEC.md` Tenet 0) is code-first extraction that projects to every transport/target including "clients." Today, a consumer gets typed access only by being in the SAME monorepo and importing the hand-authored source functions directly (or via `codegen/openapi`'s output being fed to an EXTERNAL, non-apigen-built codegen tool). There is no first-party "generate a typed TS client SDK from the descriptor" output - a real, load-bearing gap for any cross-service or cross-language consumer that isn't just importing the same TS source file.

**Not urgent/blocking for FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001** - the architect's finding was specifically that this absence introduces NO additional risk to the batch design (nothing about `_batch`'s `oneOf`+`discriminator` shape would behave differently here than any other operation with a union-shaped field already does). But the gap itself is real and worth its own tracked item, independent of batch.

**Fix direction:** scope a JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration generator (or adopt/wrap an existing one, e.g. `json-schema-to-typescript`) as a new apigen codegen target (`--type ts-client` or similar), with `_batch`'s discriminated-union branches used as one of its first fixtures once it exists (so this exact case is proven, not assumed).

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, architect-reviewer, apigen-batch-spec-revision, docs/spec/apigen/BATCH_0.0.1.md §7 (open question 1, resolved); packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/ts-json-schema.ts (TS→JSON-Schema direction only); packages/apigen/codegen/openapi (OpenAPI emission, passes oneOf/discriminator through natively); packages/apigen/apigen-base-logical/src/lib/emit.ts:171,201-205,326+ (emitOneOf, runtime transcode); packages/apigen/apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/validate-layer.ts:60-68 (runtime validation, custom discriminator handling); packages/apigen/apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/logical/union-codec.ts:178-220 (runtime dispatch)]

**Finding:** the premise didn't hold - **there is no JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration codegen path anywhere in this repo**, for `_batch` or any other operation (verified via `grep -rn "json-schema-to-typescript|jsonSchemaToTs|generateTypes" packages/apigen`, zero hits outside node_modules/dist). `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/ts-json-schema.ts` runs the OPPOSITE direction (TS source → JSON Schema, via `ts-json-schema-generator`+`ts-morph`) and has zero references to `oneOf`/`discriminator`/`union`.

What DOES exist, all real and already correctly handling `oneOf`+`discriminator`: the JSON-Schema wire shape itself (`union.ts` nominal/$ref, `morph-walk.ts` inline/advisory), OpenAPI emission (`packages/apigen/codegen/openapi`, which just passes oneOf/discriminator through since OpenAPI 3.1 natively supports it), runtime encode/decode transcoding (`apigen-base-logical/src/lib/emit.ts`'s `emitOneOf`), runtime validation (`apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/validate-layer.ts`, which deliberately does NOT use Ajv's built-in `discriminator:true` for compatibility reasons), and runtime dispatch (`union-codec.ts` routing by `discriminator.propertyName`/`.mapping`).

**Why this matters beyond batch:** apigen's stated purpose (per `docs/apigen/SPEC.md` Tenet 0) is code-first extraction that projects to every transport/target including "clients." Today, a consumer gets typed access only by being in the SAME monorepo and importing the hand-authored source functions directly (or via `codegen/openapi`'s output being fed to an EXTERNAL, non-apigen-built codegen tool). There is no first-party "generate a typed TS client SDK from the descriptor" output - a real, load-bearing gap for any cross-service or cross-language consumer that isn't just importing the same TS source file.

**Not urgent/blocking for FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001** - the architect's finding was specifically that this absence introduces NO additional risk to the batch design (nothing about `_batch`'s `oneOf`+`discriminator` shape would behave differently here than any other operation with a union-shaped field already does). But the gap itself is real and worth its own tracked item, independent of batch.

**Fix direction:** scope a JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration generator (or adopt/wrap an existing one, e.g. `json-schema-to-typescript`) as a new apigen codegen target (`--type ts-client` or similar), with `_batch`'s discriminated-union branches used as one of its first fixtures once it exists (so this exact case is proven, not assumed).

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, architect-reviewer, apigen-batch-spec-revision, docs/spec/apigen/BATCH_0.0.1.md §7 (open question 1, resolved); packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/ts-json-schema.ts (TS→JSON-Schema direction only); packages/apigen/codegen/openapi (OpenAPI emission, passes oneOf/discriminator through natively); packages/apigen/apigen-base-logical/src/lib/emit.ts:171,201-205,326+ (emitOneOf, runtime transcode); packages/apigen/apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/validate-layer.ts:60-68 (runtime validation, custom discriminator handling); packages/apigen/apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/logical/union-codec.ts:178-220 (runtime dispatch)]

content:
union.ts (nominal/$ref) vs morph-walk.ts (inline/advisory) are two distinct discriminated-union mechanisms with no doc distinguishing them - easy to pick the wrong one, and both share an undocumented ≥2-variant constraint

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, during design work on `FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001` (generic batch operations) - the design's own author (a Claude session) initially cited `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts` as the mechanism for `_batch`'s discriminated-union input schema. An architect revision pass caught that this was the WRONG one: `union.ts`'s `buildUnionSchema` (verified `union.ts:111-139`) only emits `$ref`-based branches into `#/$defs/<ClassName>`, requires each variant to be a *nominal* type already registered by `nominal.ts`, and throws (`union.ts:114-118`) below 2 variants. The actual fit for synthetically-constructed, non-nominal inline branches is `morph-walk.ts`'s `InlineDiscriminator`/`detectDiscriminator` (`morph-walk.ts:276-287,298-309`), whose own doc comment explicitly contrasts itself with `union.ts` ("unlike `union.ts`'s `$ref`-based `buildUnionSchema`, the mapping target is a same-document pointer") - meaning the codebase already documents the distinction, just not anywhere a plugin author would find it before picking one.

**Compounding issue:** BOTH builders independently enforce the same undocumented invariant - a discriminated union needs ≥2 variants (`union.ts:114-118` throws; `morph-walk.ts`'s `detectDiscriminator` returns `undefined` below 2, `morph-walk.ts:301`). Any future `MountCapability`/plugin author building a schema whose variant count is descriptor-dependent (unknown until runtime, as with batch's "one branch per batchable operation") needs to know this and explicitly handle the 0-or-1-variant case (e.g. don't mount at all) - today this is discoverable only by reading both files' internals or by hitting the thrown error/silent `undefined` in practice.

**Fix direction:** add a short comparison note (a doc comment on `MountCapability` in `plugin.ts`, and/or a README section in `schema-builders/`) stating: (1) `union.ts` is for nominal, already-extracted TS classes needing `$ref`+`$defs` identity; `morph-walk.ts`'s inline discriminator is for synthetically-constructed, non-nominal branches (e.g. a dynamically-sized mount-contributed union); (2) both require ≥2 variants - a caller constructing a union whose size depends on runtime/descriptor state MUST handle the <2-variant case explicitly (e.g. contribute zero synthetic operations) rather than assume a union is always constructible.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, architect-reviewer, apigen-batch-spec-revision, docs/spec/apigen/BATCH_0.0.1.md §1.1 (round-2 correction); packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts:111-139; packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/morph-walk.ts:276-287,283-284,298-309]

backlog_append_note/backlog_get_item fail with an unhelpful "item not found" when humanId is correct but repo string doesn't exactly match how the item was filed - no hint that the item exists under a different repo value

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, writing 25 real triage-verdict notes back onto agent-mcp-related backlog items after a triage sweep. 5 of 25 `backlog_append_note` calls failed with `MCP error -32603: backlog item not found: PseudoSky/adhd::agent-mcp-00X` even though every other sibling item in the same batch (same apparent project, same naming convention) succeeded under `repo:"PseudoSky/adhd"`.

**Root cause:** those 5 items (`agent-mcp-001`, `agent-mcp-002`, `agent-mcp-004`, `agent-mcp-005`, `agent-mcp-006`) were filed at some earlier point with `repo:"adhd"` (bare, no `PseudoSky/` prefix) instead of the `"PseudoSky/adhd"` convention every other item in the same logical project uses. Confirmed via `backlog_list_items` grep: `humanId:"agent-mcp-002"` exists exactly once, with `repo:"adhd"` on file - `backlog_get_item({repo:"PseudoSky/adhd", humanId:"agent-mcp-002"})` doesn't error, it silently returns a null result (itself a separate, likely-related bug - see `BUG-APIGEN-LOGICAL-NULL-OBJECT-RESULT-INT64-001`, the returned shape was literally `{"$apigen":"int64","v":"null"}`, that bug's own broken null-encoding leaking through here), while `backlog_append_note` with the same wrong repo throws the less-ambiguous but still unhelpful `-32603 item not found`.

**Impact (UX/DX):** the error message gives zero signal that the item exists under a different `repo` value - it reads identically to "this humanId was never filed at all." A caller (human or agent) has no way to distinguish "typo'd the humanId" from "right humanId, wrong repo key" without manually grep-searching the whole backlog for the humanId string and comparing repo fields by hand, which is what this session had to do. Compounded by the fact that `repo` inconsistency ('adhd' vs 'PseudoSky/adhd' vs presumably others) is apparently already possible to create in this backlog store today with no validation catching it at write time.

**Fix direction (two independent, complementary changes):**
1. **Better error, not a silent/ambiguous failure:** when a `(repo, humanId)` lookup misses but the `humanId` exists under a DIFFERENT `repo` value, the error/response should say so explicitly (e.g. `"item 'agent-mcp-002' not found for repo 'PseudoSky/adhd' - did you mean repo 'adhd'?"`), rather than a bare not-found. This alone would have saved several minutes of manual cross-referencing this session.
2. **Prevent the drift at write time:** `backlog_create_item` (and `importFromMarkdown`) should validate/normalize `repo` against a canonical known-repo list (or at minimum warn) rather than silently accepting an arbitrary string that happens to look plausible - this is presumably how the 5 items ended up on the wrong value in the first place.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: live repro this session - 5 of 25 backlog_append_note calls against humanIds agent-mcp-001/002/004/005/006 with repo:"PseudoSky/adhd" failed with "item not found", succeeded identically once repo:"adhd" was substituted; 2: backlog_get_item({repo:"PseudoSky/adhd", humanId:"agent-mcp-002"}) returned {"$apigen":"int64","v":"null"} rather than an error, cross-referencing BUG-APIGEN-LOGICAL-NULL-OBJECT-RESULT-INT64-001's known null-encoding defect]

content:
ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET not configured — all anthropic-provider agents fail at task time

ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-25 (debugger session). Original body incorrectly stated "the config file / .local.yaml layer is the intended mechanism" — this is FALSE, proven by code below. Filed BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 (cross-linked) for the code-level defect (misleading remediation message + missing secret-ref wiring); this DEBT item is retained for the missing-user-config aspect / doc fix.

Proven mechanism (not inference):
1. Provider secrets (ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET etc.) are declared in PROVIDER_DEFAULTS, entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/config.ts:210-213 — but deliberately NOT declared as FieldSpecs in agentMcpEnvironmentSpec.config (config.ts:63-189; module doc comment config.ts:11-19 explicitly notes this).
2. getProviderConfig() (config.ts:233-256) resolves the secret via env.resolveEnvName(defaults.secret) (config.ts:248); the startup check verifyAgentEnvRefs() (entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/index.ts:169-198) does the same at index.ts:188.
3. Environment.resolveEnvName() (packages/environment/environment-core-node/src/environment.ts:317-320): `if (!this.isEnvNameAllowed(name)) return undefined; return process.env[name];` — reads ONLY live process.env, zero file-layer fallback.
4. The file-layer cascade (system→global→project→local config.yaml/config.local.yaml) is resolveConfig() in packages/environment/environment-builder/src/config-resolver.ts:143-193, iterating Object.keys(configSpec) (line 154) — ONLY declared FieldSpec keys get file-layer treatment. resolveConfig runs exactly once, inside the Environment constructor (environment.ts:228); resolveEnvName never calls it and has no path to the layered config at all.
5. So a value placed in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml for ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET is silently inert — never read. Only a literal env var already present in process.env (shell export, or an MCP host's .mcp.json per-server env:{} block) works.
6. verifyAgentEnvRefs()'s own warning text (index.ts:194-196) says 'Set them in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml or the environment directly' — the config.local.yaml half is provably false per (3)-(5) and will never fix the warning.
7. content:
agent-mcp config references renamed plugin package — budget enforcement silently disabled

Root cause: .adhd/agent-mcp/config.json referenced @adhd/agent-mcp-budget (module field, line 4) which was renamed to @adhd/agent-plugin-budget when packages/ai/ directory was deleted. The plugin loader logged 'Plugin resolution failed — skipping' at startup and continued without loading budget caps.

Impact: All budget caps defined in config.json (token limits, tool call limits, filesystem__directory_tree block) were silently never enforced. Agents could run unbounded.

Fix (two parts):
1. Changed config module path from bare package name to relative path: ./packages/agent/agent-plugin-budget/dist/index.js (bare package name fails because createRequire searches from CWD/orchestrator dir, neither has the package in node_modules)
2. Added @adhd/agent-plugin-budget as a dependency of @adhd/agent-mcp

Files changed:
- .adhd/agent-mcp/config.json:4
- entrypoint/agent-mcp/package.json

Verified: Startup log now shows 'External plugin installed ./packages/agent/agent-plugin-budget/dist/index.js'. All 16 MCP tools advertise correctly.

Discovered & fixed: 2026-07-25

Root cause: .adhd/agent-mcp/config.json referenced @adhd/agent-mcp-budget (module field, line 4) which was renamed to @adhd/agent-plugin-budget when packages/ai/ directory was deleted. The plugin loader logged 'Plugin resolution failed — skipping' at startup and continued without loading budget caps.

Impact: All budget caps defined in config.json (token limits, tool call limits, filesystem__directory_tree block) were silently never enforced. Agents could run unbounded.

Fix (two parts):
1. Changed config module path from bare package name to relative path: ./packages/agent/agent-plugin-budget/dist/index.js (bare package name fails because createRequire searches from CWD/orchestrator dir, neither has the package in node_modules)
2. Added @adhd/agent-plugin-budget as a dependency of @adhd/agent-mcp

Files changed:
- .adhd/agent-mcp/config.json:4
- entrypoint/agent-mcp/package.json

Verified: Startup log now shows 'External plugin installed ./packages/agent/agent-plugin-budget/dist/index.js'. All 16 MCP tools advertise correctly.

Discovered & fixed: 2026-07-25

Priority rationale: Documentation-completeness item, correctly low urgency even if still real; strong on-disk evidence suggests it may already be substantially resolved for at least 2 of the packages it names, reinforcing that LOW (not higher) is appropriate pending verification.
CAVEAT: 82% of triage agents in this run had NO backlog tool access and reasoned from prompt-inlined data. Treat triage lines as unverified.

[debugger lane] verdict=DEAD
Evidence: All three packages matching agent-plugin-*/agent-generator-plugin already declare config docs+schema, checked against current source. agent-plugin-budget/README.md:5 '## Config' section with full JSON example + README.md:28 '## Caps' field table; src/index.ts:89 capSchema, src/index.ts:185 dimensionSchema, src/index.ts:231 pluginConfigSchema (exported zod schema), src/index.ts:262 'export type PluginConfig = z.input<typeof pluginConfigSchema>'. agent-plugin-sanitize/README.md:5 '## Installation' + README.md:21 '## Configuration' with a full option table; src/index.ts:12 'export const configSchema = z.object({...})', src/index.ts:127 '.parse(config)', src/index.ts:34 'export type SanitizeConfig = z.infer<typeof configSchema>'. agent-generator-plugin (the only other agent-*plugin* package, confirmed via `ls packages/agent | grep -i plugin/generator`) is an Nx codegen generator, not an agent-mcp runtime plugin, so it has no analogous 'config' concept; its generator CLI options are documented in its own README '### Options' table, and src/test/generator.spec.ts:90 explicitly asserts scaffolded packages must NOT depend on zod (proving the design intentionally excludes a runtime config schema for that package). Directory listing (`ls packages/agent`) shows no fourth candidate package. Both readings of the item -- human docs and machine-readable schema -- are satisfied for every real target; premise does not hold against current code.
Recommended action: Resolve as DEAD / not a bug. If desired, file a separate low-priority DOCS/DEBT item noting the two runtime plugins use inconsistent config-file-location conventions in their READMEs (budget says '.adhd/agent-mcp/config.json auto-discovered'; sanitize says 'agent-mcp.config.json (project root or ~/.agent-mcp/config.json) or ADHD_AGENT_PLUGINS env var') -- that inconsistency is real but is a distinct, much smaller issue than 'undocumented config', and was outside this item's scope to verify further (would need to trace the actual plugin-loader discovery code to confirm which claim is accurate).
(The debugger lane HAD shell access; its evidence is reproducible.)

@adhd/agent-mcp@2.1.4 (npm latest) is UNINSTALLABLE — ETARGET on dangling @adhd/agent-store-tools ^2.1.7 range (max published 2.1.6); same dangling-range pattern also live in the apigen family

**Repro (clean room, verified live):** `npm install @adhd/agent-mcp@2.1.4` in an empty dir fails:
```
npm error code ETARGET
npm error notarget No matching version found for @adhd/agent-store-tools@^2.1.7.
```
[1]

**Broken edge:** `agent-mcp@2.1.4` deps on `@adhd/agent-engine-compiler ^2.1.4` -> resolves to published `2.1.6` -> `agent-engine-compiler@2.1.6`'s own published `dependencies` declares `@adhd/agent-store-tools: "^2.1.7"` [2] — but `@adhd/agent-store-tools`'s max published version on the npm registry is `2.1.6` (`npm view @adhd/agent-store-tools versions --json` -> [2.1.0..2.1.6], no 2.1.7 exists) [3]. `agent-mcp@latest` currently resolves to 2.1.4 (stale — every direct/transitive agent-* sibling has moved past it: store-tools/store-runtime/engine-compiler at 2.1.6, core-provider/core-policy at 2.1.7).

**This is not an isolated incident — full sweep found the SAME dangling-range class already live in the apigen family** (npm `dependencies` vs max published `version`, all confirmed via `npm view <pkg> version dependencies --json` + `npm view <pkg> versions --json`):

| dependent (published) | declares | target max published | 
|---|---|---|
| agent-engine-compiler@2.1.6 | `@adhd/agent-store-tools ^2.1.7` | 2.1.6 |
| apigen-engine-gateway@0.1.6 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-api-express@0.1.5 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5`, `@adhd/apigen-engine-runtime ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4, 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-api-fastify@0.1.6 | same two ranges | 0.1.4, 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-cli-output@0.1.6 | same two ranges | 0.1.4, 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-health@0.1.7 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-jsonschema@0.1.6 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-logger@0.1.7 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-mcp@0.1.6 | same two ranges | 0.1.4, 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-openapi@0.1.7 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-py-flask@0.1.6 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |
| apigen-plugin-py-grpc@0.1.6 | `@adhd/apigen-core-client ^0.1.5` | 0.1.4 |

[4] Every one of these means `npm install` of the listed package (or any package that depends on it, incl. `@adhd/apigen-cli`, which transitively depends on nearly all of them) is or will imminently be ETARGET-broken the same way agent-mcp is right now, the moment npm re-resolves (some may currently resolve only because a consumer's own lockfile happens to pin an older transitive version — a fresh `npm install` with no lockfile is not so lucky, exactly like the agent-mcp repro).

**No other dangling ranges found** in the dispatch, data, or environment families (dispatch-*, data-query-engine, data-base-transforms, environment, environment-base-spec, environment-builder) — every internal `@adhd/*` range in those families currently resolves against the max published version of its target [5].

**Impact:** `@adhd/agent-mcp` — the flagship MCP server package — cannot be installed by ANY new consumer via `npm install @adhd/agent-mcp` or `npx @adhd/agent-mcp`. This is a full outage of the published package, not a degraded-mode issue.

**Minimal unbreak (exact versions):** (1) publish `@adhd/agent-store-tools@2.1.7` (source is already at 2.1.7 on disk, unpublished — see companion item BUG-RELEASE-ATOMICITY-DEP-RANGE-AHEAD-OF-TARGET-PUBLISH for why), which alone fixes the `agent-engine-compiler@2.1.6` resolution; (2) then run a normal `pnpm release` pass so `agent-mcp` picks up a new patch version whose own manifest re-resolves against now-consistent siblings, moving `latest` off the stale 2.1.4. Do NOT hand-publish; route through `pnpm release` / `nx run-many -t version,publish` per PUBLISHING.md — see companion DEBT item for why the underlying process gap must ALSO be closed or this recurs.

**Correct fix:** full coordinated republish of the agent + apigen families through the sanctioned `pnpm release` path (build -> `nx run-many -t version` -> `nx run-many -t publish`), which will: bump `agent-store-tools` (already-changed source, currently stuck below its own on-disk version), bump `apigen-core-client`/`apigen-engine-runtime` to real new versions >= 0.1.5 (their dependents already claim 0.1.5 in their published ranges but 0.1.5 was NEVER actually published for either — see companion item), then let every dependent's `sync-deps`/`dist-manifest` step re-resolve against the now-real published versions on the NEXT release pass, and publish everything not yet on the registry. Do not execute any publish without human sign-off (2FA/OTP) per PUBLISHING.md.

**Verification recipe (must pass post-fix):**
```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/agent-mcp-clean-room-verify && cd /tmp/agent-mcp-clean-room-verify
npm init -y
npm install @adhd/agent-mcp@latest   # must exit 0, no ETARGET
npx @adhd/agent-mcp@latest --help    # or the real bin smoke per entrypoint/agent-mcp/PUBLISHING.md
# repeat with: npm install @adhd/apigen-cli@latest ; npx @adhd/apigen-cli@latest --help
```

Citations: [PseudoSky/adhd, main, claude, release-triage, 1: clean-room `npm install @adhd/agent-mcp@2.1.4` in an empty temp dir (2026-07-25), exact ETARGET output reproduced verbatim above, 2: `npm view @adhd/agent-engine-compiler@2.1.6 dependencies --json` (2026-07-25) -> `{"@adhd/agent-store-tools":"^2.1.7", ...}`, 3: `npm view @adhd/agent-store-tools versions --json` (2026-07-25) -> ["2.1.0".."2.1.6"], 4: `npm view <pkg> version dependencies --json` for all 45 published @adhd/* packages cross-referenced against `npm view <target> versions --json` (2026-07-25), 5: same full sweep — dispatch-base-spec/dispatch-core-client/dispatch-core-optimizer/dispatch-orchestrator/dispatch-serializer-json/dispatch-cli, data-query-engine, data-base-transforms, environment/environment-base-spec/environment-builder all clean]

**Repro (clean room, verified live):** `npm install @adhd/agent-mcp@2.1.4` in an empty dir fails:
```
npm error code ETARGET
npm error notarget No matching version found for @adhd/agent-store-tools@^2.1.7.
```
[1]

**Broken edge:** `agent-mcp@2.1.4` deps on `@adhd/agent-engine-compiler ^2.1.4` -> resolves to published `2.1.6` -> `agent-engine-compiler@2.1.6`'s own published `dependencies` declares `@adhd/agent-store-tools: "^2.1.7"` [2] — but `@adhd/agent-store-tools`'s max published version on the npm registry is `2.1.6` (`npm view @adhd/agent-store-tools versions --json` -> [2.1.0..2.1.6], no 2.1.7 exists) [3]. `agent-mcp@latest` currently resolves to 2.1.4 (stale — every direct/transitive agent-* sibling has moved past it: store-tools/store-runtime/engine-compiler at 2.1.6, core-provider/core-policy at 2.1.7).

content:
Release pipeline is non-atomic: a dependent's @adhd/* range gets stamped from a dependency's on-disk (not-yet-published) version, and `publish` has no `^publish` graph edge to stop it shipping anyway

**PROVEN root cause (direct source + on-disk-state evidence, mechanism A — agent-store-tools):**

1. `@adhd/nx-build:version`'s topological ordering (`dependsOn:["build","assets","^version"]`, `tools/nx-plugins/build/plugin.js:67`) runs a dependency's `version` task before its dependents'. When `agent-store-tools`'s own `version` task decided a real bump was needed, it wrote its SOURCE `package.json`'s version field forward to `2.1.7` — confirmed still on disk today at `packages/agent/agent-store-tools/package.json` (`"version": "2.1.7"`) [1].
2. `agent-engine-compiler`'s own `version` task then ran `reconcileOwnInternalRanges` -> `reconcileInternalRangesFromDisk` (`tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.js:206-275`), which reads each declared internal `@adhd/*` dependency's version **directly from that dependency's on-disk source `package.json`** (impl.js:234-241: `depPkgPath = join(..., depProject.root, 'package.json'); depVersion = JSON.parse(readFileSync(depPkgPath)).version`) — i.e. `agent-store-tools`'s NEW on-disk `2.1.7`, with NO check of whether `2.1.7` was ever actually published. It rewrote `agent-engine-compiler`'s own range to `^2.1.7` (impl.js:242-243, 249-263).
3. `dist-manifest` (`@adhd/nx-build:manifest`, `tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/manifest/impl.js`) does the SAME thing at pack time: `buildVersionMap` (impl.js:27-45) builds `{ "@adhd/x": version, ... }` from EVERY sibling's SOURCE `package.json` on disk, then `generateDistManifest` stamps the dist manifest's internal ranges from that map — again with no registry check.
4. `agent-engine-compiler:publish` then ran and succeeded, shipping `@adhd/agent-store-tools: "^2.1.7"` in its published `dependencies` (confirmed: `npm view @adhd/agent-engine-compiler@2.1.6 dependencies --json`) [2] — **even though `agent-store-tools@2.1.7` was never published** (npm max is `2.1.6`; `published-state.json`'s own cached entry for `@adhd/agent-store-tools` is still `{version: "2.1.6", ...}` [3], meaning `agent-store-tools`'s own `publish` task never wrote through a successful 2.1.7 publish).
5. **The structural gap that allowed step 4 to succeed regardless of step 1-4's ordering:** `publish`'s `dependsOn` (`tools/nx-plugins/build/plugin.js:72`) is `["test", "^test", "version", "dist-manifest", "verify-dist-load", "publish-hygiene"]` — **there is no `^publish`**. Unlike `version`, which topologically forces a dependency's OWN version task to complete first (`^version`), `publish` has no graph edge requiring a dependency's OWN `publish` task to complete (or even run, or succeed) before a dependent's `publish` runs. `publish/impl.js` itself performs zero registry-resolution check of its own internal `@adhd/*` ranges before calling `npm publish` (`tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/publish/impl.js:93-149` — the only registry calls are the existence-check for ITS OWN name@version, never its dependencies' ranges). So nx's task graph and the publish executor both allow (and in this incident, produced) a dependent publishing successfully with a dependency-range pointing at a version that was never actually pushed.

**SAME failure class, second occurrence, independently confirmed (mechanism B — apigen-core-client / apigen-engine-runtime, INFERRED specific trigger, proven file evidence):**

`apigen-engine-gateway`, `apigen-plugin-api-express`, `apigen-plugin-api-fastify`, `apigen-plugin-cli-output`, `apigen-plugin-health`, `apigen-plugin-jsonschema`, `apigen-plugin-logger`, `apigen-plugin-mcp`, `apigen-plugin-openapi`, `apigen-plugin-py-flask`, `apigen-plugin-py-grpc` are all published declaring `@adhd/apigen-core-client: "^0.1.5"` (several also `@adhd/apigen-engine-runtime: "^0.1.5"`) [4], but **`apigen-core-client` and `apigen-engine-runtime` have NEVER had a `0.1.5` on the npm registry** (`npm view @adhd/apigen-core-client versions --json` -> `[0.1.0..0.1.4]` only) [5], AND **no commit in ANY local ref/branch ever recorded `0.1.5` in `apigen-core-client`'s source `package.json`** (`git log --all --oneline` + full diff scan of every commit touching that file: only 0.1.0->0.1.2->0.1.3->0.1.4 transitions exist) [6] — unlike mechanism A, this isn't explained by "disk is ahead of registry" alone, since disk was never at 0.1.5 either.

The one piece of direct evidence of a 0.1.5 ever existing anywhere: `packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/CHANGELOG.md`'s current top entry is `## 0.1.5 (2026-07-25)`, listing real fixes ("killable serve, configurable namespace, flaky test + log spam") [7] — committed in `6eaa57ab "chore(release): version bumps + published-state.json (45 packages)"`, THE SAME COMMIT whose diff on `apigen-core-client/package.json` only shows `"version": "0.1.3" -> "0.1.4"` [8], never touching 0.1.5. I.e. within one release-run commit, `writeChangelogEntry` (impl.js:146-175, called with `next` computed from `bumpVersion(version, level)`) and the package.json version-field write (impl.js:444-447, same run) disagree about what version was actually being released.

**INFERENCE (not fully proven from static files — no process/timing logs available):** the most consistent explanation is a **race between two concurrent invocations of the `version` task for the same package** — this repo runs many concurrent named agents against a SHARED working tree (per this session's own active-agent roster: multiple apigen-focused agents were running simultaneously the same day as this commit, 2026-07-25) [9], and `version`'s read-decide-write sequence (impl.js:380-447) is NOT file-locked/atomic across separate `nx` processes: one invocation's `bumpVersion` computation (from a `cached`/registry baseline of 0.1.4) can decide `next=0.1.5` and successfully generate/commit a changelog for 0.1.5, while a second, differently-timed invocation's own `raw`/`version` read (racing on the same `package.json`) ends up writing only `0.1.3->0.1.4` to the file — leaving the changelog and the source version permanently disagreeing, and (via mechanism-A's same on-disk-read path in dependents' `reconcileInternalRangesFromDisk`/`buildVersionMap`) letting AT LEAST ONE dependent's `dist-manifest` observe the transient `0.1.5` state and bake `^0.1.5` into its own published manifest before `apigen-core-client`'s own version settled back down to (or never left) `0.1.4`.

**Fix direction:**
1. Add `^publish` to `publish`'s `dependsOn` (`plugin.js:72`) so nx's task graph enforces that every internal `@adhd/*` dependency's OWN publish completes successfully before a dependent's publish can run — closes the structural gap that let mechanism A ship.
2. Before `npm publish`, have `publish/impl.js` (or a new pre-publish check) verify each internal `@adhd/*` range in the dist manifest actually resolves against a REAL registry version (`npm view <dep>@<range> version` or equivalent, allow-listing genuinely-not-yet-published siblings only if they're in the SAME release batch and about to publish first per the corrected `^publish` ordering) — turns a silent bad-range publish into a hard failure.
3. content:
No post-publish clean-room `npm install` smoke gate exists anywhere — every existing gate resolves @adhd/* deps via the local pnpm workspace, never the real npm registry, so a dangling published range (BUG-RELEASE-UNINSTALLABLE-AGENTMCP-001) ships undetected

**Gate blind-spot, confirmed file-by-file — none of these ever contact the real npm registry to validate an internal `@adhd/*` dependency RANGE:**

1. **`verify-dist-load`** (`@adhd/nx-build:verify`, `dependsOn:["build"]` only — `tools/nx-plugins/build/plugin.js:70`) `require()`/`import()`s the project's own built `dist/` entry in-process/subprocess to prove it loads. It resolves `@adhd/*` imports via the pnpm workspace's `node_modules` symlinks (created from source `package.json` `dependencies`, per PUBLISHING.md's in-source-dist layout), NOT via the published dist manifest's ranges against the registry. It cannot detect "this range doesn't resolve on npm" — the workspace symlink resolves regardless of what version is actually published.
2. **`@nx/dependency-checks`** (wired via `sync-deps`/`sync-deps-check`, `tools/nx-plugins/deps/executors/{sync,check}/impl.js`, invoked from `lint`'s `dependsOn:["sync-deps"]` per `PUBLISHING.md`'s "lint is self-healing" section) resolves each internal `@adhd/*` dependency's "correct" version through **Nx's own project graph** (every sibling's on-disk source `package.json`) — explicitly documented as such in `tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.js:177-200`'s own comment ("resolves each internal `@adhd/*` dependency's 'correct' version through NX'S OWN PROJECT GRAPH"). Zero network.
3. **`nx affected -t test`** and friends run against source/dist resolved via tsconfig path aliases + pnpm workspace links (this repo's own CLAUDE.md §5 confirms: "A green `nx test` resolves to source"). Never touches the registry.
4. **`publish`** (`tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/publish/impl.js:93-149`) only checks existence of ITS OWN `name@version` (via the `published-state.json` cache, or `isPublishedLive`'s `npm view <name>@<version>` fallback) — it never resolves its OWN internal `@adhd/*` dependency ranges against the registry before calling `npm publish` (see companion item BUG-RELEASE-ATOMICITY-DEP-RANGE-AHEAD-OF-TARGET-PUBLISH for the exact consequence).
5. **CI's `Publish` step is independently broken/disconnected** (already tracked: `BUG-CI-PUBLISH-STALE-TARGETS-001`, `PUBLISHING.md:283-301` — CI calls legacy `nx affected -t version/publish` targets hardcoding a nonexistent `dist/libs/core` path, never `release-publish.mjs`), so there isn't even a place where a CI-gated post-publish check COULD run today.
6. **`PUBLISHING.md`'s own "Post-publish checklist"** (`PUBLISHING.md:309-319`) is a **manual, human-run** checklist (`npm view @adhd/<name>` shows new version as latest; `npx @adhd/<name>@latest --version`) — it is not automated, not gated, and evidently was not actually followed for `agent-store-tools@2.1.7`/`apigen-core-client@0.1.5`/`agent-mcp@2.1.4`'s dependents, since all three shipped broken.

**Net effect:** nothing in this repo's toolchain has ever driven `npm install @adhd/<pkg>@latest` in a directory with NO pnpm workspace, NO tsconfig paths, and NO local `node_modules` symlinks — the exact scenario every real external consumer hits. `BUG-RELEASE-UNINSTALLABLE-AGENTMCP-001` (agent-mcp uninstallable) and its apigen-family siblings shipped through EVERY existing gate green because every gate is workspace-local by construction.

**Fix direction (per this repo's own Testing Protocol, CLAUDE.md §7 "Live testing is mandatory" — a clean-room `npm install` against the real registry is exactly the kind of default-running, unflagged, real-entrypoint test that section requires, not an env-gated exception):**
1. Add a new nx target, e.g. `@adhd/nx-build:smoke` or a plain `nx:run-commands` wrapping a script, that: (a) creates a scratch dir under `tmp/<project>/cleanroom-install/` (per CLAUDE.md §10's canonical ephemeral-artifact root), (b) runs `npm install <published-name>@<version-just-published>` there with `--no-workspaces`/outside the repo's pnpm context (or literally `cd` to a directory outside the repo tree — must NOT resolve via the pnpm workspace or tsconfig paths, or it reproduces this exact blind spot), (c) for bin-bearing packages, runs the real bin smoke (e.g. `npx @adhd/agent-mcp@latest --help` / the boot-and-exit-cleanly smoke already described in `entrypoint/agent-mcp/PUBLISHING.md`), (d) fails loudly (nonzero exit) on ETARGET/E404/any install or bin-smoke failure.
2. Wire it into `publish`'s `dependsOn` as a POST-step (or a separate `publish-verify` target that `pnpm release` runs immediately after `nx run-many -t publish`) so a broken publish is caught in the SAME release run that caused it, not discovered later by an external consumer's `npm install` failing (which is how BUG-RELEASE-UNINSTALLABLE-AGENTMCP-001 was actually discovered).
3. This is the automation of `PUBLISHING.md`'s existing manual "Post-publish checklist" (`PUBLISHING.md:309-319") — replace the checkbox list with an enforced gate, not a human-remembered step.
4. Once `^publish` ordering (companion BUG item) is fixed, this clean-room smoke becomes the FINAL proof that the whole coordinated release actually produced an installable artifact — it is the one check that would have caught both the agent-mcp and apigen-core-client incidents before either shipped.

**Cross-reference:** directly related to (but distinct from) `DEBT-BUILD-VERIFY-DIST-LOAD-NO-INPROCESS-001` (that item is about verify-dist-load's subprocess-vs-in-process execution model, not about registry-vs-workspace resolution) and `DEBT-BUILD-RELEASE-PUBLISH-NO-TEST-001` (that item is about the retired/dead `release-publish.mjs` script's own unit-test coverage gap, not about a missing consumer-facing smoke gate).

Citations: [PseudoSky/adhd, main, claude, release-triage, 1: tools/nx-plugins/build/plugin.js:67-72 (full target dependsOn wiring), 2: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/verify/impl.js (verify-dist-load body — dependsOn build only), 3: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.js:177-200 (comment proving @nx/dependency-checks resolves via Nx project graph, not registry), 4: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/publish/impl.js:93-149 (existence-check is self-only, no internal-range registry check), 5: PUBLISHING.md:283-301 (CI publish step broken/disconnected, BUG-CI-PUBLISH-STALE-TARGETS-001), 6: PUBLISHING.md:309-319 (manual, unautomated post-publish checklist), 7: CLAUDE.md "Proving features actually work" / "Live testing is mandatory" sections (this repo's own DoD standard for exactly this class of gate)]

REGRESSION from the @adhd/environment zero-config redesign, root-caused while investigating DEBT-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 (see that item for the full trace; cross-linked).

Proven root cause (code, not inference):
1. Provider-credential env-var names (ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET, _OPENAI_SECRET, _DEEPSEEK_SECRET — entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/config.ts:210-213 PROVIDER_DEFAULTS) are deliberately NOT declared as FieldSpecs in agentMcpEnvironmentSpec.config (config.ts:63-189; own doc comment at config.ts:11-19).
2. Both read paths — getProviderConfig() at config.ts:248 and the startup check verifyAgentEnvRefs() at entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/index.ts:188 — resolve these names via env.resolveEnvName(name).
3. Environment.resolveEnvName() (packages/environment/environment-core-node/src/environment.ts:317-320) is a direct process.env[name] read (gated only by the ADHD_AGENT_ prefix allowlist) — it has NO connection to the file-layer cascade.
4. The file-layer cascade (system→global→project→local config.yaml/config.local.yaml, per ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2) is implemented by resolveConfig() (packages/environment/environment-builder/src/config-resolver.ts:143-193), which only iterates Object.keys(configSpec) (line 154) — i.e. declared FieldSpec keys. It runs once inside the Environment constructor (environment.ts:228) and is never consulted by resolveEnvName.
5. Net effect: setting a provider secret in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml (or any config.yaml layer) does NOTHING — the value is silently never read. Only a literal env var already present in the process's process.env works (shell export, or an MCP host's .mcp.json per-server env:{} block).
6. The startup warning itself (index.ts:194-196) tells the user to fix this by setting the var 'in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml or the environment directly' — the config.local.yaml half of that instruction is false and will never resolve the warning, misleading anyone who follows it.
7. This is a genuine regression, not just missing user config: the pre-redesign agent-mcp (commit 9681e0c8, 2026-06-27) shipped packages/ai/agent-mcp/src/utils/load-env.ts, a loadEnvHierarchy() that loaded <cwd>/.env > <cwd>/.adhd/.env > ~/.adhd/.env into process.env via dotenv before any config/credential read — so a secret kept in ~/.adhd/.env (a documented, common location) worked. The @adhd/environment redesign removed this loader with no replacement for secret-shaped values (confirmed: zero dotenv references anywhere under entrypoint/agent-mcp/src; the shipped marketing copy at entrypoint/agent-mcp/docs/marketing/.catalog/capabilities.json:513 explicitly says 'No dotenv .env files ... the pre-redesign .adhd/.env / .env / load-env.js cascade was removed'). The redesign DID design a replacement mechanism for exactly this case — FieldSpec.secret:true, documented in packages/environment/ARCHITECTURE.md §3.1 line 85 ('never logged; stored as env-ref, resolved at runtime') and implemented in config-resolver.ts:157,184-188 (isLive branch, env-ref + file-layer + live env-var precedence) — but agent-mcp's own config.ts:386 comment concedes the spec 'declares none' of these. The mechanism exists in the package and was simply never wired up for agent-mcp's provider credentials.

Fix direction (pick one, both close the gap):
(a) Declare `providers.<name>.secret` as FieldSpecs with `secret: true` and an explicit `env:` name matching PROVIDER_DEFAULTS in agentMcpEnvironmentSpec.config, then read them via `env.config.providers.<name>.secret` (which resolves through resolveConfig's isLive/env-ref path, giving file-layer + live env-var precedence) instead of raw resolveEnvName() calls in getProviderConfig()/verifyAgentEnvRefs(). This is the architecturally-intended fix per ARCHITECTURE.md §3.1.
(b) At minimum, fix the false remediation text at index.ts:194-196 to stop recommending config.local.yaml for credentials until (a) ships.

Verification standard: a live test that sets ONLY a config.local.yaml value (no process env var) and asserts getProviderConfig()/verifyAgentEnvRefs() actually resolve it — this is exactly the negative control that would have caught this at introduction time, since resolveEnvName provably cannot see file layers.

Discovered: 2026-07-25, debugger session tracing DEBT-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001.

nx-release-publish's packageRoot:dist + stale source-relative "files" field ships near-empty tarballs — @adhd/agent-engine-orchestrator@2.1.6 published BROKEN, unpublish blocked

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, executing the human-approved Tier-2 agent-mcp release publish (orchestrator@2.1.6 + agent-mcp@2.1.5) handed off by team-lead. `npx nx release publish --projects=agent-engine-orchestrator` succeeded (exit 0) and published `@adhd/agent-engine-orchestrator@2.1.6` to the real npm registry — but the published tarball contains ONLY `package.json`, zero compiled code. Verified twice: (1) `npm pack --dry-run` against the exact publish root (`packages/agent/agent-engine-orchestrator/dist`) before publishing showed `entryCount: 1` (only `package.json`, same shasum as what actually got published); (2) fresh `npm pack @adhd/agent-engine-orchestrator@2.1.6` from a clean temp dir against the live registry confirms `total files: 1`, `package/package.json` only.

**Root cause:** `packages/agent/agent-engine-orchestrator/project.json`'s `nx-release-publish` target sets `options.packageRoot: "{projectRoot}/dist"` — npm publishes FROM the `dist/` directory as package root. But the `package.json` copied into `dist/` still carries the SOURCE-relative `"files": ["dist", "CHANGELOG.md"]` field, unrewritten for the new root. Relative to `dist/` itself, `"dist"` means a nonexistent nested `dist/dist`, and `CHANGELOG.md` isn't copied there either — so npm's `files` allowlist matches nothing. `main` (`./src/index.js`, correctly resolvable relative to that root — `dist/src/index.js` exists) was NOT force-included by npm despite being the documented always-included exemption, for reasons not yet root-caused (possibly `type:module` + `exports` field presence changing npm's inclusion behavior in the npm version in use — needs isolated repro).

**Same defect confirmed on `entrypoint/agent-mcp`** (identical `packageRoot: "{projectRoot}/dist"` config, identical unrewritten `"files"` field) via `npm pack --dry-run` against `entrypoint/agent-mcp/dist` — only 6 files (README/CHANGELOG/LICENSE/llms.txt/AGENTS.md/package.json; missing `dist/src/**` and `dist/drizzle/**`). **agent-mcp@2.1.5 was NOT published** — the executing agent stopped the moment this was discovered on orchestrator, before touching agent-mcp.

**Scope, not yet audited:** every `@adhd/*` package release-published through this `packageRoot: "{projectRoot}/dist"` pattern is a candidate for having shipped equally broken to npm at some prior version. dist-manifest rebase clobbered by a later build re-materialization → empty (1-file) tarballs

**Discovered & FIXED:** 2026-07-26, during the coordinated agent-family republish (deployment-engineer, commit ccada6fc).

**Root cause:** `dist-manifest` is a SIBLING of `build`/`test`/`version` in `publish`'s `dependsOn` (tools/nx-plugins/build/plugin.js). nx guarantees all siblings complete before `publish` runs, but NOT their relative order. `@nx/js:tsc`'s `build` (clean:true) can re-materialize its own un-rebased `dist/package.json` AFTER `dist-manifest` already rebased it, clobbering the rebase into a self-referential `"files":["dist",...]` allowlist that packs to nothing but package.json itself.

**Impact:** produced two empty (fileCount=1) published tarballs — agent-engine-compiler@2.1.7 and @2.1.8 (both burned, live on npm, need deprecation). An empty tarball on the `latest` tag makes every dependent uninstallable. Same class as the earlier empty-tarball incidents.

**Fix (shipped, commit ccada6fc):** single shared writeDistManifest() (tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/manifest/generate-manifest.js) that re-runs the REAL assets copy executor + regenerates the manifest as the truly-last write, called from dist-manifest, version (before hashing), and publish (before packing) — correctness no longer depends on nx's sibling-task scheduling order. Negative-control-verified teeth test in tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/publish/impl.spec.mjs (goes red when the fix is reverted, green when restored).

**Related:** DEBT-RELEASE-NO-CLEANROOM-INSTALL-SMOKE-001 (the gate that would catch a shipped empty tarball before consumers do), DEBT-BUILD-VERSION-CHANGELOG-BATCHING-001.

Citations: [PseudoSky/adhd@ccada6fc, deployment-engineer, claude, agent-mcp release, 1: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/manifest/generate-manifest.js, 2: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/manifest/impl.js, 3: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/publish/impl.js, 4: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/publish/impl.spec.mjs, 5: npm view @adhd/agent-engine-compiler@2.1.7 dist.fileCount => 1]

stale assets nx-cache hit after build's clean:true wipe leaves README.md missing → unbounded version-rebump loop

**Discovered & FIXED:** 2026-07-26, during the coordinated agent-family republish (deployment-engineer, commit ccada6fc).

**Root cause:** the `assets` target is nx-cached INDEPENDENTLY of `build`'s `clean:true` wipe of the SAME shared `dist/` directory. A stale `assets` cache-HIT after a fresh `build` leaves README.md permanently missing from `dist/`. Hashed for versioning, a dist that's permanently missing README.md differs from the last published tarball forever, so the version task re-bumps every single run with ZERO real code changes.

**Impact:** this is what made agent-store-tools / agent-core-env / etc. keep re-bumping on every release attempt — misdiagnosed earlier in the session as a concurrent version-bumping agent (it was not; single writer confirmed). Wasted a chain of version numbers and produced the leapfrog symptom.

**Fix (shipped, commit ccada6fc):** the same shared writeDistManifest() helper re-runs the REAL assets copy executor as the truly-last write before hashing/packing, so a stale assets cache-hit can no longer leave README.md missing at version/publish time. Negative-control-verified teeth test in tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.spec.mjs (goes red when reverted, green when restored).

**Related:** BUG-BUILD-PUBLISH-DISTMANIFEST-CLOBBERED-001 (same fix helper), DEBT-BUILD-VERSION-SYNCDEPS-REDUNDANT-001.

Citations: [PseudoSky/adhd@ccada6fc, deployment-engineer, claude, agent-mcp release, 1: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/manifest/generate-manifest.js, 2: tools/nx-plugins/assets/executors/copy/impl.js, 3: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.js, 4: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.spec.mjs]

yarn.lock is classic v1 format but package.json pins yarn@4.5.3 (Berry) — corepack yarn install rewrites it to Berry

**Discovered:** 2026-07-26 by the BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 fix agent, incidentally. Not fixed (out of scope for that bug; flagged per disclosure policy).

**Detail:** package.json's packageManager field pins yarn@4.5.3 (Berry), but the committed yarn.lock is in classic Yarn v1 format. Running `corepack yarn install` (which AGENTS.md §5 instructs agents to run in fresh worktrees to populate node_modules before dependency-checks) rewrites yarn.lock from v1 to Berry format as a side effect. The fix agent reverted that regeneration via `git restore -- yarn.lock` to keep it out of an unrelated bug commit.

**Note (this repo is pnpm-first now):** MEMORY + AGENTS.md indicate a yarn→pnpm migration (pnpm-lock.yaml is the active lockfile; `pnpm release` is the release path). The yarn.lock + packageManager:yarn@4.5.3 pins may be vestigial. Reconciliation options: (a) if pnpm is authoritative, remove yarn.lock + the yarn packageManager pin; (b) if yarn is still needed for some path, regenerate yarn.lock to Berry format deliberately and commit it once. Either way a human should decide — don't let it keep silently regenerating under agents.

Citations: [PseudoSky/adhd, debugger, claude, credential-fix side-effect, 1: package.json (packageManager field), 2: yarn.lock, 3: AGENTS.md §5 (corepack yarn install guidance)]

publish-hygiene intermittently sees an un-rebased dist/package.json (stale files field) under parallel release run-many — residual tail of the empty-tarball bug class

**Discovered:** 2026-07-26 during a real `pnpm run release:dry` for the minor-bump release. GATE 1 range-check passed; version dry-run correct; but `agent-engine-compiler:publish-hygiene` FAILED with the empty-tarball shape (npm pack --dry-run → 1 file), even though dist/src/*.js is fully present on disk.

**Mechanism:** the compiler's dist/package.json at hygiene time still had the un-rebased SOURCE `files:["dist","CHANGELOG.md"]` field. Since packageRoot IS dist/, that allowlist matches nothing (no dist/dist/), so npm packs only package.json. A sibling package (agent-store-tools, SAME source files field) had its dist files field correctly stripped (files:undefined → 60 files) and PASSED — so it is package-nondeterministic, i.e. a race, not a per-package config defect.

**Why the ccada6fc fix doesn't cover it:** dist-manifest is cache:false (always runs) and dependsOn build+assets; publish-hygiene dependsOn dist-manifest. In isolation `nx run agent-engine-compiler:dist-manifest` rebases correctly (files:undefined, 56 files) and a fresh manual run FIXED it. But inside the big `nx run-many -t publish --dryRun` (54 projects / 479 tasks), build's cached dist/** restore (which re-writes the clobbered dist/package.json from tsc generatePackageJson copying the source files field) intermittently interleaves so the rebase isn't the surviving last write before hygiene packs. This is the residual tail of BUG-BUILD-PUBLISH-DISTMANIFEST-CLOBBERED-001 / BUG-BUILD-ASSETS-CACHE-STALE-AFTER-CLEAN-001 — those made publish/version restamp at pack time (so the ACTUAL publish ships correctly), but publish-hygiene packs WITHOUT restamping and so false-fails on the transient state.

**Why hygiene must NOT just restamp (rejected fix):** hygiene/impl.spec.mjs line 133/162 deliberately assert a stale-files dist MUST fail (the empty-tarball guard). Restamping in hygiene would mask genuinely-broken dists. Verified: adding writeDistManifest to hygiene turned those teeth tests green-that-should-be-red. Reverted.

**Real fix directions (need root-cause + negative-control test):**
(a) Eliminate the clobber source: stop tsc generatePackageJson from copying the source `files` field into dist/package.json (or strip `files` from the ~40 source package.json since packageRoot=dist makes it wrong), so build never writes a bad dist manifest — nothing to race against. Verify extra-doc packages (llms.txt/AGENTS.md/docs/generators.json via files) still pack their docs from dist.
(b) Serialize dist-manifest strictly after ALL build cache-restores for a project within run-many, or make build's cached output not include the un-rebased package.json.
(c) Give publish-hygiene the correct input contract so it validates the post-restamp state WITHOUT masking (e.g. a shared assertion that the dist would pack non-empty AFTER the same rebase publish applies, while still failing when rebase itself yields empty).

**Impact:** blocks `pnpm release`/`release:dry` intermittently (a different package can fail each run). The gate is working (it correctly refuses to ship an empty tarball) — but it false-fails on a state the real publish would fix, so the release can't complete reliably until this is closed.

**Also observed same run (separate, likely load flakes, not this bug):** apigen-cli:test 3/157 failed (envelope-capability-use-plugin.spec.ts, waitForHttp never responded within 15000ms / fetch failed — serve/port contention under full-suite load); workspace-codegen-nx:test listed failed but 39/39 assertions passed (only a lint warning).

Citations: [PseudoSky/adhd, claude, minor-bump-release, 1: tools/nx-plugins/build/plugin.js:69-71 (dist-manifest cache:false, hygiene dependsOn dist-manifest), 2: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/hygiene/check-publish-hygiene.mjs (empty-tarball guard), 3: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/hygiene/impl.spec.mjs:133-182 (guard teeth tests), 4: tmp/release-dry.log, 5: npm pack --dry-run in packages/agent/agent-engine-compiler/dist → 1 file pre-rebase, 56 post-rebase]

A sibling package (agent-store-tools, SAME source files field) had its dist files field correctly stripped (files:undefined → 60 files) and PASSED — so it is package-nondeterministic, i.e. a race, not a per-package config defect.

**Why the ccada6fc fix doesn't cover it:** dist-manifest is cache:false (always runs) and dependsOn build+assets; publish-hygiene dependsOn dist-manifest. In isolation `nx run agent-engine-compiler:dist-manifest` rebases correctly (files:undefined, 56 files) and a fresh manual run FIXED it. But inside the big `nx run-many -t publish --dryRun` (54 projects / 479 tasks), build's cached dist/** restore (which re-writes the clobbered dist/package.json from tsc generatePackageJson copying the source files field) intermittently interleaves so the rebase isn't the surviving last write before hygiene packs. This is the residual tail of BUG-BUILD-PUBLISH-DISTMANIFEST-CLOBBERED-001 / BUG-BUILD-ASSETS-CACHE-STALE-AFTER-CLEAN-001 — those made publish/version restamp at pack time (so the ACTUAL publish ships correctly), but publish-hygiene packs WITHOUT restamping and so false-fails on the transient state.

**Why hygiene must NOT just restamp (rejected fix):** hygiene/impl.spec.mjs line 133/162 deliberately assert a stale-files dist MUST fail (the empty-tarball guard). Restamping in hygiene would mask genuinely-broken dists. Verified: adding writeDistManifest to hygiene turned those teeth tests green-that-should-be-red. Reverted.

**Real fix directions (need root-cause + negative-control test):**
(a) Eliminate the clobber source: stop tsc generatePackageJson from copying the source `files` field into dist/package.json (or strip `files` from the ~40 source package.json since packageRoot=dist makes it wrong), so build never writes a bad dist manifest — nothing to race against. Verify extra-doc packages (llms.txt/AGENTS.md/docs/generators.json via files) still pack their docs from dist.
(b) Serialize dist-manifest strictly after ALL build cache-restores for a project within run-many, or make build's cached output not include the un-rebased package.json.
(c) Give publish-hygiene the correct input contract so it validates the post-restamp state WITHOUT masking (e.g. a shared assertion that the dist would pack non-empty AFTER the same rebase publish applies, while still failing when rebase itself yields empty).

**Impact:** blocks `pnpm release`/`release:dry` intermittently (a different package can fail each run). The gate is working (it correctly refuses to ship an empty tarball) — but it false-fails on a state the real publish would fix, so the release can't complete reliably until this is closed.

**Also observed same run (separate, likely load flakes, not this bug):** apigen-cli:test 3/157 failed (envelope-capability-use-plugin.spec.ts, waitForHttp never responded within 15000ms / fetch failed — serve/port contention under full-suite load); workspace-codegen-nx:test listed failed but 39/39 assertions passed (only a lint warning).
