content:
publish-hygiene false-fails on transient un-rebased dist/package.json (build clobbers dist-manifest rebase)

## Symptom
`pnpm release:dry` intermittently fails at `<pkg>:publish-hygiene` with an empty (package.json-only) tarball error, even though the dist is genuinely fine. A different package can fail each run. A fresh `nx run <pkg>:dist-manifest` fixes the failing package (rebases files:undefined, full file count), proving the dist is fine and the gate false-fails on a transient state the real publish would restamp.

## Root cause
The build target (`@nx/js:tsc`, clean:true) emits its OWN un-rebased `dist/package.json` carrying the source `files:["dist",...]` allowlist (wrong once dist IS the package root — matches nothing → npm packs only package.json). `dist-manifest` rebases/strips it, but is a *sibling* of `build` in the `publish` task's dependsOn (nx guarantees completion, not relative order among siblings). A `build` cache-restore that materializes after `dist-manifest` re-clobbers the rebase. `publish` and `version` defend by re-stamping via writeDistManifest as their truly-last write (generate-manifest.js:200-235); `publish-hygiene` does NOT — it trusts whatever is in dist when it runs, so it sees the clobbered manifest.

## Evidence
- generate-manifest.js:200-235 documents the identical clobber for version/publish (BUG-BUILD-PUBLISH-DISTMANIFEST-CLOBBERED-001).
- plugin.js:71 publish-hygiene dependsOn:[dist-manifest] only, cache:true.
- 55 source package.json carry a `files` field.

## Fix directions
(a) eliminate build's competing dist/package.json (generatePackageJson:false / stop copying source manifest) so nothing clobbers the rebase; or
(b) have publish-hygiene re-stamp via writeDistManifest before checking (consistent with publish+version) — but keep a teeth test that a GENUINELY empty tarball (no shippable files even after restamp) still fails; or
(c) serialize dist-manifest strictly after build restore.

Real publish is already correct (publish restamps before packing) — this is a false-negative gate only. Must pass release:dry 3 consecutive times and keep hygiene able to catch a truly empty tarball.

content:
publish target lacks ^publish → non-topological publish order can leave a dependent transiently uninstallable (ETARGET)

## Finding (architecture audit)
plugin.js:72 publish dependsOn [test,^test,version,dist-manifest,verify-dist-load,publish-hygiene] but NOT `^publish`. nx parallelizes independent publish tasks, so a dependent B can `npm publish` before its dependency A lands. A consumer running `npm install B` in that window hits `A@^x` not-yet-on-registry → ETARGET (live variant of BUG-RELEASE-UNINSTALLABLE-AGENTMCP-001). GATE 1 (range-resolvability) only validates the eventual settled state, not in-flight order.
## Fix
Add `"^publish"` to publish dependsOn in plugin.js:72, mirroring the existing `^version` pattern (plugin.js:40-51, version/impl.js:31-37). Side benefit: a failed dependency publish auto-skips its dependents instead of racing ahead. Validate release wall-time with a dry-run timing compare.
CONFIRMED by code read; architect-reviewer audit.

content:
release script &&-chains clean-room-smoke (GATE 2) so it is skipped on partial publish failure

## Finding (architecture audit)
package.json `release`: `check-release-ranges && nx run-many -t publish && clean-room-smoke`. `nx run-many -t publish` exits non-zero if ANY task fails, so `&&` stops the chain and clean-room-smoke (GATE 2 — the only real npm-install verification) never runs in exactly the partial-publish scenario where it's most needed. Proven in tmp/release-dry-2.log: 53 published, apigen-cli:test failed, run exited 1.
## Fix
Decouple GATE 2 from publish's exit code: always run clean-room-smoke after publish (`;`/`|| true` + explicit compound exit aggregation), reporting three distinct outcomes: fully-released+verified / partially-released+smoke-caught / partially-released+smoke-incomplete. Never skip smoke on partial failure.
CONFIRMED; architect-reviewer audit.

content:
publish-hygiene cache:true replays stale verdict on cache hit → undermines BUG-001 re-stamp fix

## Finding (architecture audit) — directly weakens the BUG-001 fix
plugin.js:71 publish-hygiene is cache:true with nx default inputs that EXCLUDE dist/**. Its cache key is this project's source only, not the cross-project version-resolved dist manifest that dist-manifest (cache:false) writes. On a cache HIT, run() never executes, so the new BUG-001 re-stamp (hygiene/impl.js restampDistManifest) never runs and a stale PASS/FAIL verdict is replayed for content never re-checked. publish depends on publish-hygiene, so a stale PASS can gate a real publish.
## Fix
Set publish-hygiene `cache: false` in plugin.js:71 (it only shells `npm pack --dry-run`, cheap, read-only, no network) — same reasoning already applied to dist-manifest/version/publish. This is required for the BUG-001 re-stamp to actually take effect every run.
CONFIRMED; architect-reviewer audit.

Set publish-hygiene `cache: false` in plugin.js:71 (it only shells `npm pack --dry-run`, cheap, read-only, no network) — same reasoning already applied to dist-manifest/version/publish. This is required for the BUG-001 re-stamp to actually take effect every run.

content:
version executor uses strict != (no semver-direction) → a version regression permanently poisons published-state cache and silently stops publishing

## Finding (correctness audit)
version/impl.js:426 `if (cached.version !== version)` treats ANY inequality as 'source ahead, release pending, no bump' — no semver comparison anywhere (grep: zero semver imports). If source version is REVERTED below an already-published version, version never bumps; publish then hits npm 'cannot publish over previously published version', which isAlreadyPublishedError (publish/impl.js:67-69) treats as success and unconditionally writeThroughCache (publish/impl.js:146) with the CURRENT (newer) dist hash under the OLD version number. Cache now falsely asserts published content = local newer content; next run cache-hit skips publish forever. Silent permanent stall + cache inconsistent with registry.
## Fix
Use real semver: in version/impl.js treat `semver.lt(version, cached.version)` as a hard failure/loud warning, not the same as 'ahead'. In publish/impl.js already-published branch, verify via npm view that version is actually latest before write-through; never regress cached.version to a lower value.
Does NOT affect the current release (all versions fresh/ahead). PLAUSIBLE (full code trace, not live-repro'd); correctness audit.

content:
release-commit.mjs --untracked-files=no drops a package's first-ever CHANGELOG.md → compounding --first-release full-history dumps

## Finding (correctness audit) — CONFIRMED via live git repro
release-commit.mjs:66 `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=no` suppresses UNTRACKED files. A package's first-ever CHANGELOG.md (created by `nx release changelog --first-release` when version/impl.js:107-114 finds no prior changelog commit) is untracked, so collectReleasePaths stages only package.json and the new CHANGELOG.md is left permanently untracked. Next release again finds no changelog commit → --first-release again → dumps FULL history every release. Compounding functional regression.
## Fix
Drop --untracked-files=no (or use --untracked-files=all) and filter to isReleaseArtifact (already scopes to package.json/CHANGELOG.md under a project root — safe against sweeping unrelated untracked work). Will bite the current release (packages getting new CHANGELOGs) when release:commit runs.
CONFIRMED (shell repro); correctness audit.

content:
verify-dist-load audits the SOURCE package.json, not dist/package.json → blind to any generate-manifest rebase/exports/bin bug

## Finding (correctness audit) — CONFIRMED
verify-dist-load.mjs:117-123 reads pkgJsonPath = join(pkgRoot,'package.json') (SOURCE root), and collectEntries/verifyEntry resolve its unrebased main/module/exports/bin against the source root — landing on the same physical files but via a DIFFERENT manifest shape than what ships. The gate whose stated purpose is 'prove the real built artifact loads like a consumer' never reads the actual shipped dist/package.json. A wrong rebaseExports/rebaseBin/resolveInternalDeps in the published manifest would pass green.
## Fix
Read {projectRoot}/dist/package.json (already-rebased) and resolve entries relative to distDir, matching what a consumer's node_modules/<pkg>/package.json contains.
CONFIRMED; correctness audit.

content:
published-state.json durability tied to opt-in release:commit → successful publish can leave bookkeeping unpersisted on failure path

## Finding (architecture audit)
release-commit.mjs is DELIBERATELY opt-in and NOT invoked by `release`/`release:dry`. writeThroughCache (publish/impl.js:83-92) mutates published-state.json (a source-controlled snapshot) on disk only. On a partial-failure release (see BUG-003), 53 packages' cache entries + version bumps exist only as uncommitted local edits; if that tree is discarded before someone remembers `release:commit`, the npm-side publish is durable but local bookkeeping is lost (next run falls back to reconcile tarball-diff, or version behaves unexpectedly if the source bump was also discarded).
## Fix
Fold a published-state.json-only auto-commit into the write-through path (NOT the version bumps, which want human review), or make `release` failure/success output explicitly require/prompt release:commit before the cycle is considered closed. At minimum surface it in the release script's own output, not only a separate file header.
CONFIRMED; architect-reviewer audit.

Fold a published-state.json-only auto-commit into the write-through path (NOT the version bumps, which want human review), or make `release` failure/success output explicitly require/prompt release:commit before the cycle is considered closed. At minimum surface it in the release script's own output, not only a separate file header.
CONFIRMED; architect-reviewer audit.

apigen-cli startServe() readiness timeout hardcoded 15s with no override → serve LIVE tests flake under parallel release load

## Finding (surfaced fixing release-gate flakiness)
entrypoint/apigen-cli/src/lib/commands/serve.ts:367-434 waitForReady/waitForGrpcReady have a hardcoded default timeoutMs=15000 with no caller override; the internal call site (~1454 waitForReady(h)) always uses it. Under `nx run-many -t publish` (479 tasks) the two serve.spec.ts [serve.live] tests (proxies TS+Python; gRPC on shared front port) drive production startServe() and blow the 15s ceiling under CPU/port contention (serve.spec.ts takes ~18s even in isolation). apigen-cli:test passes 157/157 in isolation but failed these two under release load (release-dry-2/3). Test-side timeout bumps don't help — production gives up at 15s first.
## Fix (in progress)
Make the readiness timeout configurable: opts.readyTimeoutMs -> env APIGEN_SERVE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS -> 15000 default (prod unchanged when unset); tests set 60s. Fail-fast-on-!host.alive already present (serve.ts:377-381,420-424) — only the fixed ceiling needs to become overridable.
CONFIRMED root cause; discovered by test-automator during publish-hardening.

dispatch-orchestrator & dispatch-core-optimizer ship src/test helpers into published tarball (tsconfig.lib excludes only *.spec)

## Finding (surfaced by widened publish-hygiene test-dir pattern, DEBT-002 #3)
packages/dispatch/dispatch-orchestrator and packages/dispatch/dispatch-core-optimizer compile non-spec test HELPERS (src/test/helpers/fixtures.ts, fake-mcp-client.ts, mock-agent-runner.ts) into dist/test/*.d.ts+*.js and ship them in the npm tarball. Their tsconfig.lib.json include `src/**/*.ts` and exclude only `*.spec.ts`/`*.test.ts`/vite.config — so the src/test/ helper dir (non-.spec) is compiled and published. Harmless to consumers (typings/js of test helpers) but real cruft.
## Fix (in progress)
Add `src/test/**` + `src/**/test/**` to `exclude` in both tsconfig.lib.json so test dirs never compile into dist. vitest uses a separate config so tests unaffected. Verified caught by the new publish-hygiene test/ pattern.
CONFIRMED via release:dry-5 (dispatch-*:publish-hygiene FAIL: forbidden pattern test/ matched test/helpers/*.d.ts).

content:
verify-dist-load exposed to dist/package.json clobber race (build cache-restore leaves exports/bin un-rebased) — needs re-stamp like hygiene

## Finding (surfaced fixing BUG-007)
After BUG-007 made verify-dist-load read the rebased dist/package.json, it became exposed to the same clobber race as BUG-001/BUG-004: @nx/js:tsc build output rebases main/module/types but NOT exports/bin (leaves source ./dist/...); a build cache-restore leaves dist/package.json partially-rebased. verify-dist-load reads dist directly without re-stamping, so it nondeterministically sees un-rebased exports/bin. Observed: only agent-engine-compiler:verify-dist-load failed in release:dry-5 (exports['.'].default -> dist/dist/src/index.js) while its on-disk manifest was actually correct — a transient. Adding dist-manifest to verify's dependsOn (done) is necessary but not sufficient (build can re-materialize after dist-manifest).
## Fix (in progress)
verify/impl.js re-stamps via writeDistManifest before invoking verify-dist-load.mjs — mirroring hygiene/impl.js restampDistManifest + publish/version. Same established pattern for the clobber race.
CONFIRMED via release:dry-5; same class as BUG-001/BUG-004.

## Finding (surfaced fixing BUG-007)
After BUG-007 made verify-dist-load read the rebased dist/package.json, it became exposed to the same clobber race as BUG-001/BUG-004: @nx/js:tsc build output rebases main/module/types but NOT exports/bin (leaves source ./dist/...); a build cache-restore leaves dist/package.json partially-rebased. verify-dist-load reads dist directly without re-stamping, so it nondeterministically sees un-rebased exports/bin. Observed: only agent-engine-compiler:verify-dist-load failed in release:dry-5 (exports['.'].default -> dist/dist/src/index.js) while its on-disk manifest was actually correct — a transient. Adding dist-manifest to verify's dependsOn (done) is necessary but not sufficient (build can re-materialize after dist-manifest).
## Fix (in progress)
verify/impl.js re-stamps via writeDistManifest before invoking verify-dist-load.mjs — mirroring hygiene/impl.js restampDistManifest + publish/version. Same established pattern for the clobber race.
CONFIRMED via release:dry-5; same class as BUG-001/BUG-004.

agent-mcp isMainModule guard fails under symlinked invocation (npx/.bin/pnpm/tmp) → published server silently no-ops (exit 0, never starts)

## Symptom (why agent-mcp won't go live in opencode/npx)
The published @adhd/agent-mcp@2.2.0 server starts ONLY when invoked via its canonical realpath. When invoked via ANY symlink — `node_modules/.bin/agent-mcp` (npm/npx bin), pnpm's symlinked store, or `/tmp`->`/private/tmp` on macOS — main() never runs: the process loads env then exits 0 with no DB, no logs, no port bound. An MCP host (opencode `type:local command:[npx,-y,@adhd/agent-mcp]`) launches via the bin symlink → silent no-op.

## Root cause
entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/index.ts isMainModule:
`const isMainModule = process.argv[1] !== undefined && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`
`path.resolve(argv[1])` only normalizes — does NOT resolve symlinks. node sets import.meta.url to the REAL (realpath-resolved) module path. For a symlinked argv[1] the two differ → isMainModule=false → the `if(isMainModule) main()` block is skipped → clean exit 0.

## Evidence (clean-room, @2.2.0 from npm)
- node <canonical /private/tmp/.../src/index.js> ADHD_AGENT_TRANSPORT=http → binds port, real MCP client lists 16 tools. ✅
- node <node_modules/.bin/agent-mcp> (same env) → exits 0, never binds. ❌

## Fix
Resolve argv[1] through realpath before comparing (import.meta.url is already realpath-resolved):
`realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` (with a try/catch fallback to the old path.resolve compare). Add a teeth test that spawns the built bin THROUGH A SYMLINK and asserts the server actually starts (binds/handshakes) — must fail on the current code.

Requires a patch release (2.2.1). CONFIRMED via clean-room install + real MCP StreamableHTTP client.

content:
Batch item rejection's Error.message doesn't survive JSON.stringify over the wire

**Where:** `entrypoint/apigen-cli/src/test/integration/batch-plugin-e2e.spec.ts:183-191` (discovered and disclosed in a test comment during the FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001 rollout implementation, but never actually filed to the backlog since the implementing agent was stopped before its own backlog write-up step).

**Description:** When a batch item's target operation throws a plain `Error`, `invokeBatch`'s per-item `BatchItemResult` correctly surfaces it as `{index, status:'rejected', reason: <the error>}` (proven by the e2e test: item 1 in a 3-item batch throws on `getItem('missing')` and is correctly rejected without aborting the batch, per `onItemError:'continue'`). But over an HTTP/JSON transport, `reason` is serialized via `JSON.stringify`, and a bare thrown `Error` object has no own enumerable properties (`message`/`stack`/`name` are all non-enumerable on the prototype chain) — so the wire payload's `reason` field loses the actual error message entirely, surfacing as `{}` or similar to a real consumer trying to diagnose why an item failed.

The e2e test's own assertion only checks `reason` is `defined` (not what it contains) specifically because of this gap — disclosed in-line rather than papered over.

**Fix direction:** `invokeBatch` (or the batch mount's handler, wherever `BatchItemResult.reason` is constructed before serialization) should normalize a thrown `Error` into a JSON-serializable shape (e.g. `{name, message, ...(stack if configured)}`) before it's returned, so wire consumers get the real failure reason instead of an empty object. Verify against apigen's existing error-model conventions (`apigen-base-errors` / `ApiError`) for the correct normalized shape rather than inventing a new one.

**Status:** OPEN.

content:
apigen-plugin-mcp silently discards a mount operation's real input schema when it isn't already top-level {type:'object'} (e.g. batch's oneOf) - advertises an empty inputSchema instead

**Discovered:** 2026-07-27, while independently verifying FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001's shipped batch plugin against a REAL external consumer (not an internal fixture) - `~/dev/ai/scratch/agent-browser/search-mcp-source.ts`, mounted exactly as opencode's global MCP config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`'s `search` server entry) invokes it in production: `apigen-cli run --source <that file> --type mcp`. Adding `--use batch` and calling `tools/list` showed the real `batch_action` tool's advertised `inputSchema` as `{"type":"object","properties":{}}` - completely empty, even though the tool's real accepted shape is a discriminated union (`oneOf`) with required `operation`/`items` fields.

**Root cause (traced to real code):** `packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-mcp/src/lib/run.ts:471-481` (pre-existing code, NOT part of the batch diff - this logic predates batch and was written for health/openapi's zero-arg mounts) has an explicit fallback: if `mountedOp.input` isn't already a top-level `{type:'object', ...}` shape, it substitutes `{type:'object', properties:{}}` for the advertised `inputSchema`, per its own comment: "MCP's Tool.inputSchema is constrained to a top-level `{type:\"object\"}` shape by the SDK's own zod validation." This was harmless for health/openapi (their real input genuinely IS `{}` - zero-arg, so the fallback happens to be truthful), but batch's mount op has a real `oneOf`-rooted schema with real required properties, and the fallback silently discards it, advertising an empty schema to any MCP client that inspects `tools/list` before calling.

**Verified real end-to-end anyway:** the underlying dispatch/validation still works correctly when called with the correct (but now undocumented-to-the-client) shape - I confirmed this directly: `tools/call` with `arguments: {operation: 'agent-browser/search-mcp-source/list-providers', items: [{}, {}], concurrency: 2}` against the real running MCP server returned two real, correct `listProviders()` results. So this is a discoverability/introspection gap, not a functional break - but it means an LLM or MCP client relying on the advertised `inputSchema` to know how to call `batch_action` has zero information to go on.

**Relationship to BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ROOT-ONEOF-UNSUPPORTED-001:** that item's own body explicitly claims "MCP ... unaffected by this gap - MCP passes the raw JSON schema through to the client/LLM as inputSchema with no per-property decomposition" - this claim is WRONG, disproven by the direct testing above. That item is about CLI flag generation (a different file, different mechanism); this item is the MCP-specific analog, both stemming from the same root pattern (root-level oneOf schemas aren't handled by transport projections designed around flat object schemas). Filed separately since the fix lives in a different package with a different mechanism (MCP SDK's Tool.inputSchema constraint vs. CLI's per-property flag iteration) - cross-linked, not a duplicate. The old item's incorrect MCP claim should be corrected.

**Fix direction:** MCP's SDK constrains `Tool.inputSchema` to a top-level object shape, so the real oneOf schema can't be advertised verbatim - but silently substituting an EMPTY schema is worse than a partial/best-effort one. Consider wrapping the oneOf under a top-level object envelope MCP's zod validation accepts (e.g. `{type:'object', properties:{operation:{...}, items:{...}, ...}, description: '<oneOf/discriminator details in prose since MCP cannot render them structurally>'}`) so at minimum the field NAMES are visible, even if the full discriminated-union semantics can't be structurally expressed. Needs research into what MCP SDK's zod validation actually accepts before implementing - don't guess.

**Status:** OPEN.

Re-tested against the real running MCP server (same probe as before): tools/list now shows batch_action's full real 7-branch oneOf+discriminator (previously {}), and the same real batch calls (list-providers x2, tripwire-status x3) still succeed identically - schema-only change, zero execution regression. apigen-plugin-mcp: 85 tests pass unmodified, lint clean, build clean. One disclosed caveat, not a regression: the merged top-level `properties.items` reflects only the FIRST oneOf branch's item shape (since all branches share field names but items' element type differs per target operation) - a client using the discriminator+oneOf gets every operation's shape exactly right; a client that naively reads only the top-level `properties` without consulting `oneOf` could be misled about `items`' shape for non-first operations. This is a real, inherent limit of MCP's flat Tool.inputSchema contract, not something this fix could close further without MCP protocol support for oneOf-rooted tool schemas.

Added a real regression test suite (not just the manual probe scripts used to discover/verify this): packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-mcp/src/test/run.spec.ts, new describe block '[BUG-APIGEN-MCP-ROOT-ONEOF-001] deriveMcpMountInputSchema' (4 tests: already-valid passthrough, zero-arg fallback preserved, oneOf+discriminator preserved with merged properties, required-intersection across branches). Proved the tests have real teeth via a negative control: temporarily reverted deriveMcpMountInputSchema to the old always-empty behavior, confirmed exactly 3 of the 4 new tests correctly went red (the 4th - zero-arg fallback - correctly stayed green since that path is genuinely unchanged), then restored the real fix and confirmed all 89 tests green again. apigen-plugin-mcp: 89 tests pass (was 85 before this fix+tests), lint clean.

apigen-plugin-cli-output's static codegen path (generate.ts) never collects mount capabilities - batch/health/openapi never appear in a generated standalone CLI

**Discovered:** 2026-07-27, resolving BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ROOT-ONEOF-UNSUPPORTED-001 during the FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001 batch rollout, flagged in that item's own resolution note rather than silently left implicit.

**Root cause:** apigen-plugin-cli-output has two independent code paths: run.ts (live/interactive dispatch - this session's batch rollout gave it real hostBridge/mount-capability wiring, matching fastify/express/mcp) and generate.ts (the static codegen path that emits a standalone cli.ts artifact via `apigen generate`). generate.ts's PluginInput.packages iteration has no call to collectMountedOperations() (or any equivalent) anywhere - it only ever renders operations from the package's own composed schemas. This means --use batch (or --use health, --use openapi) mount ops are fully live and dispatchable via run.ts, but a generated standalone CLI produced by `apigen generate --use batch` would render ZERO batch/health/openapi commands - the mount ops never reach the codegen path's operation set.

**Scope note - not batch-specific:** this predates and is orthogonal to batch; it equally affects health and openapi, the two pre-existing mount capabilities. BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ROOT-ONEOF-UNSUPPORTED-001's fix (root-level oneOf+discriminator -> N Commander subcommands) makes generate() capable of correctly rendering such an operation once it's in the package set - but does not put mount ops into that set in the first place. Two independent gaps; only the first is fixed.

**Relation to FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-008:** that item already flags cli-output's run.ts as having 'NO --use layer/mount support at all' and asks the eventual TransportAdapter migration to decide whether to add it or file a follow-up. This item is the concrete follow-up for the codegen half specifically (generate.ts), distinct from run.ts (already fixed for run.ts by this session's batch rollout).

**Fix direction:** teach generate.ts's package-iteration loop to also call collectMountedOperations() (or the equivalent mount-collection helper already used by all 4 host run.ts files) for any --use plugins passed to `apigen generate`, folding mounted ops into the same operation set that emits Commander commands - reusing BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ROOT-ONEOF-UNSUPPORTED-001's new emitDiscriminatedCommand() for any mount op shaped as a root-level oneOf+discriminator (batch), and the existing flat-flag path for zero-arg mounts (health/openapi).

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, typescript-pro, claude, FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001, 1: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts (package-iteration loop, no collectMountedOperations call); 2: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/run.ts (contrast - now has hostBridge/mount wiring per this session's batch rollout); 3: FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-008 (adjacent, broader TransportAdapter migration item for cli-output's run.ts --use support)]

apigen-core-client's extracted CreateItemInput schema carries no top-level `required` array - missing required-in-TS fields silently pass AJV validation

**Discovered:** 2026-07-27, during the entrypoint/backlog batch-adoption proof-of-adoption work for FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001 / FEAT-BACKLOG-005 - while designing a real per-item validation-failure test case for a batch POST /_batch/action against backlog's real `createItem` operation.

**Description:** `entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts`'s `CreateItemInput` TypeScript type marks `family` as a required (non-optional) field. But the JSON Schema `apigen-core-client`'s `extract()` produces for it (dereferenced by `server.ts`'s own `dereferenceSchema`) carries no top-level `required` array for `CreateItemInput` - so a request that omits `family` entirely is NOT rejected by the real composed validate-Layer (the same AJV-backed layer every request, batch or single, goes through). The store silently persists `family: "undefined"` (the literal string) instead of rejecting the write. Confirmed empirically while building a negative-control test case: an enum violation (`priority: 'NOT_A_REAL_PRIORITY'`) correctly rejects with AJV's `enum` violation, but a missing-`family` payload does not reject at all.

**Impact:** any apigen-extracted operation whose TS input type has required (non-optional) fields is silently under-validated at the JSON-Schema layer if extraction fails to carry those fields into a `required` array - this is a correctness gap in the shared extraction pipeline (`apigen-core-client`), not specific to backlog. It means the wire-level validate-Layer's guarantee ("malformed input rejected before dispatch") does not actually hold for missing-required-field cases across ANY apigen-based consumer, not just backlog.

**Fix direction:** investigate `apigen-core-client`'s `extract()`/schema-generation path (ts-json-schema-generator config) to determine why required (non-optional, no `?`) TS properties are not being carried into the generated JSON Schema's top-level `required` array for at least `CreateItemInput`, and fix the extraction so required-in-TS fields are always required-in-schema. Verify against a minimal repro type before assuming the fix generalizes.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, typescript-pro, claude, FEAT-BACKLOG-005, 1: entrypoint/backlog/src/batch-adoption.spec.ts:102-108 (test comment documenting the empirical gap); 2: entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts (CreateItemInput.family - required, non-optional TS field); 3: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts (dereferenceSchema - the dereferenced schema consumed by the validate-Layer)]

**Discovered:** 2026-07-27, during the entrypoint/backlog batch-adoption proof-of-adoption work for FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001 / FEAT-BACKLOG-005 - while designing a real per-item validation-failure test case for a batch POST /_batch/action against backlog's real `createItem` operation.

**Description:** `entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts`'s `CreateItemInput` TypeScript type marks `family` as a required (non-optional) field. But the JSON Schema `apigen-core-client`'s `extract()` produces for it (dereferenced by `server.ts`'s own `dereferenceSchema`) carries no top-level `required` array for `CreateItemInput` - so a request that omits `family` entirely is NOT rejected by the real composed validate-Layer (the same AJV-backed layer every request, batch or single, goes through). The store silently persists `family: "undefined"` (the literal string) instead of rejecting the write. Confirmed empirically while building a negative-control test case: an enum violation (`priority: 'NOT_A_REAL_PRIORITY'`) correctly rejects with AJV's `enum` violation, but a missing-`family` payload does not reject at all.

**Impact:** any apigen-extracted operation whose TS input type has required (non-optional) fields is silently under-validated at the JSON-Schema layer if extraction fails to carry those fields into a `required` array - this is a correctness gap in the shared extraction pipeline (`apigen-core-client`), not specific to backlog. It means the wire-level validate-Layer's guarantee ("malformed input rejected before dispatch") does not actually hold for missing-required-field cases across ANY apigen-based consumer, not just backlog.

**Fix direction:** investigate `apigen-core-client`'s `extract()`/schema-generation path (ts-json-schema-generator config) to determine why required (non-optional, no `?`) TS properties are not being carried into the generated JSON Schema's top-level `required` array for at least `CreateItemInput`, and fix the extraction so required-in-TS fields are always required-in-schema. Verify against a minimal repro type before assuming the fix generalizes.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, typescript-pro, claude, FEAT-BACKLOG-005, 1: entrypoint/backlog/src/batch-adoption.spec.ts:102-108 (test comment documenting the empirical gap); 2: entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts (CreateItemInput.family - required, non-optional TS field); 3: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts (dereferenceSchema - the dereferenced schema consumed by the validate-Layer)]

citations.context: walkType object branch now computes required from !sym.isOptional()
new regression tests, including a CreateItemInput-shaped real-world case

notes.text: Independently re-verified: git diff confirms morph-walk.ts changed (+28/-1 lines) plus two new test files (fixtures/required-fields.ts, required-fields.spec.ts). Ran `npx nx test apigen-core-client` myself directly -- 13/13 test files, 300/300 tests, exit 0. Dispatch agent additionally confirmed a concrete before/after: extract() on the real entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts createItem operation now produces `properties.input.required: ["family","title","body","repo"]` matching model.ts's actual required fields exactly (was: no required key at all). Downstream affected-test sweep (20 projects/57 tasks) + backlog's own build+test all green. NOTE: the live backlog MCP server connection in this session is still running pre-fix code (no restart/reload happened), so its tool schema still shows no `required` array -- this is expected staleness, not a fix defect; a server restart/redeploy is needed before the live MCP surface reflects the fix. This bug is also the root cause of BUG-BACKLOG-HUMANID-COLLISION-001 (multiple items colliding on humanId 'undefined-001') -- that item remains open separately since it also needs backlog's own store-level defense-in-depth validation, not just this upstream fix.

[transition to RESOLVED] Root cause: apigen-core-client's schema-extraction 'Path 2' fallback (morph-walk.ts's walkType, object branch) never computed a `required` array at all -- it built `properties` for every named property but never inspected Symbol.isOptional(). Path 1 (ts-json-schema-generator direct) silently fails for locally-defined interface parameter types because ts-morph's getTypeAtLocation with no enclosing-node context emits a fully-qualified `import("/abs/path").TypeName` string that the generator can't resolve by name, so extraction always falls through to the broken Path 2 for these shapes -- generator-wide, not specific to CreateItemInput. Fixed by collecting `required` from `!sym.isOptional()` in walkType's object branch, omitted when empty to match ts-json-schema-generator's own convention.

[grooming wf_28c6a91a-4c9 — RECLAIMED] Analysis recovered from a run that was killed before its write phase.
Item status at analysis time: RESOLVED.

[triage] flag=debug-triage route=debugger
Route reason: Ticket premise ('needs verification of no regressions on nested properties') is uncertain against current code: I found a dedicated required-fields.spec.ts (packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/test/required-fields.spec.ts) that already exercises exactly this nested-property scenario with teeth (negative assertions on optional fields). It's plausible this ticket is already fully satisfied and just needs a real `npx nx test apigen-core-client` run to confirm green, which is debugger-lane verify-or-kill work, not a spec/architecture task.
Priority rationale: This is a verification/regression-check task on an already-fixed bug, not new user-facing breakage. LOW is appropriate; no evidence surfaced to escalate. Could not call backlog_set_priority (tool unavailable) so no write was made regardless.
CAVEAT: 82% of triage agents in this run had NO backlog tool access and reasoned from prompt-inlined data. Treat triage lines as unverified.

[debugger lane] verdict=DEAD
Evidence: Fix is present and proven by a real, teeth-bearing regression suite that is currently green. (1) Fix in source: packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/morph-walk.ts:274 `if (!sym.isOptional()) required.push(name);` and :283 `...(required.length > 0 ? { required } : {})` — exactly the fix the ticket describes (walkType's object branch now emits `required` from TS optionality, omitted when empty). (2) Dedicated regression test packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/test/required-fields.spec.ts (3 tests: required.minimal, required.all-optional, required.create-item-input-shaped) asserts nested-property `required` arrays with negative assertions (`.not.toContain('priority')`, `.not.toContain('tags')`) and an exact CreateItemInput-shaped real-world fixture mirroring the production bug (entrypoint/backlog's CreateItemInput.family). (3) Ran the real suite: `npx nx affected -t test --files=packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/test/required-fields.spec.ts` (exit 0) — apigen-core-client's full vitest run: 'Test Files 15 passed (15)', 'Tests 319 passed (319)', including `src/test/required-fields.spec.ts (3 tests)` at line 674 of captured log. (4) `git log --oneline -- .../morph-walk.ts .../required-fields.spec.ts` shows the fix landed in commit b2a5b50f 'fix(apigen): schema extraction required-array + CLI mount/discriminated-union gaps', which also added the test file in the same commit — this is not a partial/doc-only fix, source and test co-landed. Ticket's premise ('needs verification of no regressions on nested properties') is fully satisfied; there is nothing left to verify or spec — the verification IS the outcome and it's green. No PARTIALLY_LIVE gap found: nested-property, mixed-required/optional, all-optional, and real-world-shaped cases are all covered and passing.
Recommended action: Resolve the item as fixed/verified (route to whoever holds backlog write access for this run) citing commit b2a5b50f and the passing test run above. No further spec or dev work needed.
(The debugger lane HAD shell access; its evidence is reproducible.)

content:
@adhd/backlog published tarball crashes at mount — backlogDistDir() escapes to node_modules/@adhd/dist after dist-manifest rebase

@adhd/backlog@0.1.0 installed from the public npm registry crashes at load under both `npx @adhd/backlog` and `pnpm add -g`:

`Error: @adhd/backlog: cannot mount — <...>/node_modules/@adhd/dist/client.d.ts does not exist. Run "nx build backlog" first (extract() needs the built .d.ts for type information).`

Reproduced in an isolated clean room: `npm i @adhd/backlog@latest` then `npx backlog --help` → exit 1 with the above (index.js:190/191, from src/server.ts extractClientOperations→backlogDistDir).

ROOT CAUSE (verified): src/server.ts backlogDistDir() returns join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),'..','dist'). The @adhd/nx-build dist-manifest executor rebases the published package so index.js lives at the PACKAGE ROOT and client.d.ts ships as a SIBLING of index.js at the root. When published, dirname(import.meta.url) IS the package root, so '../dist' escapes to node_modules/@adhd/dist (nonexistent). The '../dist' form only satisfies the two in-repo layouts: vitest runs from src/ (../dist reaches <root>/dist) and dev-built runs from <root>/dist (../dist round-trips). It breaks ONLY for the published rebased-to-root layout. client.d.ts IS shipped (confirmed at published pkg root) — only the path computation is wrong.

FIX: layout-probing resolver — if client.d.ts exists as a sibling of dirname(import.meta.url) return that dir (published + dev-built), else fall back to join(here,'..','dist') (vitest from src/). Both call sites (extractClientOperations client.d.ts, buildBacklogApigenPackage importPath client.js) route through backlogDistDir().

SCOPE: the other 4 published entrypoints verified WORKING in the same clean-room sweep (apigen-cli 0.2.0 --help exit 0; decompile-cli 0.2.0 --help exit 0; agent-mcp 2.2.1 boots MCP stdio+SSE; dispatch-cli 0.1.0 library loads CJS+ESM). backlog is the sole broken entrypoint — the 'most entrypoints broken' report was inaccurate.

GENERAL RISK: any future published package that resolves a shipped sibling asset via '../dist' relative to import.meta.url will hit the identical rebase escape. Candidate for a shared apigen-mount asset resolver.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, publish-verification, 1: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts:109-115 (backlogDistDir); 2: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts:202-209 (extractClientOperations mount+throw); 3: entrypoint/backlog/package.json:3-5 (bin ./dist/index.js pre-rebase)]

backlog install-skill broken on published tarball + expand to `install` that registers MCP server in host configs

TWO shipped defects in `backlog install-skill` (reproduced from @adhd/backlog@0.1.1 installed from npm), plus a feature expansion requested by the user.

DEFECT 1 (path escape, BUG-012 class): install-skill.ts packagedSkillMdPath() returns join(dirname(import.meta.url),'..','skill','SKILL.md'). After the publish-from-dist rebase, dirname(import.meta.url) IS the package root, so '../skill' escapes to node_modules/@adhd/skill (missing package-name segment). Reproduced: `node .../@adhd/backlog/index.js install-skill --host opencode --scope project` -> exit 1: `packaged skill file not found at /private/tmp/.../node_modules/@adhd/skill/SKILL.md`. The in-code comment WRONGLY claims skill/ is a sibling of dist 'in a published package' — it is not, because publish is from dist/.

DEFECT 2 (asset not shipped): skill/SKILL.md is never copied into dist/, so it is absent from the published tarball entirely (ls node_modules/@adhd/backlog/skill -> ENOENT; only install-skill.d.ts present). project.json build.options.assets is just ['entrypoint/backlog/*.md']; it must also copy skill/SKILL.md into dist/skill/ (mirror agent-mcp/project.json's assets glob pattern that ships drizzle/ + docs/ into dist). The source package.json files:[...,'skill'] is a red herring — irrelevant under publish-from-dist.

FEATURE (user request): change install-skill -> a richer `install` command that ALSO writes a correct, working MCP server registration into host configs at the right scopes, idempotently, without clobbering existing servers: Claude Code (~/.claude.json mcpServers @ user, <project>/.mcp.json @ project; stdio entry) and opencode (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json mcp.<name> @ user, project opencode.json @ project; {type:'local',command:[...]} entry), plus codex/etc best-effort. Keep install-skill working (back-compat alias). Fix must ship 0.1.2 and be verified from the real registry by driving the WRITTEN config as a real MCP host (37 tools).

GENERAL: the GATE 2 bin smoke only runs `--help`, so it never exercises subcommands (install-skill/serve) — this class of subcommand-only publish breakage is not covered; candidate follow-up to smoke a representative subcommand.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, publish-verification, 1: entrypoint/backlog/src/install-skill.ts:56-64 (packagedSkillMdPath ../skill escape); 2: entrypoint/backlog/project.json build.options.assets (skill/ not copied into dist); 3: empirical run: install-skill exit 1 'node_modules/@adhd/skill/SKILL.md' not found]

agent-engine-compiler resolves sibling @adhd drizzle migrations via 3-hop ../../../ that assumes a nonexistent monolithic dist

Found by repo-wide audit for the BUG-012/BUG-013 publish-rebase path-escape class.

CONFIRMED live in-repo (not just at publish): src/cli/compile.ts (~L47-74) computes AI_DIST = path.resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('.',import.meta.url)), '../../../') and then joins 'agent-core-provider/drizzle' (+4 more siblings). The 3-hop count assumes a MONOLITHIC dist (dist/packages/agent/agent-engine-compiler/src/cli/compile.js) that does not exist — this monorepo builds one dist per project (@nx/js:tsc, packages/agent/agent-engine-compiler/dist/src/cli/compile.js).

Repro: `node packages/agent/agent-engine-compiler/dist/src/cli/compile.js compile some-slug --db /tmp/x.db` -> 5x `migration folder not found: .../agent-engine-compiler/agent-core-provider/drizzle` (all siblings silently skipped by fs.existsSync guard) -> crash `no such table: registry_agents`. Published @2.2.0 works only by npm flat-hoist luck; pnpm's isolated store defeats the 3-hop math.

FIX: resolve sibling migration dirs via real module resolution, not `..` arithmetic. NOTE (verified): require.resolve('<pkg>/package.json') throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED (exports restricts the subpath) — instead createRequire(import.meta.url), req.resolve('<pkg>') then walk up to the package root and join 'drizzle' (each sibling ships drizzle/ at its package root, per the SAFE-verified migrate-runner pattern). Tighten the existsSync-warn-and-continue into a HARD error. Add a regression test that EXECUTES `compile <slug>` (gate blind spot: verify-dist-load only checks bin existence, hygiene only npm-pack-dry-run — neither runs a subcommand).

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, audit, 1: packages/agent/agent-engine-compiler/src/cli/compile.ts:64-74 (AI_DIST 3-hop + sibling joins); 2: packages/agent/agent-engine-compiler/project.json (@nx/js:tsc per-project dist); 3: empirical run: 5x migration-folder-not-found + no-such-table crash]

content:
apigen-python-env published but never ships apigen_python sources into dist — py-grpc/py-flask unusable off-monorepo

Found by repo-wide audit for the publish-rebase path-escape / missing-shipped-asset class.

@adhd/apigen-python-env is published to npm (0.2.0 live) and exports resolvePythonPkgDir() (src/lib/python-env.ts ~L69-90) to locate the apigen_python Python sources (at packages/apigen/python/apigen_python), consumed by @adhd/apigen-plugin-py-grpc and @adhd/apigen-plugin-py-flask. But project.json build.options.assets is only ['packages/apigen/python-env/*.md'] — the Python sources are NEVER copied into dist. So for any consumer installing py-grpc/py-flask from npm OUTSIDE this monorepo, resolvePythonPkgDir()'s primary ('../../../python') AND its 20-level walk-up both fail (dir absent from node_modules); py runtime (spawning Python with the right site-packages) is unusable. Graceful (no load crash) but functionally broken for external consumers.

FIX: (a) ship apigen_python into dist via a project.json assets entry ({input:'packages/apigen/python', glob:'apigen_python/**/*', output:'python', ignore __pycache__/*.pyc}) so it lands at dist/python/apigen_python; (b) make resolvePythonPkgDir probe the co-located bundled copy FIRST (published <pkgRoot>/python/apigen_python + dev-built dist/python/apigen_python), keeping the monorepo-source primary + walk-up as fallbacks. Regression test must simulate the published layout OUTSIDE the monorepo and assert resolution succeeds.

content:
MISSING: clean-room FUNCTIONAL external-consumer e2e + literal global-install host-session (claude/opencode) verification across ALL published libraries

ROOT-CAUSE GAP behind BUG-012/013/014/015 (all four shipped despite green CI): there is NO test that installs the PUBLISHED (rebased) artifact and drives REAL downstream FUNCTIONALITY. The two halves exist but never intersect.

WHAT EXISTS (verified):
- GATE 2 clean-room-smoke.mjs: installs every publishable pkg @latest from the real registry but only checks LIVENESS (bin `--help` comes up / library import() loads). Not functional; never runs a subcommand.
- entrypoint/apigen-cli/src/test/e2e/real-consumer.spec.ts: a genuine functional consumer test (MCP+HTTP, real clients, deep-equal ground truth) BUT (a) runs the WORKSPACE-built bin, not an npm-installed/rebased tarball; (b) apigen generate --link-workspace is documented 'PRE-PUBLISH ONLY ... a published consumer runs npm install instead' — the npm-install path is ASSUMED, not tested; (c) covers only apigen-cli's transform demo, not backlog/agent-*/py-grpc/py-flask/dispatch-*.
- verify-dist-load: bin = existence-only (never executed). publish-hygiene: npm pack --dry-run (file LIST only). nx test: vitest resolves against src/ — the one layout where ../ hop math is always correct. So EVERY gate runs in a frame where the bug is invisible; the shipping frame is never exercised.

BUILD THIS (the capstone that makes the class un-shippable):
1. Shared `packed-consumer-smoke` harness: `npm pack` each package's built dist -> install the TARBALL into an ephemeral external project (exact shipped bytes; deterministic, offline, no propagation lag; runnable PRE-publish as a publish dependsOn so a broken artifact never ships). One functional spec per consumed library asserting the OUTCOME, not liveness:
   - backlog: install tarball -> `backlog serve --transport mcp` -> real MCP client -> tool call returns correct data; + `backlog install`/`install-skill` subcommands actually write/find shipped assets.
   - apigen-cli: the real-consumer proof but against the PACKED tarball + npm install (prove the path the --link-workspace comment only assumes). MUST INCLUDE the ACTUAL global example: `apigen-cli run --source /Users/nix/dev/ai/scratch/agent-browser/search-mcp-source.ts --type mcp` (this is verbatim how apigen-cli is consumed in the global opencode config — ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json mcp.search) — stand it up and drive tools/list + a real tool call.
   - py-grpc/py-flask: generate -> spawn python -> real request (proves BUG-015 shipped python sources resolve).
   - agent-engine-compiler: `compile <slug>` against a real registry DB -> tables created (proves BUG-014).
   - agent-mcp: its loop, from the tarball.
2. LITERAL global-install host-session verification (the real host wiring layer no SDK-client test covers — host config parsing, tool registration, output-size limits, rebased tarball): after a real global install (`pnpm add -g <tarball>` / npm i -g), spawn ACTUAL host CLIs in subshells and assert functional tool output:
   - claude (2.1.220, verified): `claude -p "<prompt that forces a specific tool call>" --mcp-config <json pointing at the globally-installed server> --strict-mcp-config --output-format stream-json` -> assert the tool was invoked and returned the correct payload.
   - opencode (1.18.0, verified): `opencode run --prompt "..."` with the MCP configured (mcp.<name> = {type:'local',command:[...]}) -> assert the tool ran + correct output. Also exercise the agent-browser search MCP + backlog MCP entries specifically.
   These are gated behind an env flag ONLY if they invoke a paid model (per AGENTS.md live-testing rule, documented owner in README+AGENTS.md+test header); the wiring/tool-list assertions that need no model must run by default.
3. Wire the packed-consumer functional gate into publish dependsOn (pre-publish) so it fails the release BEFORE shipping, not after (GATE 2 is post-publish).

SCOPE: every published/consumed library, not just entrypoints. This is the DRY, tarball-based, host-driven external-consumer gate that converts this bug class from whack-a-mole to structurally-impossible.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, publish-verification, 1: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/smoke-test/clean-room-smoke.mjs (liveness-only smoke); 2: entrypoint/apigen-cli/src/test/e2e/real-consumer.spec.ts:1-27 (workspace-built, not tarball); 3: entrypoint/apigen-cli/src/lib/commands/generate.ts:216-217 (--link-workspace 'PRE-PUBLISH ONLY ... published consumer runs npm install instead'); 4: /Users/nix/.config/opencode/opencode.json (mcp.search = apigen-cli run --source agent-browser/search-mcp-source.ts --type mcp); 5: /Users/nix/dev/ai/scratch/agent-browser/search-mcp-source.ts (the real external source); 6: verified claude 2.1.220 --mcp-config/--print + opencode 1.18.0 run/--prompt headless]

ROOT-CAUSE GAP behind BUG-012/013/014/015 (all four shipped despite green CI): there is NO test that installs the PUBLISHED (rebased) artifact and drives REAL downstream FUNCTIONALITY. The two halves exist but never intersect.

WHAT EXISTS (verified):
- GATE 2 clean-room-smoke.mjs: installs every publishable pkg @latest from the real registry but only checks LIVENESS (bin `--help` comes up / library import() loads). Not functional; never runs a subcommand.

- verify-dist-load: bin = existence-only (never executed). publish-hygiene: npm pack --dry-run (file LIST only). nx test: vitest resolves against src/ — the one layout where ../ hop math is always correct. So EVERY gate runs in a frame where the bug is invisible; the shipping frame is never exercised.

Shared `packed-consumer-smoke` harness: `npm pack` each package's built dist -> install the TARBALL into an ephemeral external project (exact shipped bytes; deterministic, offline, no propagation lag; runnable PRE-publish as a publish dependsOn so a broken artifact never ships).    - apigen-cli: the real-consumer proof but against the PACKED tarball + npm install (prove the path the --link-workspace comment only assumes).    These are gated behind an env flag ONLY if they invoke a paid model (per AGENTS.md live-testing rule, documented owner in README+AGENTS.md+test header); the wiring/tool-list assertions that need no model must run by default.
3. Wire the packed-consumer functional gate into publish dependsOn (pre-publish) so it fails the release BEFORE shipping, not after (GATE 2 is post-publish).

project.json build.options.assets is a SILENT NO-OP for all @nx/vite:build packages — latent asset-shipping footgun (generated BUG-013 & BUG-015)

MECHANISM (proven): with this repo's @nx/vite:build version, `targets.build.options.assets` in project.json is silently DROPPED — unrecognized top-level vite key, zero files copied (confirmed via @nx/vite build.impl.js getBuildExtraArgs() + a fresh `nx build data-base-transforms` experiment showing its assets:['*.md'] copies nothing). ~31 vite-built packages declare build.options.assets; every one of those declarations is dead. Developers reasonably assume adding a project.json assets entry ships the file (it DOES for @nx/js:tsc packages like agent-mcp) — for vite packages it ships nothing. This footgun directly generated BUG-013 (backlog skill/) and BUG-015 (python-env apigen_python/): both added/relied on project.json assets and shipped empty.

IMPACT AUDIT (verified, not assumed):
- ~29 packages: assets is only '*.md' — HARMLESS (README/CHANGELOG ship via the separate @adhd/nx-assets publish-pipeline copy target, not build.options.assets).
- apigen-core-client lib/descriptor.schema.json: HARMLESS — inlined into dist/index.js bundle (its $id string is present in the built bundle); the dead lib/*.json asset is dead weight, nothing reads it by path.
- dispatch-base-spec src/*.json (dag-v4.schema.json, valid-ops-by-kind.json): HARMLESS — present in dist/ (emitted by rollup because imported in code).
- backlog skill/: LIVE — not shipped (BUG-013, being fixed via a vite.config.ts writeBundle copy plugin).
- python-env apigen_python/: LIVE — not shipped (BUG-015, fixed via vite writeBundle plugin).

FIX (systemic, so no future vite package silently ships nothing):
1. Remove the ~31 dead build.options.assets declarations (they mislead), OR make @nx/vite:build honor them via a shared vite plugin. Prefer: a single shared workspace vite plugin (e.g. tools/vite-plugins/copy-assets) that reads a declared asset list and does the writeBundle copy — one working mechanism instead of per-package hand-rolled copy plugins (backlog + python-env now each hand-roll their own; DRY that up).
2. Add a build-time assertion / lint: a vite package declaring build.options.assets with a NON-glob-md, runtime-read target must use the working plugin, else fail.
3. Document in AGENTS.md §1/§5: for @nx/vite:build, project.json assets does NOT ship files; use the shared vite copy plugin.
4. TASK-001's tarball functional-consumer gate is the backstop that catches any instance that still slips.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, publish-verification, 1: node_modules/@nx/vite/src/executors/build/build.impl.js getBuildExtraArgs (drops options.assets); 2: 31 vite pkgs w/ dead build.options.assets (grep @nx/vite:build + build.options.assets); 3: packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/dist/index.js (descriptor.schema.json $id inlined — harmless); 4: BUG-013 backlog skill/, BUG-015 python-env apigen_python/ (the two live casualties)]

inferred nx `assets` target declares no `outputs` — a build cache-hit restores stale dist and silently wipes copied assets (non-deterministic)

Found while fixing BUG-013. The globally-inferred/registered `assets` target (@adhd/nx-assets:copy, copies package.json-declared asset dirs into dist/) declares NO `outputs`. Because `build` owns `dist/` as ITS cached output, a later cache-HIT on `build` restores build's OLD dist snapshot (from before `assets` ran) and silently WIPES the asset-copied files (e.g. dist/skill/, dist/drizzle/). Result: `nx test`/publish non-deterministically see or don't see the copied assets depending on invocation/cache history — a Heisenbug that makes 'it shipped last time' unreliable.

CONFIRMED via BUG-013: backlog's dist/skill/ would appear then vanish across runs until hardened. Immediate mitigation applied (backlog-scoped): project.json `assets` target override with explicit `outputs`/`inputs`; also the vite writeBundle plugin makes the build-path copy cache-correct independent of the assets target. But the ROOT is the inferred target's missing `outputs` — GENERAL across every package that relies on @adhd/nx-assets:copy for a runtime asset dir (any package.json with an `assets` array). Note: @adhd/nx-assets:copy DOES honor package.json `assets:[...]` for IN-package dirs (files = ['README.md','CHANGELOG.md','llms.txt','drizzle', ...pkg.assets]) — corrects the earlier claim that only README/CHANGELOG ship; the defect is purely the cache-outputs gap, not the copy itself.

FIX: give the inferred `assets` target (tools/nx-plugins/assets createNodes) a correct `outputs` declaration (its dist asset paths) AND/OR make it not race `build` over dist/ ownership (e.g. build dependsOn assets, or assets writes are part of build's output set). Add a test that proves a `build` cache-hit does NOT drop assets.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, BUG-013-followup, 1: tools/nx-plugins/assets/executors/copy/impl.js (files list incl pkg.assets); 2: inferred assets target createNodes (no outputs); 3: BUG-013 backlog dist/skill/ appear-then-wipe repro]

[transition to FIXED] Fixed in e6e9453e. CORRECTION to the filed mechanism: a build cache-hit does NOT wipe the copied assets — measured directly, they survive it. The actual defect is that the inferred assets target was declared cache:true with NO outputs, and an nx cacheable task with no declared outputs restores nothing on a cache hit while still reporting success. So once assets was cached, a dist missing README.md/CHANGELOG.md/llms.txt stayed missing and a publish shipped a package with no README. The prescribed fix was right even though the mechanism was not. assetOutputs() now enumerates the asset files that actually exist for the project and declares each as an individual {projectRoot}/dist/<basename> output. Per-file, deliberately not the whole dist directory: BUG-026 established that a whole-directory output makes nx do a destructive remove(dir);copy(cachedDir,dir) swap that would wipe the build compiled output; per-file outputs merge. Regression pin bug-017-assets-outputs.spec.mjs: 5/5 green with the fix, 5/5 RED with the plugin reverted, plugin restored and md5-verified. Repro before the fix: rm dist/README.md; nx run backlog:assets -> reads from cache -> README still absent. NOT fixed and filed separately: the executor chmod of pkg.bin targets is still lost on an assets cache hit, since claiming build outputs here would reintroduce BUG-026.

content:
Sequenced Nx 18→19+ then pnpm 10 upgrade — relocate pnpm settings to pnpm-workspace.yaml, eliminate npm Unknown-config warnings

GOAL: stop npm emitting `npm warn Unknown project config "<key>"` on every in-repo npm invocation. FIVE keys warn under npm 11.6.2: node-linker, link-workspace-packages, prefer-workspace-packages, strict-peer-dependencies, auto-install-peers (all in repo .npmrc; all pnpm-recognized so pnpm itself never warns — npm-only wart).

WHY IT'S NOT A QUICK FIX (verified by devops dispatch, all reverted clean):
1. The clean fix is moving these settings to pnpm-workspace.yaml (npm never reads it). But pnpm 9 SILENTLY IGNORES nodeLinker in pnpm-workspace.yaml (falls back to isolated; `pnpm config get nodeLinker`->undefined on 9.15.9) — only pnpm 10.x honors it (`pnpm config get nodeLinker`->hoisted on 10.34.5; per pnpm#9274 / @zkochan). So pnpm 10 is required, not 9.
2. ANY pnpm >=9 bumps pnpm-lock.yaml lockfileVersion '6.0'->'9.0'. Nx 18.3.4 (pinned) CANNOT parse v9.0: `CI=true npx nx build agent-mcp` -> `NX The externalDependency 'eslint' for 'agent-core-policy:sync-deps' could not be found` (Nx native Rust task-hasher builds its external-dep graph from the lockfile). Breaks EVERY project with a sync-deps target (all @nx/dependency-checks users, AGENTS.md §5) — workspace-wide.
3. pnpm 10 also gates native postinstall build scripts by default (supply-chain). Needs an onlyBuiltDependencies allowlist in pnpm-workspace.yaml for better-sqlite3, @swc/core, esbuild, etc. (devops drafted+validated this with a fresh-store install; better-sqlite3 built + require() succeeded).

SEQUENCED PLAN: (a) upgrade Nx 18.3.4 -> 19/20+ via `nx migrate` (parses lockfile v9), prove workspace build/test/sync-deps green; THEN (b) corepack pin pnpm 8.15.9 -> 10.x, move all 5 keys to pnpm-workspace.yaml (camelCase: nodeLinker/linkWorkspacePackages/preferWorkspacePackages/strictPeerDependencies/autoInstallPeers), add onlyBuiltDependencies allowlist, `pnpm install` (lockfile v9), prove: hoisted layout + @adhd/* workspace symlinks intact, nx build/test parity, `npm config ls` from repo root emits ZERO Unknown-config warnings.

INTERIM (not applied — has collateral): `.npmrc loglevel=error` suppresses the npm warnings but also quiets pnpm's own output (pnpm honors loglevel) — rejected. Per-command `--loglevel=error` or a user shell alias `npm='npm --loglevel=error'` works for interactive use without touching repo config.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, devops-dispatch, 1: .npmrc (5 pnpm keys); 2: pnpm#9274 (nodeLinker in pnpm-workspace.yaml only honored on pnpm 10); 3: verified Nx 18.3.4 fails on lockfileVersion 9.0 (sync-deps externalDependency lookup); 4: package.json packageManager pnpm@8.15.9]

Implement backlog INTERFACE_v2 — consolidate 37 MCP tools into 6 (get/query/create/update/relate/admin)

Per docs/spec/backlog/INTERFACE_v2.md: collapse the current 37 backlog MCP tools (backlog_create_item, backlog_get_item, backlog_list_items, backlog_transition_status, ...) into 6 consolidated tools — an 83% reduction in the tool surface every MCP host loads (37 tool schemas -> 6), cutting per-session context + latency substantially.

TARGET SURFACE (mapping fully specified in the spec):
- backlog_get (3 cmds): get-item [+ include:['audit_trail'|'blockers']]
- backlog_query (5): view: list|ready|spotlight|topo|graph
- backlog_create (3): create; splitFrom+children; supersedes+reason
- backlog_update (12): patch/status/priority/assignedTo/claim(claim|release|renew)/addNote/addCitation/softDeleteReason
- backlog_relate (4): {sourceId,targetId,relation:dependency|related|plan,action:add|remove}
- backlog_admin (9): action: archive|export|import|render_markdown|merge|migration_status|set_migration_phase|stale_claims|stats

REQUIREMENTS: preserve ALL existing behavior; every legacy command maps to exactly one consolidated call. `repo` and `by` (present across 24 commands today) are extracted from session context, not passed per-call (see the reporter-capture task, this depends on/pairs with it). Keep back-compat: either retain the 37 legacy tools as thin shims for a deprecation window, or provide a migration for existing callers (agents + the backlog CLI + all mcp__backlog__* consumers in this repo's docs/skills). Regenerate the apigen tool surface (backlog serve --transport mcp) so a real host lists 6 tools, and prove each consolidated tool round-trips via a real MCP client (per AGENTS.md §7 — drive the loaded tools, not a bypass). Update docs/skills that reference the 37-tool names.

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, 1: docs/spec/backlog/INTERFACE_v2.md (full 36->6 mapping + consolidation summary); 2: docs/spec/backlog/INTERFACE_v2.md:95 (repo/by extracted from session context)]

content:
backlog: capture the reporter (filing agent/session/model) as a first-class field, auto-derived from session context

Today the REPORTER of a backlog item — which agent/session/model filed it or added a note/transition — is only captured ad hoc: stuffed into free-text Citations ('[main, claude, session_..., agent-name]') and the note/transition `by` string. There is no structured, queryable reporter field on the item itself. This makes provenance ('who filed/created this?'), accountability, and dedup-by-source impossible without parsing prose.

ASK: capture the reporter as a FIRST-CLASS structured field on items (and on notes/transitions/resolutions), AUTO-DERIVED from the calling session/MCP context — e.g. { reporter: { agent, session, model, via: 'mcp'|'cli' } } — rather than passed per-call. On create/update, if not explicitly provided, populate it from the transport/session context (the same mechanism INTERFACE_v2 uses to extract `repo`+`by` from session context — docs/spec/backlog/INTERFACE_v2.md:95). Backfill/interop: keep accepting an explicit `by` for CLI/non-session callers.

BENEFITS: enables `backlog_query({ filter: { reportedBy } })` (already a claimedBy/assignee-style filter), truthful audit trails, and satisfies AGENTS.md disclosure/citation rules structurally instead of by convention. Pairs with the INTERFACE_v2 consolidation task (session-context extraction is shared infrastructure).

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, 1: docs/spec/backlog/INTERFACE_v2.md:95 (repo/by from session context); 2: entrypoint/backlog/src/model.ts (item schema — add reporter); 3: AGENTS.md Disclosure § (cite-what-you-read / reporter provenance by convention today)]

content:
Promote Repository & Package to first-class graph nodes linked to backlog items (fix repo-key fork at the root)

ASSESSED (debugger, read-only). Model Repository + Package as graph node types linked to items by edges, instead of the embedded `repo`/`projectPath` strings. Motivation: `stats.byRepo` shows the SAME project forked across two keys — `PseudoSky/adhd` (299) vs `adhd` (30, all filed this session) — and this is NOT cosmetic.

WHY IT MATTERS (correctness, not just stats): `repo` is stored as the graph `namespace` column (mapping.ts:11), which is the partition key for BOTH humanId allocation (ids.ts:24-58 computeNextHumanId/findLiveByHumanId) AND the dedupe scan (crud.ts:40-72). So the two forked repo strings run INDEPENDENT id-numbering sequences and independent dedupe scopes — id-collision protection and duplicate detection silently do not span `adhd` vs `PseudoSky/adhd`. `repo` is also duplicated into metadata.repo (no single source of truth) and baked into buildNodeContent()'s FTS marker → into content_hash (mapping.ts:135; DEBT-BACKLOG-CONTENT-HASH-COLLISION-001).

GRAPH-STORE VERDICT: @adhd/sox-graph-store@0.3.0 IS a real typed-node+typed-edge store with traversal (getNeighbors/getSubgraph/isReachable), BUT node `kind` and edge `rel` are CLOSED DB-level CHECK constraints, not open strings. Precedent (already in backlog): plan nodes (kind:'generic' + tag 'backlog-plan', structure.ts:177) and assignee nodes (kind:'entity' + tag 'backlog-assignee' + ASSIGNED_TO edge, structure.ts:199). Upstream explicitly steers new concepts to kind:'generic'+sub-kind-in-tags (index.ts:786; BL-295 extensible-kind attempt was built then REVERTED). Minting NEW edge rels requires an upstream CHECK migration on a SHARED store (memory-server etc.) that has a documented CRITICAL data-loss incident from exactly this op (BL-313) — AVOID.

PROPOSED SHAPE (zero upstream schema change): Repository = kind:'generic' + tag 'backlog-repo', identity = NORMALIZED GIT REMOTE URL (strip .git, canonical host, collapse git@/https forms) with owner/name as display slug — the only signal stable across the fork (basename cannot dedup adhd↔PseudoSky/adhd; env.ts has NO git-remote derivation today, must be written). Package = kind:'generic' + tag 'backlog-package', name=projectPath, MEMBER_OF→Repository. Edges REUSE MEMBER_OF (item→Package→Repository; repo-level items item→Repository) — NO new EdgeRel. stats.byRepo becomes a getNeighbors traversal instead of countByKey string-groupby (query.ts:170).

MIGRATION: additive+reversible for the node/edge layer (find-or-create Repository/Package nodes for the 5 distinct repos + (repo,projectPath) pairs, writeEdge MEMBER_OF for all 341 items). BUT collapsing the fork AT THE SOURCE (namespace/metadata.repo/content/content_hash on the 30 'adhd' items) is NOT free — needs a new repo-rename admin op (none exists; merge_items is item-only) that rewrites those fields transactionally. Also decide what the stray 'global' (2 items) repo means.

EFFORT: **M** for the additive node/edge layer + traversal stats (precedented, zero upstream change, reversible). Escalates to **L** if (a) minting new edge rels [don't], or (b) actually collapsing the namespace/content_hash fork [bespoke migration tool]. No hard blockers; two decisions up front: keep namespace as the id/dedupe partition (additive Repository identity on top — RECOMMENDED, lower risk) vs renegotiate it (touches ids.ts correctness); and write the git-remote-URL canonicalizer.

SEQUENCING: do AFTER TASK-003 (INTERFACE_v2 touches the same store/*.ts — avoid concurrent edits to crud/query/mapping), and BEFORE/ALONGSIDE TASK-004 (reporter+repo-from-session-context is a direct beneficiary — needs correct repo identity). Own reviewed plan; do not fold silently into either.

content:
sox-graph-store: rearchitect for user-defined typed nodes + indexed kinds — closed CHECK-enum `kind`/`rel` forces external consumers to modify the library (anti-pattern)

**Root cause / thesis.** `@adhd/sox-graph-store` is published and consumed as a *generic* typed-node/typed-edge graph store, but its node `kind` and edge `rel` vocabularies are **closed SQLite `CHECK` constraints hard-wired to the memory-server's own ontology** — node.kind ∈ {episode, entity, claim, community, session, generic}; edge.rel ∈ a fixed ~10-value set. An external consumer that wants a first-class node type the library's authors did not foresee (e.g. `Repository`, `Package`) has exactly two options today, both bad: (1) fork/PR the library to add a `CHECK` value — i.e. *modify the dependency to model your own domain* — or (2) smuggle the type in as `kind:'generic'` + a sub-kind string in `tags`/`metadata`. Upstream explicitly steers consumers to option (2) (index.ts:786), and a prior attempt to open the vocabulary (BL-295 extensible-kind) was **built then reverted**. Forcing every downstream consumer to either patch the library or launder their types through an untyped `generic` escape hatch is the anti-pattern this item exists to fix: it is a lack of foresight and an avoidance of proper end-user typing — it is demonstrably **not** justified by performance or maintainability (see below).

**Why it is not a perf/maintainability trade-off (the usual defense of closed enums fails here).**
1. `kind` is **not indexed at all** — the node table carries indexes on `content_hash`, `namespace`, and `uid` only; there is no `ix_node_kind`. So the closed enum buys *zero* query-plan advantage over an open `TEXT` column: a `WHERE kind = ?` is a scan either way. The one place the fixed set could earn its keep — a fast kind-scoped lookup — is precisely the place it is left un-indexed. And the `generic`+tag workaround it pushes consumers toward is **strictly worse** for queryability: retrieving "all Repository nodes" becomes a scan of an **unindexed JSON `tags`/`meta` TEXT column**, with no index exploitable at all.
2. Maintainability is *harmed*, not helped: the escape hatch means the store now has two parallel typing systems (real `kind` for the 6 blessed types, stringly-typed sub-kinds-in-tags for everything else), so every consumer re-implements its own convention (backlog alone already mints `kind:'generic'+tag:'backlog-plan'`, `kind:'entity'+tag:'backlog-assignee'`, and needs `backlog-repo`/`backlog-package`), and none of them are type-checked, indexed, or discoverable.
3. Mutating the shared `CHECK` in place is *itself* the dangerous op the current design pretends to avoid: BL-313 documents a **CRITICAL data-loss incident from an edge CHECK-constraint rebuild** on this shared store. So the status quo simultaneously (a) forbids consumers a safe typed extension and (b) makes the only sanctioned extension path (an upstream CHECK migration) a data-loss risk. That is the worst of both worlds.

**What 'done' looks like (rearchitecture, not a patch).** Give external consumers a supported, indexed, typed extension surface that does **not** require editing the library and does **not** funnel through `generic`:
- **Open the node/edge type vocabulary to consumer-registered types** while keeping validation. Options to weigh in the design (pick one, prove it): a consumer-supplied allow-list / registered-kinds table (the BL-295 direction, done right this time), or drop the DB-level `CHECK` in favor of an application-level (Zod/TS) discriminated-union validated at the write boundary — either way the *library user* declares their kinds, the *library* enforces them, and no source edit is needed.
- **Index the type discriminator.** Add `ix_node_kind` (and, if a `sub_kind`/`type` column is introduced for structured extension types, index that too). The whole justification for a closed set evaporates once you accept the discriminator should be indexed — so index it and let it be open.
- **First-class typed extension nodes** so a consumer can define `Repository`/`Package`-style domain nodes with a real, indexed, queryable type and typed metadata — without a `generic` placeholder and without a fork.
- **Migration must be additive + reversible** and must not repeat BL-313: the shared store (memory-server + every other consumer) must round-trip existing data unchanged; existing `episode/entity/claim/community/session/generic` nodes keep working; no destructive CHECK rebuild on populated tables (use a table-rebuild-with-verify or a constraint-relaxation path that has a proven rollback).
- **Backwards-compatible public API + a real external-consumer test** (per the ecosystem's own live-testing bar): a consumer package that registers a custom kind, writes/reads/traverses it, and queries it via the new index — driven through the *published* package, not an in-repo import.

**Downstream beneficiaries / motivation (this is not hypothetical).** The adhd backlog is already deforming around this defect: TASK-001 (`PseudoSky/adhd`) and FEAT-BACKLOG-004 (`PseudoSky/adhd`) both propose Repository/Package as first-class nodes but are boxed into `kind:'generic'+tag` *specifically because* this library won't let them declare a real kind without an upstream CHECK migration. Fixing the store properly here collapses both of those into a supported feature instead of a workaround. Also adjacent (same package, sequence around it): FEAT-SOX-001 (Turso adapter) touches the same `store`/schema layer — coordinate schema changes to avoid concurrent CHECK/DDL edits; the type-openness work is orthogonal to the backend-engine swap but should not land as two conflicting migrations.

**Blast radius (library-internal).** `src/index.ts` (node/edge DDL + CHECK definitions ~ the `kind IN (...)` / `rel IN (...)` clauses and the `generic`-steer comment at ~:786), the schema/migration path, the TS type exports for `NodeKind`/`EdgeRel`, and the write/validate seam. External: every consumer that currently hard-codes `kind:'generic'`+tag (backlog `store/structure.ts`) gets a supported path but must not be forced to migrate immediately (keep `generic` working).

Citations: [main, claude, session_017XwVLwd4BHf2U6jpUysshX, sox-graph-store-rearchitecture, 1: ~/dev/ai/sox-ecosystem/libs/data/graph/graph-store/src/index.ts (node DDL: kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('episode','entity','claim','community','session','generic')); edge DDL: rel TEXT CHECK(...~10 values...); indexes ix_node_hash / ix_node_namespace / node_uid_unique only — NO ix_node_kind); 2: same file ~:786 (explicit steer of new concepts to kind:'generic'+sub-kind-in-tags); 3: BL-295 (extensible-kind attempt built then REVERTED); 4: BL-313 (CRITICAL edge-cascade data-loss from CHECK-constraint rebuild on the shared store); 5: entrypoint/backlog/src/store/structure.ts:177,199 (downstream generic+tag workaround — plan & assignee nodes); 6: backlog TASK-001 & FEAT-BACKLOG-004 (downstream Repository/Package modeling blocked on this)]
