content:
Unbounded, non-reentrant 5-min enrich timer causes overlapping healMissingVectors ticks to re-scan and discard the same head-of-queue rows — this, not lock contention or CPU saturation, is why the embed backlog never drains

**Supersedes/corrects the root-cause premise of the markdown-only BL-322 entry in BACKLOG.md** ("Analyze lock contention between embedding system, daemon, proxy, and agents", driver: "97% CPU with the enrich pipeline", candidate cause "Turso's EXCLUSIVE file locking"). Both are disproven for the current state: team-lead measured the live backend pid at 0.0% CPU while memory_recall still timed out (no saturation), and BL-322's own already-updated notes confirm `multiprocess_wal` is enabled by default (`turso-adapter.ts:111-115`), eliminating EXCLUSIVE-lock contention as a candidate. **I was unable to correct BL-322 in place via the backlog tool**: this repo's `backlog migration-status` reports phase-3 (tool-authoritative), but `backlog get-item --repo sox-ecosystem --human-id BL-322` returns null and `backlog list-items` finds no matching item — BL-319/BL-322 exist ONLY as hand-maintained markdown in BACKLOG.md and were never imported into the graph. A `backlog import-from-markdown` dry-run confirmed 42 parseable headers but a non-dry-run import was blocked by this session's Bash permission classifier as an unreviewed bulk-write. Recommend the repo owner either explicitly authorize `backlog import-from-markdown --input '{"path":"BACKLOG.md","repo":"sox-ecosystem"}'` (bringing BL-319/BL-322 under tool authority so they can be corrected in place) or hand-edit BL-322's driver section directly, citing this item.

**Root cause, verified directly by reading source:**
`extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:2041-2044` (read in full, lines 1970-2044):
```
const _periodicEnrichTimer = setInterval(() => {
  void runPeriodicEnrichPass();
}, PERIODIC_ENRICH_INTERVAL_MS);  // 5 minutes (index.ts:1848)
```
This is a bare `setInterval` with **no reentrancy guard** — nothing prevents tick N+1 from firing while tick N's `runPeriodicEnrichPass` → `runEnrichPassOnDb` → `healMissingVectors` async chain is still in flight. `healMissingVectors` (libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:560-652, read in full) selects up to `limit` (default region of the function, `ORDER BY n.rowid ASC LIMIT ?` at line 583) pending rows and sequentially embeds each one through a single shared child process (`embedWithTimeout` → `embed()`, lines 613-678) — with p50 embed duration around 25 minutes per team-lead's measurement, a single pass over 500 rows vastly exceeds the 5-minute tick interval, so overlapping ticks are guaranteed under any nontrivial backlog.

Both overlapping ticks re-run the identical `SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vec_node v WHERE v.node_id = n.rowid) ORDER BY n.rowid ASC LIMIT ?` (embed-pipeline.ts:574-585) — the same head-of-queue rows, since neither tick has landed a vec_node row for them yet at selection time. When the slower/later tick's embed for a given row finally completes, `applyEmbedding` (embed-pipeline.ts:380-407, read in full) checks `SELECT node_id FROM vec_node WHERE node_id = ?` (lines 395-398) and returns `{status:'exists'}` without inserting if a faster/earlier tick already landed that row's vector — this exists-check is CORRECT and not itself a bug (confirmed by reading it directly: it prevents double-insert, which vec0/native-vector tables would otherwise reject). But the LOSING tick's expensive ~25-minute embed computation for that row is entirely wasted: `heals_applied` does not increment (status is 'exists', not 'applied' — embed-pipeline.ts:632-635 only increments on 'applied'), while `embeds_completed` DOES increment (embed-pipeline.ts:621, unconditional on successful embed() regardless of apply outcome) and `applies_exists` increments (recordApplyOutcome, embed-pipeline.ts:301-304).

This exactly matches team-lead's live measurement: two `memory_ping` samples 12 minutes apart showed `embeds_completed +33`, `applies_exists +33`, `applies_applied +0` — i.e. every embed computed in that window was thrown away as a duplicate of work another overlapping tick had already landed, and the backlog count itself never moved (frozen at 4241 for five weeks). The child embed process (pid 42845 per team-lead) burned ~650 CPU-minutes to land only 169 real vectors — the CPU cost is real work, just almost entirely wasted work, not lock contention or lock-driven saturation.

**Important correction to avoid propagating a wrong theory:** the write/heal/apply predicates (missing-vector selection, exists-check before insert) are internally consistent and correctly symmetric between the write path and the heal path — there is NO sqlite-vs-turso predicate mismatch, and `applyEmbedding`'s exists-check is not itself a defect. If any other backlog item states otherwise, it should be corrected to point here.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Add a reentrancy guard around `runPeriodicEnrichPass` — a simple in-flight boolean/promise so a new tick observes a pass already running and skips (or queues) rather than starting a redundant duplicate pass over the same head-of-queue rows.
2. Alternatively/additionally, have `healMissingVectors` claim rows (e.g. an in-progress marker or `ORDER BY rowid ASC` cursor that advances past already-claimed-but-not-yet-applied rows) so two concurrent passes partition rather than duplicate work — more robust than a single global lock if a future design wants bounded parallelism.
3. Either way, the single shared child embed process (`sharedFastembedProcess.ts`) remains the real throughput ceiling once duplicate work is eliminated — BL-322's residual, still-open question ("does the singleton fastembed process cause head-of-line blocking for all embed requests? can we have a read-only embed queue?") remains valid and should stay open once the driver section is corrected.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that starts two concurrent `runEnrichPassOnDb` calls (or triggers the periodic timer twice in quick succession) against a store with a backlog exceeding what a single pass can drain within the tick interval, and asserts (a) today, both passes select and (wastefully) embed the same rows, `applies_exists` increments while `applies_applied` for those specific rows is 0 for the losing tick (red); (b) after the fix, only one pass runs at a time (or work is partitioned), no row is embedded twice, and `heals_applied` for a given backlog batch strictly increases with wall-clock time proportional to real embed throughput, not flatlines (green).

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE, 1: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:1848,1970-2044 (PERIODIC_ENRICH_INTERVAL_MS, runEnrichPassOnDb, runPeriodicEnrichPass, bare setInterval with no reentrancy guard) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:560-652 (healMissingVectors: LIMIT-bounded SELECT, sequential embed through shared child process, embedWithTimeout) — read directly; 3: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:380-407 (applyEmbedding: gone-check lines 387-393, exists-check lines 395-401, correct and not itself buggy) — read directly; 4: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:301-304,621,632-635 (recordApplyOutcome counters: applies_applied/applies_exists/applies_gone; embeds_completed increments unconditionally on successful embed() regardless of apply outcome) — read directly; 5: BACKLOG.md:899-935 (existing BL-322 markdown entry — driver section is the claim being corrected) — read directly; 6: live memory_ping deltas (embeds_completed +33 / applies_exists +33 / applies_applied +0 over 12 min; child pid 42845 ~650 CPU-min for 169 landed vectors; backend pid 0.0% CPU while memory_recall still timed out) — reported by team-lead, not independently reproduced by this agent (would require live queries against the running store, out of scope per this agent's constraints); 7: `backlog get-item --repo sox-ecosystem --human-id BL-322` → null, `backlog import-from-markdown --input '{...,"dryRun":true}'` → parsed:42/created:0, non-dry-run import blocked by Bash permission classifier — verified directly this session]

Both are disproven for the current state: team-lead measured the live backend pid at 0.0% CPU while memory_recall still timed out (no saturation), and BL-322's own already-updated notes confirm `multiprocess_wal` is enabled by default (`turso-adapter.ts:111-115`), eliminating EXCLUSIVE-lock contention as a candidate. **I was unable to correct BL-322 in place via the backlog tool**: this repo's `backlog migration-status` reports phase-3 (tool-authoritative), but `backlog get-item --repo sox-ecosystem --human-id BL-322` returns null and `backlog list-items` finds no matching item — BL-319/BL-322 exist ONLY as hand-maintained markdown in BACKLOG.md and were never imported into the graph. A `backlog import-from-markdown` dry-run confirmed 42 parseable headers but a non-dry-run import was blocked by this session's Bash permission classifier as an unreviewed bulk-write. Recommend the repo owner either explicitly authorize `backlog import-from-markdown --input '{"path":"BACKLOG.md","repo":"sox-ecosystem"}'` (bringing BL-319/BL-322 under tool authority so they can be corrected in place) or hand-edit BL-322's driver section directly, citing this item.

**Root cause, verified directly by reading source:**
`extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:2041-2044` (read in full, lines 1970-2044):
```
const _periodicEnrichTimer = setInterval(() => {
  void runPeriodicEnrichPass();
}, PERIODIC_ENRICH_INTERVAL_MS);  // 5 minutes (index.ts:1848)
```
This is a bare `setInterval` with **no reentrancy guard** — nothing prevents tick N+1 from firing while tick N's `runPeriodicEnrichPass` → `runEnrichPassOnDb` → `healMissingVectors` async chain is still in flight. `healMissingVectors` (libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:560-652, read in full) selects up to `limit` (default region of the function, `ORDER BY n.rowid ASC LIMIT ?` at line 583) pending rows and sequentially embeds each one through a single shared child process (`embedWithTimeout` → `embed()`, lines 613-678) — with p50 embed duration around 25 minutes per team-lead's measurement, a single pass over 500 rows vastly exceeds the 5-minute tick interval, so overlapping ticks are guaranteed under any nontrivial backlog.

Both overlapping ticks re-run the identical `SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vec_node v WHERE v.node_id = n.rowid) ORDER BY n.rowid ASC LIMIT ?` (embed-pipeline.ts:574-585) — the same head-of-queue rows, since neither tick has landed a vec_node row for them yet at selection time. When the slower/later tick's embed for a given row finally completes, `applyEmbedding` (embed-pipeline.ts:380-407, read in full) checks `SELECT node_id FROM vec_node WHERE node_id = ?` (lines 395-398) and returns `{status:'exists'}` without inserting if a faster/earlier tick already landed that row's vector — this exists-check is CORRECT and not itself a bug (confirmed by reading it directly: it prevents double-insert, which vec0/native-vector tables would otherwise reject). But the LOSING tick's expensive ~25-minute embed computation for that row is entirely wasted: `heals_applied` does not increment (status is 'exists', not 'applied' — embed-pipeline.ts:632-635 only increments on 'applied'), while `embeds_completed` DOES increment (embed-pipeline.ts:621, unconditional on successful embed() regardless of apply outcome) and `applies_exists` increments (recordApplyOutcome, embed-pipeline.ts:301-304).

This exactly matches team-lead's live measurement: two `memory_ping` samples 12 minutes apart showed `embeds_completed +33`, `applies_exists +33`, `applies_applied +0` — i.e. every embed computed in that window was thrown away as a duplicate of work another overlapping tick had already landed, and the backlog count itself never moved (frozen at 4241 for five weeks). The child embed process (pid 42845 per team-lead) burned ~650 CPU-minutes to land only 169 real vectors — the CPU cost is real work, just almost entirely wasted work, not lock contention or lock-driven saturation.

**Important correction to avoid propagating a wrong theory:** the write/heal/apply predicates (missing-vector selection, exists-check before insert) are internally consistent and correctly symmetric between the write path and the heal path — there is NO sqlite-vs-turso predicate mismatch, and `applyEmbedding`'s exists-check is not itself a defect. If any other backlog item states otherwise, it should be corrected to point here.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Add a reentrancy guard around `runPeriodicEnrichPass` — a simple in-flight boolean/promise so a new tick observes a pass already running and skips (or queues) rather than starting a redundant duplicate pass over the same head-of-queue rows.
2. Alternatively/additionally, have `healMissingVectors` claim rows (e.g. an in-progress marker or `ORDER BY rowid ASC` cursor that advances past already-claimed-but-not-yet-applied rows) so two concurrent passes partition rather than duplicate work — more robust than a single global lock if a future design wants bounded parallelism.
3. Either way, the single shared child embed process (`sharedFastembedProcess.ts`) remains the real throughput ceiling once duplicate work is eliminated — BL-322's residual, still-open question ("does the singleton fastembed process cause head-of-line blocking for all embed requests? can we have a read-only embed queue?") remains valid and should stay open once the driver section is corrected.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that starts two concurrent `runEnrichPassOnDb` calls (or triggers the periodic timer twice in quick succession) against a store with a backlog exceeding what a single pass can drain within the tick interval, and asserts (a) today, both passes select and (wastefully) embed the same rows, `applies_exists` increments while `applies_applied` for those specific rows is 0 for the losing tick (red); (b) after the fix, only one pass runs at a time (or work is partitioned), no row is embedded twice, and `heals_applied` for a given backlog batch strictly increases with wall-clock time proportional to real embed throughput, not flatlines (green).

content:
DETERMINATION NEEDED (not an unattended alarm): are the 716 pre-swap nodes — 403 episodes + 313 entities, 669 live/valid — still absent from the live store? The recovery actually performed was a clean-backup restore from the 12:15 snapshot, NOT the .recover salvage this item assumes, which reframes the 716 as a probable 12:15-to-15:30 write delta

Filed on explicit authorization from the store owner (relayed via team-lead) during the live TursoAdapter go-live incident triage. **Provenance note: the forensic comparison below was performed by a sibling agent (`db-repair`) working directly against backup/live store files under ~/.memory/, which this agent (`triage`) was explicitly instructed not to touch.** This item is filed on the store owner's authority to record the finding durably and is NOT independently re-verified by opening the referenced .db files myself — treat the specific counts as db-repair's reported forensic result, not this agent's own citation, pending db-repair's own verification pass.

**Reported finding:** comparing the live store against `memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap`, 716 uids present in the pre-swap backup are absent from the live store — 403 episodes + 313 entities. Of those, 669 are reported live/valid at the time of the pre-swap snapshot (not tombstoned/invalidated), meaning their loss is not explained by legitimate bi-temporal invalidation — this is unrecovered content loss, not expected supersession. Approximately 3027 edges that referenced those 716 nodes are also gone (edges cannot reference nonexistent nodes, so their loss is a direct consequence). Additionally reported: 4247 `organizer_queue` history rows lost, and the entire `memory_scope` config table has ZERO rows in the live store (the live server is reportedly inferring the embed model/dimension — bge-base-en-v1.5/768 — from a `sox_store_meta` fallback rather than from `memory_scope`, meaning that config table's loss is currently masked by a fallback path rather than surfaced as an error).

**Recoverability:** per db-repair, 712 of the 716 missing nodes are recoverable from a second backup, `memory.db.20260729-183823.corrupt` — reported as genuinely truncated (header declares 27,493 pages, only 18,779 present on disk, ~35.7MB short of its declared size) but salvageable via `sqlite3 .recover`. db-repair is reported to be building the restore at time of filing.

**Why this is the highest-severity item of this triage round:** every other item filed in this round (migration safety, missing FTS/vec DDL, enrich-tick stampede, uncommitted Turso wiring) describes defects that degrade availability, observability, or correctness of NEW/ongoing operations — all recoverable by re-running a fixed pipeline. This item describes actual, currently-unrecovered content loss of live user data with no automatic self-healing path; if the corrupt backup's `.recover` salvage fails or is incomplete, the 669 live/valid nodes and their ~3027 edges are gone permanently.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Complete db-repair's `.recover`-based salvage of `memory.db.20260729-183823.corrupt` and apply the recovered 712/716 nodes (plus their edges) back into the live store, with a verified row-count and content-hash check against the pre-swap backup for every recovered node.
2. For the remaining 4 of 716 not recoverable from the corrupt backup, check whether any other backup snapshot (see also BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP-001's June backups) covers them; if not, document them as a permanent, acknowledged loss with full uid list.
3. Root-cause how a corrupt/truncated backup (35.7MB short) and a fully-emptied `memory_scope` table came to exist in the first place — this item covers restoring the data; it does NOT explain the mechanism that caused the loss, which should be tracked as a follow-up once db-repair's restore work surfaces more evidence (do not close this item on restore alone if the causal mechanism remains unknown — reopen or file a companion root-cause item).
4. Add integrity guardrails so a future backup/swap operation cannot silently produce a truncated file or an emptied config table without failing loudly (ties into BUG-STOREADAPTER-MIGRATE-UNSAFE-001's verification gaps, though this specific loss predates and is broader than that migration script).

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a script/test that (a) enumerates all 716 uids present in `memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap` but absent from the live store today (red baseline, must reproduce the 716/403/313 split), (b) after the restore, re-runs the same enumeration and asserts the recoverable 712 are present with matching content hashes to the pre-swap backup, and (c) asserts `memory_scope` has the expected row(s) restored rather than relying on the `sox_store_meta` fallback. Must fail red today and pass green after db-repair's fix lands.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, BUG-MEMORY-DATALOSS-716-NODES, 1: forensic diff of live store vs memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap (716 missing uids: 403 episodes + 313 entities, 669 reported live/valid, ~3027 referencing edges, 4247 lost organizer_queue rows, memory_scope zero rows) — reported by db-repair agent via team-lead, NOT independently opened/verified by this agent per its ~/.memory/ non-touch constraint; 2: memory.db.20260729-183823.corrupt header vs actual file size (declared 27,493 pages, 18,779 present, ~35.7MB short) and sqlite3 .recover salvage plan for 712/716 nodes — reported by db-repair agent via team-lead, not independently verified by this agent]

meta_parsed.title: DETERMINATION NEEDED (not an unattended alarm): are the 716 pre-swap nodes — 403 episodes + 313 entities, 669 live/valid — still absent from the live store? The recovery actually performed was a clean-backup restore from the 12:15 snapshot, NOT the .recover salvage this item assumes, which reframes the 716 as a probable 12:15-to-15:30 write delta
meta_parsed.body:
Filed on explicit authorization from the store owner (relayed via team-lead) during the live TursoAdapter go-live incident triage. **Provenance note: the forensic comparison below was performed by a sibling agent (`db-repair`) working directly against backup/live store files under ~/.memory/, which this agent (`triage`) was explicitly instructed not to touch.** This item is filed on the store owner's authority to record the finding durably and is NOT independently re-verified by opening the referenced .db files myself — treat the specific counts as db-repair's reported forensic result, not this agent's own citation, pending db-repair's own verification pass.

**Reported finding:** comparing the live store against `memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap`, 716 uids present in the pre-swap backup are absent from the live store — 403 episodes + 313 entities. Of those, 669 are reported live/valid at the time of the pre-swap snapshot (not tombstoned/invalidated), meaning their loss is not explained by legitimate bi-temporal invalidation — this is unrecovered content loss, not expected supersession. Approximately 3027 edges that referenced those 716 nodes are also gone (edges cannot reference nonexistent nodes, so their loss is a direct consequence). Additionally reported: 4247 `organizer_queue` history rows lost, and the entire `memory_scope` config table has ZERO rows in the live store (the live server is reportedly inferring the embed model/dimension — bge-base-en-v1.5/768 — from a `sox_store_meta` fallback rather than from `memory_scope`, meaning that config table's loss is currently masked by a fallback path rather than surfaced as an error).

**Recoverability:** per db-repair, 712 of the 716 missing nodes are recoverable from a second backup, `memory.db.20260729-183823.corrupt` — reported as genuinely truncated (header declares 27,493 pages, only 18,779 present on disk, ~35.7MB short of its declared size) but salvageable via `sqlite3 .recover`. db-repair is reported to be building the restore at time of filing.

**Why this is the highest-severity item of this triage round:** every other item filed in this round (migration safety, missing FTS/vec DDL, enrich-tick stampede, uncommitted Turso wiring) describes defects that degrade availability, observability, or correctness of NEW/ongoing operations — all recoverable by re-running a fixed pipeline. This item describes actual, currently-unrecovered content loss of live user data with no automatic self-healing path; if the corrupt backup's `.recover` salvage fails or is incomplete, the 669 live/valid nodes and their ~3027 edges are gone permanently.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Complete db-repair's `.recover`-based salvage of `memory.db.20260729-183823.corrupt` and apply the recovered 712/716 nodes (plus their edges) back into the live store, with a verified row-count and content-hash check against the pre-swap backup for every recovered node.
2. For the remaining 4 of 716 not recoverable from the corrupt backup, check whether any other backup snapshot (see also BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP-001's June backups) covers them; if not, document them as a permanent, acknowledged loss with full uid list.
3. Root-cause how a corrupt/truncated backup (35.7MB short) and a fully-emptied `memory_scope` table came to exist in the first place — this item covers restoring the data; it does NOT explain the mechanism that caused the loss, which should be tracked as a follow-up once db-repair's restore work surfaces more evidence (do not close this item on restore alone if the causal mechanism remains unknown — reopen or file a companion root-cause item).
4. Add integrity guardrails so a future backup/swap operation cannot silently produce a truncated file or an emptied config table without failing loudly (ties into BUG-STOREADAPTER-MIGRATE-UNSAFE-001's verification gaps, though this specific loss predates and is broader than that migration script).

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a script/test that (a) enumerates all 716 uids present in `memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap` but absent from the live store today (red baseline, must reproduce the 716/403/313 split), (b) after the restore, re-runs the same enumeration and asserts the recoverable 712 are present with matching content hashes to the pre-swap backup, and (c) asserts `memory_scope` has the expected row(s) restored rather than relying on the `sox_store_meta` fallback. Must fail red today and pass green after db-repair's fix lands.

Vector coverage collapsed BEFORE the Turso swap — pre-swap 49MB backup has no vec_node table at all, June backups do; root cause of when/why vectors were dropped is still unknown

Filed on explicit authorization from the store owner (relayed via team-lead), same provenance caveat as BUG-MEMORY-DATALOSS-716-NODES-001: the backup-file forensics below were performed by the `db-repair` agent against files under ~/.memory/, which this agent was instructed not to touch, and are relayed (not independently re-verified) findings.

**Reported finding:** `memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap` (49MB) — the backup taken immediately before the TursoAdapter swap — has NO `vec_node` table at all. Earlier June backups (`bak-reembed`, `bak-quickfix`, exact filenames/dates as captured by db-repair) DO have populated legacy `vec0` tables. This means the vector-coverage collapse (the store having zero or near-zero usable vectors) predates the Turso migration entirely — the migration inherited an already-empty vector state rather than causing it. This is an important correction to the working theory that the TursoAdapter migration itself destroyed the vectors (that theory is what BUG-STOREADAPTER-MIGRATE-UNSAFE-001 investigates as a *risk*, correctly, but the live incident's actual vector loss appears to have a different, earlier cause not yet identified).

**Open question this item exists to track:** what happened between the last known-good June backup (with a populated `vec0` table) and the 2026-07-28 pre-swap backup (with no `vec_node` table at all) that dropped the vector data? Candidates not yet investigated: an intermediate re-embed/schema-migration step that dropped and never recreated the table, a manual `DROP TABLE`/reset during earlier debugging, a botched attempt at the same kind of adapter/schema swap this repo has now had trouble with twice, or an unrelated cleanup script. This item does not resolve the question — it exists to make sure the question is tracked and not lost once the immediate recovery work (BUG-MEMORY-DATALOSS-716-NODES-001) lands and the incident feels 'closed'.

**Secondary finding — the reported live embed_backlog metric appears to undercount:** db-repair's forensic count found 4325 episodes lacking vectors, vs. the 4241 reported by the live `memory_ping.embed_backlog` field — a discrepancy of ~84. This should be reconciled once BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001's fix lands and the backlog metric can be trusted again; if the discrepancy persists after that fix, the `embedBacklogStats()` query itself (memory-server/src/index.ts, feeding the `embed_backlog` field read at index.ts:918) likely has its own undercount bug worth a dedicated item.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Bisect available backups (June `bak-reembed`/`bak-quickfix` → 2026-07-28 pre-swap) by date to narrow the window where `vec_node`/`vec0` was dropped, using whatever backup/snapshot cadence exists between them.
2. Check `_adapter_meta`/`sox_store_meta`/`organizer_queue` history (where recoverable) for any migration or schema-change event logged in that window that would explain a table drop.
3. Once the mechanism is identified, file a companion root-cause item (or fold into this one) with the actual cause and a guardrail (e.g. a pre-flight check refusing any schema operation that would drop `vec_node` without an explicit, logged, human-approved reason).
4. Reconcile the ~84-row embed_backlog undercount once the pipeline is unstuck (BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001) and stable long enough to compare a fresh count against a fresh forensic scan.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** this is fundamentally an investigation item; the 'green' bar is a dated timeline (or explicit 'undeterminable — no further backups exist to bisect with' conclusion) identifying which backup interval the vec_node/vec0 table was dropped in, plus either a root-caused mechanism or an explicit acknowledgment that it's unrecoverable. A red→green test is not directly applicable to root-cause investigation; if a mechanism is found and fixed, that fix should get its own item with its own red→green test per repo policy.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP, 1: memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap (49MB, no vec_node table) vs June backups bak-reembed/bak-quickfix (populated legacy vec0 tables) — reported by db-repair agent via team-lead, not independently verified by this agent per its ~/.memory/ non-touch constraint; 2: forensic count of 4325 episodes lacking vectors vs live memory_ping.embed_backlog=4241 — reported by db-repair agent via team-lead; 3: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:918 (embed_backlog field, fed by embedBacklogStats()) — read directly by this agent as the likely site of the undercount if it persists post-fix]

Given the scale of the current Turso migration work touching `libs/memory-core/src/db.ts` (uncommitted 599→8xx line rewrite, see BUG-DB-TURSO-WIRING-UNCOMMITTED-001) and `embed-pipeline.ts`, shipping this without a typecheck gate risks a repeat of the BL-248/249/250 incident at exactly the worst time — mid-incident-recovery, under time pressure, with reduced review bandwidth.

~19 memory-core spec files call openDb(...) without await after it became async — ~267 test failures (test debt from the sync→async StoreAdapter migration, not a runtime regression)

Verified directly. `grep -rn '= openDb(' libs/memory-core/src/*.spec.ts | grep -v 'await openDb'` returns unawaited call sites across at least these spec files (grep output, read directly): `backup.spec.ts:80,139`; `db.spec.ts:81,108,129,136,150,161,175,189,204,211,232`; `embed-provenance.spec.ts:70`; `invalidate.spec.ts:39`; `compaction.spec.ts:59`; `outbox-queue.spec.ts:41`; `reembed.spec.ts:88,317,352` — consistent with team-lead's reported count of ~19 affected spec files. `openDb()` in the current (uncommitted, in-flight) `libs/memory-core/src/db.ts` is `async` (calls `await createStoreAdapter(...)` per the fix for BUG-DB-TURSO-WIRING-UNCOMMITTED-001), so every unawaited call site above now assigns a `Promise<...>` to `db`/`rawDb` instead of the resolved adapter/database handle, and every subsequent synchronous method call on that variable in the test body will fail or behave incorrectly at runtime.

This is TEST debt, not a production runtime regression: `openDb()`'s production call sites (in `index.ts` and elsewhere in `src/`) already `await` it correctly per the earlier grep pass for BUG-DB-TURSO-WIRING-UNCOMMITTED-001/BUG-DB-OPENDB-MISSING-FTS-VEC-DDL-001's investigation — this item is specifically about the test suite not having been updated in lockstep with `openDb()`'s sync→async signature change, reported to produce ~267 test failures across the affected files (not independently re-run by this agent — `nx test` was avoided per this session's scope, which is investigation/filing only, not fixing or executing test/build commands beyond read-only greps).

**Fix sketch:** add `await` to every `openDb(...)`/`openDbReadOnly(...)`-family call site in the listed spec files (and any not caught by the grep pattern above — re-run the grep after this item's fix to confirm zero remaining unawaited call sites), then run `npx nx test memory-core` and confirm the ~267 failures resolve to 0 (any residual failures are then genuine regressions, not this debt, and should be triaged separately per the repo's accountability rule against attributing new failures to 'test debt').

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** `npx nx test memory-core` fails today (red, ~267 failures per team-lead's count — not independently reproduced by this agent) and passes clean (green, modulo any genuinely new/unrelated failures which must be individually triaged, not swept into this item's resolution) after every listed call site is corrected to `await openDb(...)`.

Backup/snapshotting system for live backlog stores across adhd env scopes — corruption-proofing for the graph store

**Motivation:** Discovered during this session's `BUG-BACKLOG-HUMANID-COLLISION-001` incident and its own investigation/repair. The backlog graph store (`@adhd/sox-graph-store`-backed SQLite, opened via `entrypoint/backlog`'s `openGraphBacklogStore`) is a shared, live-mutated, multi-agent-write data store with real production data (backlog items, citations, notes, audit trail) and currently has **no backup/snapshot/point-in-time-recovery mechanism** of any kind. Two concrete incidents this session illustrate the real risk:
1. A `(repo, humanId)` collision (`BUG-BACKLOG-HUMANID-COLLISION-001`) caused a `backlog_resolve_item` call to silently mutate the WRONG node's status/notes/citations -- a real, if non-destructive-in-that-instance, write to the wrong record with no way to cheaply diff/rollback against a known-good prior state.
2. That same bug's fix requires a one-off data-repair script that renames 4 colliding humanIds directly against the live store -- a genuinely irreversible mutation (no rename/undo primitive exists) being run against the SAME store every other concurrent agent session in this repo reads/writes, with no snapshot taken beforehand to fall back to if the repair script has its own bug.

**Scope -- "across adhd env scopes":** the backlog store's location is resolved via the environment cascade (`@adhd/environment`), varying by scope: global (`~/.adhd/...` or equivalent), project (`.adhd/` within a given repo), and possibly per-repo namespace within a single global store (this repo's own `repo` field, e.g. `PseudoSky/adhd` vs `global`). A real backup system needs to account for ALL of these -- a snapshot mechanism that only covers one scope (e.g. project-local) while the store is actually shared/global would miss the exact multi-agent-shared risk that motivated this item.

**Fix direction (not yet investigated in depth -- initial sketch only):**
1. **Point-in-time snapshotting:** periodic (e.g. cron/scheduled, or pre-mutation-hook) SQLite-level snapshot of the backlog `.db` file(s) -- either via SQLite's own online backup API (`VACUUM INTO`, or the `sqlite3_backup_*` C API if the underlying driver exposes it), or simple file-level copy-on-write snapshotting if WAL mode allows a consistent point-in-time copy without stopping writers. Research the safest approach given this store already uses WAL mode + `busy_timeout` (per `DESIGN.md` §3) for concurrent readers/writer.
2. **Retention policy:** rolling window (e.g. last N snapshots / last N days) so this doesn't grow unbounded -- store snapshots under `tmp/` or a dedicated gitignored backup root per this repo's "ephemeral artifacts" convention (CLAUDE.md §10), NOT tracked in git (this is operational/runtime data, not source).
3. **Pre-risky-operation snapshot hook:** specifically for one-off data-repair/migration scripts (like the humanId-collision repair) -- a lightweight `snapshotBeforeRepair()` helper that any repair script can call first, so a bad repair has an immediate, cheap rollback path without needing the periodic snapshot to have happened to land at the right moment.
4. **Restore tooling:** a `backlog` CLI subcommand (or documented manual procedure) to restore from a named snapshot -- must be safe under the same multi-agent-concurrent-write assumption as everything else in this store (see `DESIGN.md` §4's CAS protocol) -- likely requires taking the store offline / advisory-locking during restore, which needs its own design thought given other agents may be actively writing.
5. Consider whether this generalizes beyond just the backlog store -- other live SQLite-backed stores in this repo (agent registry DBs, memory-server's graph DB, etc.) may have the identical gap and could share the same snapshotting mechanism/tooling rather than each inventing its own.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, session-2026-07-30, 1: BUG-BACKLOG-HUMANID-COLLISION-001 (the incident that motivated this item -- a resolve_item call silently mutated the wrong node with no rollback path); 2: entrypoint/backlog/DESIGN.md §3 (WAL mode + busy_timeout, existing concurrency design this backup mechanism must be compatible with); 3: entrypoint/backlog/DESIGN.md §4 (CAS claim protocol -- any restore tooling must respect this under concurrent writers); 4: packages/environment/ (env cascade resolving store location across global/project scopes -- the backup mechanism must cover every scope the store can live in); 5: CLAUDE.md §10 (ephemeral/backup artifacts convention -- tmp/ root, gitignored, not tracked)]

recall-parity.test.ts and heal-backend-agnostic.test.ts have NEVER executed their Turso half — vitest freezes `{skip}` at synchronous collection, before the async beforeAll that sets hasTurso runs

Verified directly by reading both files plus the newly-added `turso-clean-room.test.ts` (untracked at time of filing) which documents and fixes the same bug in its own header comment.

`extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/recall-parity.test.ts:119-139`: `let hasTurso = false;` at describe scope, then `beforeAll(async () => { hasTurso = await tursoAvailable(); })` (lines 121-129), then `it('...', { skip: !hasTurso }, async () => {...})` at line 137-139. `heal-backend-agnostic.test.ts:60-150` has the identical shape: `let hasTurso = false` (line 61), `beforeAll(async () => { hasTurso = await tursoAvailable(); })` (lines 63-64+), `it('...', { skip: !hasTurso }, ...)` at line 148-150.

Vitest evaluates the `{ skip }` options object during the synchronous `describe()` collection pass, BEFORE any `beforeAll` hook executes. `hasTurso` is therefore read while still `false` (its `let` initializer); the test's skip decision is frozen at that instant and the value `beforeAll` later assigns is never consulted. Both tests' Turso-path `it(...)` blocks have therefore *always* statically skipped on every run to date, regardless of whether a Turso driver was actually available — this is not probabilistic flakiness, it is structurally guaranteed by how vitest resolves the options object.

**This is the exact bug the new `turso-clean-room.test.ts` was written to route around** — its header comment (lines 32-57, read directly) independently derives and documents the identical root cause and cites both files by name as the pre-existing instances, then resolves availability SYNCHRONOUSLY at module load instead (following the pattern `throughput-golden.spec.ts` already uses correctly).

**Audited the rest of the repo for the same anti-pattern** — confirmed CLEAN. `grep -rn '{ *skip: *!' --include='*.spec.ts' --include='*.test.ts' .` across the whole repo (excluding node_modules) returns only: the 2 buggy call sites above, `turso-clean-room.test.ts`'s own doc-comment quoting the bug (not live code), and 5 call sites in `throughput-golden.spec.ts` (`{skip: !_hasTurso}`) which are SAFE because `_hasTurso` there is resolved via a synchronous IIFE at module load (`const _hasTurso = (() => {...})()`), not an async `beforeAll`. Five other Turso-conditional suites in the repo (`turso-recall-listing.spec.ts`, `turso-concurrent-writes.test.ts`, `migration-e2e.test.ts`, `write-queue-turso-concurrency.spec.ts`) all correctly use the synchronous-IIFE-plus-`describe.skip`-toggle pattern (`const hasTurso = (() => {...})(); const tursoDescribe = hasTurso ? describe : describe.skip;`) — this bug is confined to exactly the 2 files named above, not repo-wide, but those 2 are precisely the two dedicated cross-backend Turso-parity regression tests, so the practical safety-net impact is severe: the two tests specifically designed to catch Turso-vs-SQLite behavioral divergence have never run their Turso assertion, on any CI run, ever.

**Fix pattern (already proven correct in this repo, just needs porting):** resolve `hasTurso` synchronously at module load via a driver-presence check (file-existence/`require.resolve` style, as `turso-clean-room.test.ts`/`throughput-golden.spec.ts`/`turso-recall-listing.spec.ts` all do), not inside an async `beforeAll` referenced by a `{skip}` object evaluated before that hook runs.

embed-pipeline.ts:22-28's BL-154 invariant reads as "Phase-B work must be serialized" and isn't — three agents independently misread it and one committed a revert of Turso's concurrency defaults

Verified directly by reading `libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:1-45` in full. The file's own header now contains a dated self-correction (lines 30-40, added 2026-07-30) that states the misread explicitly: "CLARIFICATION (2026-07-30 — three agents independently misread the paragraph above as 'Phase-B work must be serialized for correctness'; it does not say that and never did): BL-154 is about QUEUE RE-ENTRANCY ONLY... It says nothing about whether concurrent Phase-B PASSES... are safe to run at the same time against the store — that is a SEPARATE question, answered by the adapter's own concurrency contract (`AdapterCapabilities.needsWriteSerialization` / `concurrentTransactions`), not by this invariant."

The original BL-154 paragraph (lines 22-28) that caused the misread: "BL-154 INVARIANT (chunk-write deadlock class): never enqueue onto a serial WriteQueue from inside a task already running on that queue... Every scheduling entry point in this module MUST be called from OUTSIDE any queue task." Read in isolation, the word "serial" applied to "WriteQueue" without the later clarification reads naturally as a blanket serialization requirement for the whole subsystem, not a narrow re-entrancy rule about one call stack shape.

**Real cost, confirmed by git history, not just a hypothetical risk:** `git log --oneline -S"needsWriteSerialization" --all` shows: `0bde9f9 fix(store-adapter): serialize Turso writes — BL-321 active data loss` immediately followed by `06fcff7 Revert "fix(store-adapter): serialize Turso writes — BL-321 active data loss"`, then `15bc78f fix(store-adapter): mutex-only fix for Turso transaction contention — BL-321` (the eventual correct, narrower fix, confirmed by this session's earlier reading of `BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001`'s citations, which independently confirms `multiprocess_wal`/concurrent-transaction defaults are what the codebase now intentionally keeps). One agent actually committed a revert of Turso's `needsWriteSerialization: false` / `concurrentTransactions: true` defaults believing BL-154 required it, and had to have that commit reverted — a real, git-recorded round-trip of wasted work, not a narrowly-averted near-miss.

**There is also a stored memory note reinforcing the same misreading** (per team-lead's report to this agent — relayed, not independently located/verified by this agent; a follow-up should search `~/.memory` for a note describing WriteQueue/BL-154 as requiring serialization and correct or supersede it once the memory-server go-live referenced elsewhere in this triage round is unblocked, since this agent was instructed not to touch the live store).

**Fix sketch:** the 2026-07-30 CLARIFICATION paragraph already added to the file (lines 30-40) is a good fix for future readers of embed-pipeline.ts itself — verify it stays in place and is not accidentally reverted/dropped in a future edit. Additionally: (a) locate and correct/supersede the memory note reinforcing the wrong reading once store access is authorized, (b) consider renaming the invariant/comment heading from "BL-154 INVARIANT" alone to something like "BL-154 INVARIANT (re-entrancy only — NOT a serialization requirement, see CLARIFICATION below)" so the misleading half isn't the first thing a skimming reader sees before reaching the correction 8 lines later, (c) audit whether any other repo doc/comment (README, CLAUDE.md, other source comments) repeats the pre-clarification framing.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** this is a documentation-clarity defect, not a code defect, so the red→green bar is: (a) confirm via `git show HEAD:libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts` that the CLARIFICATION paragraph (or an equivalent, at-least-as-clear correction) is present and committed (green) vs. absent (red — the pre-2026-07-30 state, reconstructable via `git log -p` on this file before the clarification commit), and (b) a grep across `~/.memory` / repo docs for the phrase "WriteQueue"+"serial" that could still reinforce the wrong reading returns nothing once the follow-up in (a)/(b) above is done.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-DOC-BL154-MISREAD-SERIALIZATION, 1: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:1-45 (full header read directly — original BL-154 paragraph lines 22-28, self-correcting CLARIFICATION lines 30-40); 2: `git log --oneline -S"needsWriteSerialization" --all` and `git log --oneline -S"concurrentTransactions" --all` — both show 0bde9f9 (serialize Turso writes, BL-321) immediately followed by 06fcff7 (Revert of the same commit), then 15bc78f (mutex-only fix, BL-321) — run directly this session; 3: memory note reinforcing the misread — reported by team-lead, NOT independently located/verified by this agent]

content:
CONFIRMED root cause: Turso silently never executes trigger bodies at all — fts5 triggers referencing the missing `fts_node` table succeed as no-ops; latent risk if a future Turso version starts honoring them

**UPDATE 2026-07-30 (this agent, correcting its own earlier draft):** `fts-unify` independently reproduced this from scratch and found the actual mechanism, confirmed now committed directly in `libs/data/store/store-adapter/src/turso-adapter.ts:246-261` (read directly, verbatim doc comment on `TursoAdapterImpl.exec()`):

> "CAVEAT (verified independently by two agents, 2026-07-30): `DROP TABLE` and `DROP TRIGGER` issued through Turso against fts5 (and vec0) objects 'succeed' with no error, but the object REMAINS in `sqlite_master` — Turso silently no-ops the drop rather than honoring it... Relatedly: Turso also never invokes fts5 trigger bodies at all — INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on a triggering table succeed with stale fts5 triggers present, but the trigger body silently never runs. This happens to be harmless today only because nothing depends on those triggers firing; it would break instantly if a future Turso version starts executing them for real."

**This resolves my earlier candidate-1 theory ("the live server was running the in-flight capability-gated fix while the direct-INSERT repro used a different checkout") as WRONG.** The real mechanism is simpler and applies regardless of which db.ts revision is running: Turso's engine does not execute fts5 trigger bodies at all, full stop — so even where `FTS_TRIGGERS` IS installed (unconditionally, per committed HEAD, or accidentally left behind as residue), an `INSERT INTO node` against Turso never actually attempts the `INSERT INTO fts_node(...)` inside the trigger body, hence no error, regardless of whether `fts_node` exists. This is NOT specific to the capability gate landing or not — it is a property of the Turso engine's trigger execution (or non-execution) itself.

**Reframing per team-lead's instruction: this is a LATENT-RISK item, not an open investigation.** The mechanism is confirmed. What remains genuinely open:

1. **A real, unreconciled discrepancy between two independent repro attempts, recorded here rather than papered over:** team-lead's own repro against a copy of the ACTUAL LIVE FILE, using `.prepare()`-style execution, produced `prepare failed: no such table: fts_node`. `restore-db`, working against a SYNTHETIC pre-migration store using raw `exec()`/`run()`-style inserts, could NOT reproduce that failure — its inserts succeeded cleanly. Two agents, two different outcomes, neither confirmed wrong. Candidate explanations, none yet verified: (a) a `.prepare()`-vs-`.exec()`/`.run()` code path difference in how the Turso/libSQL driver validates or plans a statement before executing it (a `.prepare()` call might eagerly validate referenced tables/triggers in a way a fire-and-forget `.exec()` does not); (b) something specific to the real live file's schema/history (e.g. residue left by an earlier code path) that a fresh synthetic store doesn't reproduce; (c) a driver-version or connection-mode difference between the two repros not yet controlled for. This should be tracked and resolved, not assumed away.
2. **No regression test exists yet** asserting the confirmed behavior (trigger bodies never fire on Turso) so a future Turso upgrade that starts honoring triggers would be caught immediately rather than silently breaking every write.

**Mitigation already in place (cross-linked, not duplicated):** `libs/memory-core/src/db.ts` already works around BOTH silent-no-op classes directly: `dropVec0ViaBetterSqlite3()`/`dropFts5ResidueViaBetterSqlite3()` (commit `f350c83`, "fix(memory-core): BL-323 sqlite-vec default-export bug + Turso FTS index/residue") route all vec0/fts5-residue DROPs through better-sqlite3 instead of the Turso adapter, and db.ts:594-616 explicitly checks `sqlite_master` after any Turso-side DROP attempt rather than trusting the return value. This is the correct established pattern per the adapter's own doc comment ("route the drop through better-sqlite3 instead... see db.ts's VACUUM/vec0-drop compatibility repair for the established pattern").

**Why this stays open despite the mitigation existing:** the safety today is caller-side and manual (db.ts remembering to route through better-sqlite3 and re-verify via `sqlite_master`) — there is no test asserting this holds, and no guard against a FUTURE Turso engine version that starts actually executing DROP/trigger bodies for real, which per the adapter's own doc comment would "break instantly." The accidental-safety framing matters: nothing here was designed to be safe, it happens to be safe because Turso currently doesn't do what SQL says it should.

**Fix sketch (updated):** (a) resolve the `.prepare()`-vs-`.exec()` discrepancy between team-lead's and restore-db's repros — have one agent re-run both reproductions side-by-side against the SAME file with the SAME statement-execution method, to isolate which variable (file identity vs. execution method) actually explains the divergence; (b) add a regression test (see acceptance criteria) that pins today's no-op behavior so a future Turso version upgrade is caught the moment it changes; (c) the companion item (Turso silently no-ops DDL drops, filed separately this round) tracks the broader adapter-contract gap this belongs to.

content:
Embed-pipeline success counters (applies_applied, heals_applied, etc.) are lifetime monotonic counters with no gauge/current-state equivalent — comparing them to COUNT(*) sent multiple agents chasing phantom data loss for hours

This generalizes and gives a structural, code-verified basis to the confusion `BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001` describes as a consequence of duplicate overlapping ticks. This item's claim is broader and holds even WITHOUT duplicate ticks: any embed-pipeline counter recorded in `EmbedPipelineState` only ever increments, for the lifetime of the process, on every successful apply — it has no way to express 'current backlog size' or 'rows healed that are still healed' as a point-in-time fact, so ANY comparison of a cumulative counter against a live `COUNT(*)`-style query is comparing two fundamentally different kinds of quantity, independent of the stampede bug.

Verified directly: `libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:301-304` (`recordApplyOutcome`) and `:621,632-635` increment `applies_applied`/`heals_applied`/`embeds_completed` unconditionally on a successful outcome, held in an in-memory `Map` (`stateFor(wq.storePath)`, confirmed via `BUG-MEMORYSERVER-EMBED-HEAL-NOOPERATOR-001`'s citations of the same state object) — there is no decrement, no 'currently missing' complement tracked alongside it.

**Concretely, `healStaleVectors` (libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:789-860, read directly) makes the double-counting mechanism explicit and reproducible in code, even though it is currently DEFAULT-OFF and NOT wired into memory-server** (`staleHealEnabled()` gates on `SOX_HEAL_STALE_VECTORS=1`, default unset; comment at line 761: "NOT wired in memory-server" — confirmed by reading the full function). Its heal loop (lines 825-834+) explicitly `DELETE FROM vec_node WHERE node_id = ...` for a row that ALREADY HAS a vector, then re-embeds and re-inserts it via the same `applyEmbedding` path used by `healMissingVectors` — the code comment at line 829-830 states this outright: "Delete the stale vec_node row first so applyEmbedding sees no existing row and proceeds with the INSERT (vec0 tables have no UPDATE trigger — BL-91)". Since `applyEmbedding` sees no existing row after the DELETE, it reports `status:'applied'` (not `'exists'`) and increments `applies_applied`/`heals_applied` — for a row whose live vector-coverage state (does this episode have SOME vector right now) has not changed at all: it had one before the heal cycle and has one after. Every stale-heal pass over the same set of stale rows (e.g. if re-triggered, or if the same rows keep drifting stale) would keep incrementing a counter that never reflects a net change in coverage.

**Even without `healStaleVectors` ever being enabled, the identical structural risk applies to `healMissingVectors`** (the pipeline that IS wired in, per `BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001`): its `heals_applied` counter is a pure lifetime total of successful applies, with no corresponding 'current backlog size, net of this cycle's applies' field returned alongside it. An operator reading `memory_ping`'s `heals_applied:147` with no context has no way to tell whether that represents '147 out of a 200-row backlog, nearly done' or '147 lifetime applies against a backlog that has grown to 4241 and is still growing' — exactly the ambiguity that (per team-lead, relayed) caused multiple agents to spend hours chasing 'phantom data loss' by comparing a cumulative counter's plausible-looking non-zero value against a live row count that told a completely different story.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Add a gauge-style companion metric alongside every lifetime counter surfaced in `memory_ping`'s `embed_pipeline`/`enrichment` blocks: e.g. `embed_backlog` (already exists, per `BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP-001`'s citation of `index.ts:918`) should be explicitly documented/labeled as the gauge counterpart to `heals_applied`'s counter, and the response schema/docs should state outright "X_applied is a lifetime counter, reset only on process restart; it does NOT indicate current backlog size — use embed_backlog for that".
2. If/when `healStaleVectors` is ever wired in, give it its OWN counter namespace distinct from `heals_applied` (e.g. `stale_heals_applied`) so a re-embed-of-an-already-good-row is never conflated with net-new backlog drain in the same counter — or track a `net_vectors_added` gauge computed from before/after `COUNT(*)` on `vec_node`, not from apply-outcome tallies.
3. Add a one-line doc comment at each counter's declaration site (`EmbedPipelineState` interface, embed-pipeline.ts) stating explicitly: "lifetime, monotonic, resets on process restart, NOT comparable to a live row count."

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that (a) seeds a store with N rows missing vectors, runs one heal pass, asserts `heals_applied` increments by N (expected, today's behavior); (b) re-runs a heal pass over the SAME now-healed rows via `healStaleVectors` (with `SOX_HEAL_STALE_VECTORS=1`) or an equivalent re-heal trigger, and asserts TODAY `heals_applied`/`applies_applied` increments again by N even though `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vec_node` is unchanged (red — demonstrates the counter/gauge conflation); (c) after the fix (separate counter namespace or a documented+enforced gauge field), asserts an operator-facing field exists that correctly reports 'no net change in vector coverage occurred' for step (b) (green).

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-METRICS-LIFETIME-COUNTER-VS-GAUGE, 1: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:301-304,621,632-635 (recordApplyOutcome and heal counters, unconditional lifetime increment) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:756-865 (healStaleVectors full function — staleHealEnabled() default-off gate at 763-765, DELETE-then-reinsert at 825-834, comment explicitly describing the delete-to-force-reinsert mechanism) — read directly; 3: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:918-962 (memory_ping embed_pipeline/enrichment fields, no documented lifetime-vs-gauge distinction) — read directly (cross-referenced from BUG-MEMORYSERVER-EMBED-HEAL-NOOPERATOR-001's own citations); 4: BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001 (this repo, filed earlier this triage round) — documents the duplicate-tick-specific instance of the same counter/gauge conflation; this item generalizes the claim to hold independent of duplicate ticks; 5: 'multiple agents chasing phantom data loss for hours by comparing counters to COUNT(*)' — relayed by team-lead, not independently reproduced by this agent]

meta_parsed.title: Embed-pipeline success counters (applies_applied, heals_applied, etc.) are lifetime monotonic counters with no gauge/current-state equivalent — comparing them to COUNT(*) sent multiple agents chasing phantom data loss for hours
meta_parsed.body:
This generalizes and gives a structural, code-verified basis to the confusion `BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001` describes as a consequence of duplicate overlapping ticks. This item's claim is broader and holds even WITHOUT duplicate ticks: any embed-pipeline counter recorded in `EmbedPipelineState` only ever increments, for the lifetime of the process, on every successful apply — it has no way to express 'current backlog size' or 'rows healed that are still healed' as a point-in-time fact, so ANY comparison of a cumulative counter against a live `COUNT(*)`-style query is comparing two fundamentally different kinds of quantity, independent of the stampede bug.

Verified directly: `libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:301-304` (`recordApplyOutcome`) and `:621,632-635` increment `applies_applied`/`heals_applied`/`embeds_completed` unconditionally on a successful outcome, held in an in-memory `Map` (`stateFor(wq.storePath)`, confirmed via `BUG-MEMORYSERVER-EMBED-HEAL-NOOPERATOR-001`'s citations of the same state object) — there is no decrement, no 'currently missing' complement tracked alongside it.

**Concretely, `healStaleVectors` (libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:789-860, read directly) makes the double-counting mechanism explicit and reproducible in code, even though it is currently DEFAULT-OFF and NOT wired into memory-server** (`staleHealEnabled()` gates on `SOX_HEAL_STALE_VECTORS=1`, default unset; comment at line 761: "NOT wired in memory-server" — confirmed by reading the full function). Its heal loop (lines 825-834+) explicitly `DELETE FROM vec_node WHERE node_id = ...` for a row that ALREADY HAS a vector, then re-embeds and re-inserts it via the same `applyEmbedding` path used by `healMissingVectors` — the code comment at line 829-830 states this outright: "Delete the stale vec_node row first so applyEmbedding sees no existing row and proceeds with the INSERT (vec0 tables have no UPDATE trigger — BL-91)". Since `applyEmbedding` sees no existing row after the DELETE, it reports `status:'applied'` (not `'exists'`) and increments `applies_applied`/`heals_applied` — for a row whose live vector-coverage state (does this episode have SOME vector right now) has not changed at all: it had one before the heal cycle and has one after. Every stale-heal pass over the same set of stale rows (e.g. if re-triggered, or if the same rows keep drifting stale) would keep incrementing a counter that never reflects a net change in coverage.

**Even without `healStaleVectors` ever being enabled, the identical structural risk applies to `healMissingVectors`** (the pipeline that IS wired in, per `BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001`): its `heals_applied` counter is a pure lifetime total of successful applies, with no corresponding 'current backlog size, net of this cycle's applies' field returned alongside it. An operator reading `memory_ping`'s `heals_applied:147` with no context has no way to tell whether that represents '147 out of a 200-row backlog, nearly done' or '147 lifetime applies against a backlog that has grown to 4241 and is still growing' — exactly the ambiguity that (per team-lead, relayed) caused multiple agents to spend hours chasing 'phantom data loss' by comparing a cumulative counter's plausible-looking non-zero value against a live row count that told a completely different story.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Add a gauge-style companion metric alongside every lifetime counter surfaced in `memory_ping`'s `embed_pipeline`/`enrichment` blocks: e.g. `embed_backlog` (already exists, per `BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP-001`'s citation of `index.ts:918`) should be explicitly documented/labeled as the gauge counterpart to `heals_applied`'s counter, and the response schema/docs should state outright "X_applied is a lifetime counter, reset only on process restart; it does NOT indicate current backlog size — use embed_backlog for that".
2. If/when `healStaleVectors` is ever wired in, give it its OWN counter namespace distinct from `heals_applied` (e.g. `stale_heals_applied`) so a re-embed-of-an-already-good-row is never conflated with net-new backlog drain in the same counter — or track a `net_vectors_added` gauge computed from before/after `COUNT(*)` on `vec_node`, not from apply-outcome tallies.
3. Add a one-line doc comment at each counter's declaration site (`EmbedPipelineState` interface, embed-pipeline.ts) stating explicitly: "lifetime, monotonic, resets on process restart, NOT comparable to a live row count."

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that (a) seeds a store with N rows missing vectors, runs one heal pass, asserts `heals_applied` increments by N (expected, today's behavior); (b) re-runs a heal pass over the SAME now-healed rows via `healStaleVectors` (with `SOX_HEAL_STALE_VECTORS=1`) or an equivalent re-heal trigger, and asserts TODAY `heals_applied`/`applies_applied` increments again by N even though `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vec_node` is unchanged (red — demonstrates the counter/gauge conflation); (c) after the fix (separate counter namespace or a documented+enforced gauge field), asserts an operator-facing field exists that correctly reports 'no net change in vector coverage occurred' for step (b) (green).

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-METRICS-LIFETIME-COUNTER-VS-GAUGE, 1: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:301-304,621,632-635 (recordApplyOutcome and heal counters, unconditional lifetime increment) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:756-865 (healStaleVectors full function — staleHealEnabled() default-off gate at 763-765, DELETE-then-reinsert at 825-834, comment explicitly describing the delete-to-force-reinsert mechanism) — read directly; 3: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:918-962 (memory_ping embed_pipeline/enrichment fields, no documented lifetime-vs-gauge distinction) — read directly (cross-referenced from BUG-MEMORYSERVER-EMBED-HEAL-NOOPERATOR-001's own citations); 4: BUG-EMBED-ENRICH-TICK-STAMPEDE-001 (this repo, filed earlier this triage round) — documents the duplicate-tick-specific instance of the same counter/gauge conflation; this item generalizes the claim to hold independent of duplicate ticks; 5: 'multiple agents chasing phantom data loss for hours by comparing counters to COUNT(*)' — relayed by team-lead, not independently reproduced by this agent]

content:
`cp` of a live Turso/WAL-mode SQLite store does not capture recent writes — every forensic row count taken from a plain-cp snapshot during today's incident is a lagging read

Filed on the store owner's authorization to record a process/tooling gap surfaced during the live incident. **The empirical proof is relayed from team-lead's own report, not independently reproduced by this agent** (reproducing it would mean writing a probe row to the live store and taking a live cp snapshot, both outside this agent's scope — investigation/filing only, no store mutation): team-lead reports writing a probe that moved `total_episodes` 4410→4411 live, then copying `memory.db` WITH its `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar files (`cp memory.db memory.db-wal memory.db-shm <dest>` or equivalent, exact invocation not captured in the relay) and finding the COPY still showed the pre-probe state (4410), i.e. the copy did not observe the write that had already committed against the live file.

**Why this is plausible and not surprising, verified independently by reasoning about WAL mechanics (general SQLite knowledge, not a claim requiring a citation into this repo's source):** in WAL mode, a plain filesystem `cp` of the main db file plus its `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars is not guaranteed to be transactionally consistent unless the copy is taken while no writer holds the WAL, or via a mechanism that establishes a read transaction across all three files atomically (e.g. `sqlite3 .backup`, `VACUUM INTO`, or holding a shared lock during the copy). A `cp` invoked while the source is open for writes can read the main file and WAL/SHM at different instants relative to a concurrent checkpoint or write-transaction commit, producing a copy that is neither the pre-write nor fully the post-write state — exactly the 'copy still showed the pre-probe state' symptom reported.

**Real cost this session:** per the mission brief for this triage round, "every forensic row count taken from a cp snapshot today is therefore a lagging read" — several forensic comparisons this incident (backup-vs-live diffs, missing-node counts) may have been performed against `cp`-based snapshots whose freshness relative to the live store was not verified, meaning some of today's own forensic conclusions (including ones already filed as backlog items, e.g. `BUG-MEMORY-DATALOSS-716-NODES-001`'s and `BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP-001`'s db-repair-agent forensics) may themselves rest on stale snapshots — not because the analysis was wrong, but because the ground truth it compared against may have moved. This item does not itself invalidate those findings (this agent has no evidence either way and was instructed not to touch the store to check) — it exists so a review pass can happen with the correct snapshot method once store access is authorized.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Document (in this repo's incident/runbook docs, or a CONTRIBUTING.md section) the CORRECT way to take a consistent point-in-time snapshot of a live `~/.memory/*.db` store: prefer the existing `backupStore()` utility (`libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts`, which per `BUG-STOREADAPTER-MIGRATE-UNSAFE-001`'s citation already uses `VACUUM INTO` + `PRAGMA integrity_check`) over a raw `cp`, OR use `sqlite3 <db> ".backup <dest>"` / a WAL checkpoint (`PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) immediately before any `cp`-based snapshot if `backupStore()` isn't invokable in context.
2. Add a lightweight verification step to any future forensic snapshot: compare a cheap, monotonic marker (e.g. `SELECT MAX(rowid) FROM node` or a dedicated heartbeat counter) between the live store and the snapshot immediately after copying, and warn/abort if they diverge in a way inconsistent with the elapsed time.
3. Retroactively flag which specific forensic counts taken today used a raw `cp` (vs. `backupStore()`/`.backup`) so `BUG-MEMORY-DATALOSS-716-NODES-001` and `BUG-VECTOR-COVERAGE-COLLAPSE-PRE-SWAP-001` can be re-verified against a freshly, correctly taken snapshot before their restore work is considered final.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test/script that (a) opens a WAL-mode SQLite store, starts a write transaction that is held open (or writes then immediately re-writes without a checkpoint), takes a raw `cp`-based snapshot mid-sequence, and asserts today's behavior can produce a snapshot missing the latest committed write (red, reproducing the reported symptom mechanically rather than relying solely on the relayed incident); (b) repeats the same sequence using the recommended snapshot method (`backupStore()`/`.backup`/checkpoint-then-copy) and asserts the snapshot always reflects the latest committed write at the instant the backup call returns (green).

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-PROCESS-CP-SNAPSHOT-STALE-WAL, 1: team-lead's report — wrote a probe moving total_episodes 4410→4411 live, cp'd memory.db+sidecars, copy still showed 4410 — relayed, NOT independently reproduced by this agent (no store mutation performed); 2: libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts (backupStore() utility using VACUUM INTO + PRAGMA integrity_check) — cross-referenced from BUG-STOREADAPTER-MIGRATE-UNSAFE-001's own citations, read directly in this triage round as evidence a correct snapshot mechanism already exists in-repo but was apparently not used for today's forensic cp; 3: general SQLite WAL-mode consistency semantics (plain filesystem cp of main+wal+shm files is not guaranteed atomic relative to a live writer) — general domain knowledge, not a repo-specific citation]

Seven agents on one working tree caused four incidents today (work absorbed into others' commits, files reverted mid-edit, muddled attribution) — recommend mandatory worktrees for parallel dispatch during incident response

backup.ts/index.ts carry a complete, unrelated feature (BL-313 pre-restart auto-backup + BL-55 scope db path) sitting uncommitted and tangled with today's incident fixes — should be committed separately

Verified directly. `git diff --stat HEAD -- libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts libs/memory-core/src/index.ts extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts libs/memory-core/src/backup.spec.ts` shows: `backup.ts` +131 lines (new, read directly: exports `AutoBackupResult`/`autoBackup()` — a pre-restart auto-backup feature with env-controlled enable/disable, mtime-based idempotency marker, and an explicit doc-comment header "Pre-restart auto-backup: create a timestamped VACUUM INTO backup of the memory database when the process is about to restart or shut down"), `backup.spec.ts` +201 lines (new test coverage for the same feature), `libs/memory-core/src/index.ts` +3/-1 (re-export wiring), and `extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts` +81/-3 lines including (grep-confirmed, read directly) a `BL-55` scope-based db-path resolution block (`db_path` resolution chain comments at lines 777-1031) and a `BL-313` pre-restart auto-backup wiring block at lines 2255-2272 (`process.on(signal, ...)` handler invoking `autoBackup(dbPathForBackup)` before shutdown).

This is a complete, independently-testable feature (its own 201-line spec file exists and, per this feature's own doc comments, addresses two DIFFERENT backlog items — BL-313 and BL-55 — neither of which is the Turso/db.ts incident this triage round is about) sitting in the SAME uncommitted working tree as the incident-recovery work (db.ts's Turso wiring restore, per `BUG-DB-TURSO-WIRING-UNCOMMITTED-001`) and this round's own new test files. If the incident-recovery work is committed as a single commit that also happens to sweep in `backup.ts`/`index.ts`'s unrelated feature (or vice versa), the commit history loses the ability to distinguish 'this commit fixed the live incident' from 'this commit also happened to ship an unrelated auto-backup feature' — complicating any future `git bisect`, revert, or audit of either change independently.

**Fix sketch:** commit the BL-313/BL-55 auto-backup feature (`backup.ts`, `backup.spec.ts`, the re-export in `index.ts`, and the `BL-55`/`BL-313` wiring blocks in `extensions/.../memory-server/src/index.ts`) as its OWN commit, separate from and either before or after (not interleaved with) whatever commit(s) land the Turso incident-recovery fixes (BUG-DB-TURSO-WIRING-UNCOMMITTED-001, BUG-DB-OPENDB-MISSING-FTS-VEC-DDL-001, etc.). Use `git add <specific files>` (never `-A`/`.`/`-a`, per this repo's explicit-path-staging policy) to keep the two efforts' diffs cleanly separated at commit time, even though they currently sit in the same working tree.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** red — today, `git log --oneline -1` for the tip of `wip/turso-live-metrics` shows no commit containing ONLY the BL-313/BL-55 auto-backup diff (it doesn't exist as a commit at all yet, uncommitted). Green — after this item's fix, `git show --stat <the-auto-backup-commit>` contains exactly `backup.ts`, `backup.spec.ts`, the `index.ts` re-export, and the memory-server wiring block, with ZERO files touched by the separate Turso-incident commit(s), verifiable via `git diff <auto-backup-commit> <turso-incident-commit> --name-only` showing no overlap.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-UNCOMMITTED-BACKUP-FEATURE-TANGLED-WITH-INCIDENT, 1: `git diff --stat HEAD -- libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts libs/memory-core/src/index.ts extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts libs/memory-core/src/backup.spec.ts` — run directly this round, shows backup.ts +131, backup.spec.ts +201 (new file), index.ts +3/-1, memory-server/src/index.ts +81/-3; 2: libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts (diff content, read directly) — AutoBackupResult/autoBackup() new export, pre-restart auto-backup feature; 3: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:777-1031 (BL-55 scope/db_path resolution comments), :2255-2272 (BL-313 pre-restart auto-backup wiring, process.on(signal,...) handler calling autoBackup()) — grep+read directly this round]
