TursoAdapter's `exec()` contract implies DDL is honored, but for DROP TABLE/TRIGGER on fts5 and vec0 objects it silently no-ops — no post-drop verification helper exists at the adapter layer, only ad hoc caller-side workarounds in db.ts

Confirmed via `fts-unify`'s from-scratch reproduction (relayed by team-lead) and independently verified by this agent reading the now-committed documentation of the finding: `libs/data/store/store-adapter/src/turso-adapter.ts:246-261` (read directly, doc comment on `TursoAdapterImpl.exec()`):

> "CAVEAT (verified independently by two agents, 2026-07-30): `DROP TABLE` and `DROP TRIGGER` issued through Turso against fts5 (and vec0) objects 'succeed' with no error, but the object REMAINS in `sqlite_master` — Turso silently no-ops the drop rather than honoring it."

**The problem this item tracks (distinct from `INVESTIGATION-FTS-TRIGGER-TURSO-UNRESOLVED-001`, which covers the trigger-non-execution half of the same underlying Turso limitation):** the `StoreAdapter` interface's `exec(sql): Promise<void>` contract, by any reasonable reading, implies that DDL passed to it is applied — a caller has no way to know, from the interface alone, that some DDL statement kinds silently do nothing on this particular adapter implementation. The ONLY place this is currently guarded against is inside `libs/memory-core/src/db.ts` (`dropVec0ViaBetterSqlite3()`, `dropFts5ResidueViaBetterSqlite3()`, and the explicit `sqlite_master` re-check after any Turso-side DROP at db.ts:594-616) — a caller-side, hand-maintained special case in ONE consumer of the adapter, not a property enforced or even flagged by the adapter itself beyond the doc comment. Any OTHER caller of `TursoAdapterImpl.exec()` anywhere in this codebase or a future downstream consumer (per `libs/data/CLAUDE.md`'s own package listing, `graph-store`/`vector-store`/`hybrid-search` are all PUBLIC, independently consumable packages) that issues a `DROP TABLE`/`DROP TRIGGER` against an fts5 or vec0 object and assumes it succeeded (because `exec()` resolved without throwing) will be silently wrong, with no test or runtime assertion catching it.

**Dedup check performed:** searched existing tool-side items for 'vec0'/'DROP'/'residue'/'silent' — `BUG-DB-OPENDB-MISSING-FTS-VEC-DDL-001` covers DDL CREATION being missing (openDb never creating fts_node/vec_node), which is the inverse problem (missing CREATE, not a no-op DROP) and does not mention DROP semantics at all. No existing item covers the DROP-no-op contract gap itself — filing as new, cross-linked to both `BUG-DB-OPENDB-MISSING-FTS-VEC-DDL-001` and `INVESTIGATION-FTS-TRIGGER-TURSO-UNRESOLVED-001`.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Add a reusable, adapter-level (not caller-side) verification helper — e.g. `StoreAdapter.dropTableVerified(name)` or a `verifyDropped(objectName)` utility in `store-adapter` itself — that issues the DROP and then checks `sqlite_master` for the object's absence, throwing a clear `E_DROP_NOOP`-style error if the Turso engine silently no-op'd it. This turns today's silent lie into a loud, catchable failure for ANY caller, not just db.ts's hand-rolled path.
2. Extend `TursoAdapterImpl`'s own `exec()` (or a stricter sibling method) to optionally self-verify DDL of known-affected kinds (DROP TABLE/TRIGGER referencing fts5/vec0 objects) before returning success — or, at minimum, export the `sqlite_master`-verification helper from `store-adapter` so `db.ts`'s current inline logic can be replaced by a shared, tested utility rather than duplicated ad hoc wherever the next caller needs it.
3. Add the same caveat to `StoreAdapter`'s own top-level interface doc (not just the Turso implementation's `exec()` override), since a caller reading only the interface today would never discover this limitation exists.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that (a) opens a Turso-backed store with a vec0 (or fts5) residue table present, calls the adapter's plain `exec('DROP TABLE ...')`, and asserts TODAY the object still exists in `sqlite_master` afterward with no error thrown (red — demonstrates the silent no-op, the current de-facto contract violation); (b) after the fix, calls the new verified-drop helper against the same setup and asserts it either successfully removes the object (by routing through better-sqlite3 as db.ts already does) or throws a clear, typed error identifying the no-op rather than silently returning success (green).

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, BUG-TURSO-ADAPTER-EXEC-DDL-SILENT-NOOP, 1: libs/data/store/store-adapter/src/turso-adapter.ts:246-261 (TursoAdapterImpl.exec() doc comment, committed) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/db.ts:338-341,594-616 (only existing mitigation, caller-side/hand-rolled in one consumer) — read directly; 3: libs/data/CLAUDE.md (package listing — graph-store/vector-store/hybrid-search are PUBLIC, independently consumable packages that could call TursoAdapterImpl.exec() without db.ts's special-casing) — read directly; 4: BUG-DB-OPENDB-MISSING-FTS-VEC-DDL-001 (this repo, filed earlier this triage round) — confirmed via re-read to cover DDL CREATION gaps only, not DROP no-op semantics — cross-linked, not a duplicate; 5: INVESTIGATION-FTS-TRIGGER-TURSO-UNRESOLVED-001 (this repo, this triage round, updated) — covers the sibling trigger-non-execution half of the same Turso limitation — cross-linked companion item]

Repo-wide bare-catch{} audit across memory-core/data/memory-server write, apply, and migration paths — 88 candidate sites triaged; 4 in extensions.ts ranked HIGH (silent vec_node/edge insert failures inside functions that still report success/imported counts)

Fan-out audit requested by team-lead after the original incident-causing bare catch (`applyEmbedding`, already fixed 2026-07-30 — confirmed via comment at `embed-pipeline.ts:456`) hid 5 weeks of silent vector-write failures because the catch sat AFTER a committed INSERT and the enclosing function still returned `status:'applied'`. This item hunts for the same signature elsewhere: **a bare/near-empty catch positioned after a state mutation, where the enclosing function still reports success.**

**Method:** wrote a brace-matching scanner (not just a literal-`catch{}` grep, since most real instances are `catch { /* comment */ }` or `catch { log.debug(...) }` multi-line) over every non-spec `.ts` file under `libs/memory-core/src`, `libs/data/**`, and `extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src`. Flagged any catch body that is empty, comment-only, or log-only with no `throw`/rejection. 88 candidate sites across 26 files. Each was individually read in context (not just the scanner's snippet) to classify severity. Full raw scan output available on request; only the ranked, read-verified findings are reported below — sites confirmed as false positives (log-then-rethrow/reject, which my regex's naive `throw`-keyword check missed) are excluded from the ranking, not omitted silently: `write-queue.ts:533,814` both flagged by the scanner but READ and confirmed to correctly `return Promise.reject(err)` / `item.reject(wrapped)` after logging — these propagate the error to the caller and are NOT bugs.

---

## RANKED FINDINGS (highest severity first)

### HIGH — silent per-row vec_node/edge insert failures during import/copy, success still reported

**`libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts`, inside `graphifyImport()` (function spans ~509-741) and `buildCommunities()` (~741-905):**

1. **`extensions.ts:649`** (read directly, in `graphifyImport`'s dst-node copy path): 
```
try {
  await dstAdapter.executeRun('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vec_node(node_id, embedding) VALUES (...)', [...]);
} catch {
  /* non-fatal */
}
```
A failed vec_node insert here is swallowed with no counter, no log, nothing. The copied node proceeds without ANY vector, and nothing downstream is told.

2. **`extensions.ts:687`** (read directly, in `graphifyImport`'s main import loop): identical `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vec_node(...)` wrapped in `catch { /* non-fatal */ }`, immediately followed by `uidMap.set(origId, uid); importedNodes++;` — **the increment and the vec_node insert are NOT coupled**: `importedNodes` increments unconditionally whether or not the vector actually landed. The function's final return, `{ ok: true, imported: importedNodes, edges_imported: importedEdges, shape: shapeName }` (confirmed by reading the function's return statement), therefore reports `ok:true, imported:N` even when some fraction of those N nodes have silently missing vectors — this is the EXACT shape of the incident bug: state successfully mutated (node row imported), embedding step failed, failure swallowed, caller told success.

3. **`extensions.ts:1048`** (read directly, edge-insert loop later in `graphifyImport`): `importedEdges++` sits INSIDE the `try`, so a failed edge insert does not inflate the count (better than #2) — but the caller still gets no signal that N edges were silently dropped; `edges_imported` undercounts with no way to distinguish "nothing to import" from "some imports failed."

4. **`extensions.ts:870`** (read directly, `buildCommunities`'s MEMBER_OF edge-insert loop): same shape as #3 — `memberCount++` inside `try`, catch is `/* skip */` with no aggregate failure count returned to the caller.

**Why HIGH, not CRITICAL:** unlike the original `applyEmbedding` bug, these don't lie about a SPECIFIC row's status (there's no per-row status object here to falsify) — they lie about (#2) or are silent about (#3, #4) the AGGREGATE result of a bulk operation. Still severe: an operator re-importing/copying a graph subset via `graphifyImport` has no way to know their `imported: 40` response might mean "40 nodes copied, some subset silently missing vectors" versus the intended "40 nodes copied and fully embedded."

### MEDIUM — already-mitigated / self-aware, flagging for completeness

5. **`libs/data/queue/task-queue/src/worker-pool.ts:149-158`**: when `handler(task)` throws, `queue.fail(task.id, message)` is called to mark it; if THAT call also throws, the catch is `console.warn(...'task is now in an inconsistent state and must be reconciled manually'...)` with no further recovery — already self-documents the risk in its own message, but there is no automated reconciliation path, only a warn-and-abandon. Worth a follow-up (out of this item's scope) to add an automatic reconciliation sweep rather than relying on a human reading stderr.

6. **`libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:456`** — the ORIGINAL incident site, confirmed ALREADY FIXED (comment at that line states so directly); included here only so the audit inventory is visibly complete, not as an open finding.

### LOW — read-path / diagnostic / setup-time fallbacks, correctly scoped as best-effort

Read and confirmed benign — either (a) a read/diagnostic path where a stale or missing value is an acceptable degraded result, not a correctness violation, or (b) an already-documented, intentional Turso/SQLite dialect-difference workaround with a loud path for genuine failures:

- `libs/memory-core/src/db.ts` (13 sites, all inside `openDb()`'s DDL/migration setup): every one read in context — all are either explicit "Turso rejects IF NOT EXISTS"/"table already exists" benign-error string-matches (e.g. `db.ts:596` correctly distinguishes benign-vs-loud by testing the error message and `log.error`s anything that ISN'T the known-benign case — this is the CORRECT pattern, not a bug) or one-time QoL migrations explicitly commented `// Non-fatal`.
- `libs/memory-core/src/lease.ts` (10 sites) — all lock-file/adapter-cleanup "best effort" catches during lease release/renewal teardown, not data-mutation paths.
- `libs/memory-core/src/recall.ts` (7 sites) — all read-path (FTS query malformed-input tolerance, embed-timeout-in-recall which explicitly sets `embedVecFailed=true` rather than silently proceeding, permission-error tolerance on optional lookups).
- `libs/memory-core/src/telemetry.ts` (5 sites) — explicitly documented: "Logging must NEVER break or slow the caller—swallow anything." Correct by design for a logging subsystem.
- `libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts` (7 sites), `extensions.ts:331` (memory_scope.meta backward-compat), `cluster.ts` (2), `curate.ts`, `update.ts`, `export.ts`, `provenance.ts`, `autolink.ts:65` — all malformed-JSON/legacy-schema tolerance on READ, not silent write-failure.
- `extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts` (8 sites) — all `memory_ping` diagnostic-metadata best-effort reads (file fingerprint, WAL size, host-compat manifest, community meta parse) with sane fallback defaults; none is on a write path.
- `libs/data/store/blob-store/src/store.ts` (5 sites) — lower priority: this package is itself flagged **orphaned, zero live consumers** per `libs/data/store/blob-store/CLAUDE.md` (BL-166) — not worth prioritizing catch-hardening in unused code; `count()`'s `catch { /* ignore — return 0 */ }` is the closest to concerning but only affects an advisory count, not blob durability itself.
- `libs/data/store/store-adapter/src/{sqlite,turso}-adapter.ts` (2+2 sites) — rollback-error and non-fatal-stamp tolerance, correctly scoped.
- `libs/data/verify/claim-verification/src/{index,prefilter}.ts` (2 sites) — intentional fallback-to-NLI design, logged.
- `libs/data/vectors/vector-store/src/lancedb-worker.ts:246` — documented as an expected-transient training failure on small/skewed tables, self-heals on next upsert.
- `libs/data/embed/embedding-provider/src/embedWorker.ts:416`, `libs/memory-core/src/write-queue.ts:342` — both are "already closed"/idempotent-teardown tolerance, not data-loss risk.

**No silent catches found on the memory_write/memory_recall Phase-A hot path itself, in `write.ts`, or in `WriteQueue`'s main dequeue loop** (`write-queue.ts:814`, the one candidate there, correctly propagates via `item.reject(wrapped)` — confirmed a scanner false positive, not a defect).

---

**Fix sketch (scoped to the HIGH findings only — #1/#2 in `graphifyImport`, #3/#4 aggregate-undercounting):**
1. `graphifyImport`: track a `vecNodeInsertFailures` counter alongside `importedNodes`, increment it in the catch blocks at lines 649 and 687, and surface it in the function's return value (`{ ok: true, imported, edges_imported, shape, vec_insert_failures: N }`) so a caller can tell full success from partial-vector-loss success.
2. `graphifyImport`/`buildCommunities`'s edge-insert catches (lines 1048, 870): similarly track and surface a `skipped_edges`/`skipped_members` count rather than silently discarding the information the catch already has.
3. Do NOT change these to rethrow/abort the whole import on one bad row — per-row tolerance during a bulk import is a reasonable design; the defect is the SILENCE, not the tolerance.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that calls `graphifyImport()` against a fixture where one node's vec_node insert is forced to fail (e.g. a malformed embedding value or a locked table), and asserts (a) TODAY the function's return value shows `ok:true, imported:N` with no indication anything failed (red — demonstrates the silent aggregate lie); (b) after the fix, the return value surfaces a non-zero failure/skip count for the affected row (green). A second test does the same for `buildCommunities`'s MEMBER_OF edge insert.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-SILENT-CATCH-AUDIT-WRITE-APPLY-PATHS, 1: libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts:640-654 (graphifyImport dst-node vec_node insert, catch{/* non-fatal */}) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts:680-696 (graphifyImport main-loop vec_node insert, catch{/* non-fatal */}, immediately followed by unconditional importedNodes++) — read directly; 3: libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts:509,730-741 (graphifyImport function bounds and final return statement {ok:true, imported, edges_imported, shape}) — read directly; 4: libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts:1040-1051 (graphifyImport edge-insert loop, importedEdges++ correctly inside try, catch{/* skip */} with no failure count surfaced) — read directly; 5: libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts:860-875 (buildCommunities MEMBER_OF edge insert, memberCount++ inside try, catch{/* skip */}) — read directly; 6: libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:456 (original incident site, comment confirms already fixed 2026-07-30) — read directly; 7: libs/data/queue/task-queue/src/worker-pool.ts:144-159 (fail()-call-itself-fails warn-and-abandon path) — read directly; 8: libs/memory-core/src/write-queue.ts:495-541,780-824 (both scanner-flagged sites read in full — confirmed correct error propagation via Promise.reject/item.reject, NOT silent swallows, false positives excluded from ranking) — read directly; 9: libs/data/store/blob-store/CLAUDE.md (package flagged orphaned/zero-consumers, BL-166) — read directly, informs LOW priority for store.ts findings; 10: full scanner methodology — custom brace-matching Node script run directly this session over 26 files, 88 candidate catch sites, each individually read in context before classification (not scanner-output-only)]

meta_parsed.title: Repo-wide bare-catch{} audit across memory-core/data/memory-server write, apply, and migration paths — 88 candidate sites triaged; 4 in extensions.ts ranked HIGH (silent vec_node/edge insert failures inside functions that still report success/imported counts)
meta_parsed.body:
Fan-out audit requested by team-lead after the original incident-causing bare catch (`applyEmbedding`, already fixed 2026-07-30 — confirmed via comment at `embed-pipeline.ts:456`) hid 5 weeks of silent vector-write failures because the catch sat AFTER a committed INSERT and the enclosing function still returned `status:'applied'`. This item hunts for the same signature elsewhere: **a bare/near-empty catch positioned after a state mutation, where the enclosing function still reports success.**

**Method:** wrote a brace-matching scanner (not just a literal-`catch{}` grep, since most real instances are `catch { /* comment */ }` or `catch { log.debug(...) }` multi-line) over every non-spec `.ts` file under `libs/memory-core/src`, `libs/data/**`, and `extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src`. Flagged any catch body that is empty, comment-only, or log-only with no `throw`/rejection. 88 candidate sites across 26 files. Each was individually read in context (not just the scanner's snippet) to classify severity. Full raw scan output available on request; only the ranked, read-verified findings are reported below — sites confirmed as false positives (log-then-rethrow/reject, which my regex's naive `throw`-keyword check missed) are excluded from the ranking, not omitted silently: `write-queue.ts:533,814` both flagged by the scanner but READ and confirmed to correctly `return Promise.reject(err)` / `item.reject(wrapped)` after logging — these propagate the error to the caller and are NOT bugs.

---

## RANKED FINDINGS (highest severity first)

### HIGH — silent per-row vec_node/edge insert failures during import/copy, success still reported

**`libs/memory-core/src/extensions.ts`, inside `graphifyImport()` (function spans ~509-741) and `buildCommunities()` (~741-905):**

1. **`extensions.ts:649`** (read directly, in `graphifyImport`'s dst-node copy path): 
```
try {
  await dstAdapter.executeRun('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vec_node(node_id, embedding) VALUES (...)', [...]);
} catch {
  /* non-fatal */
}
```
A failed vec_node insert here is swallowed with no counter, no log, nothing. The copied node proceeds without ANY vector, and nothing downstream is told.

2. **`extensions.ts:687`** (read directly, in `graphifyImport`'s main import loop): identical `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO vec_node(...)` wrapped in `catch { /* non-fatal */ }`, immediately followed by `uidMap.set(origId, uid); importedNodes++;` — **the increment and the vec_node insert are NOT coupled**: `importedNodes` increments unconditionally whether or not the vector actually landed. The function's final return, `{ ok: true, imported: importedNodes, edges_imported: importedEdges, shape: shapeName }` (confirmed by reading the function's return statement), therefore reports `ok:true, imported:N` even when some fraction of those N nodes have silently missing vectors — this is the EXACT shape of the incident bug: state successfully mutated (node row imported), embedding step failed, failure swallowed, caller told success.

3. **`extensions.ts:1048`** (read directly, edge-insert loop later in `graphifyImport`): `importedEdges++` sits INSIDE the `try`, so a failed edge insert does not inflate the count (better than #2) — but the caller still gets no signal that N edges were silently dropped; `edges_imported` undercounts with no way to distinguish "nothing to import" from "some imports failed."

4. **`extensions.ts:870`** (read directly, `buildCommunities`'s MEMBER_OF edge-insert loop): same shape as #3 — `memberCount++` inside `try`, catch is `/* skip */` with no aggregate failure count returned to the caller.

**Why HIGH, not CRITICAL:** unlike the original `applyEmbedding` bug, these don't lie about a SPECIFIC row's status (there's no per-row status object here to falsify) — they lie about (#2) or are silent about (#3, #4) the AGGREGATE result of a bulk operation. Still severe: an operator re-importing/copying a graph subset via `graphifyImport` has no way to know their `imported: 40` response might mean "40 nodes copied, some subset silently missing vectors" versus the intended "40 nodes copied and fully embedded."

### MEDIUM — already-mitigated / self-aware, flagging for completeness

5. **`libs/data/queue/task-queue/src/worker-pool.ts:149-158`**: when `handler(task)` throws, `queue.fail(task.id, message)` is called to mark it; if THAT call also throws, the catch is `console.warn(...'task is now in an inconsistent state and must be reconciled manually'...)` with no further recovery — already self-documents the risk in its own message, but there is no automated reconciliation path, only a warn-and-abandon. Worth a follow-up (out of this item's scope) to add an automatic reconciliation sweep rather than relying on a human reading stderr.

6. **`libs/memory-core/src/embed-pipeline.ts:456`** — the ORIGINAL incident site, confirmed ALREADY FIXED (comment at that line states so directly); included here only so the audit inventory is visibly complete, not as an open finding.

### LOW — read-path / diagnostic / setup-time fallbacks, correctly scoped as best-effort

Read and confirmed benign — either (a) a read/diagnostic path where a stale or missing value is an acceptable degraded result, not a correctness violation, or (b) an already-documented, intentional Turso/SQLite dialect-difference workaround with a loud path for genuine failures:

- `libs/memory-core/src/db.ts` (13 sites, all inside `openDb()`'s DDL/migration setup): every one read in context — all are either explicit "Turso rejects IF NOT EXISTS"/"table already exists" benign-error string-matches (e.g. `db.ts:596` correctly distinguishes benign-vs-loud by testing the error message and `log.error`s anything that ISN'T the known-benign case — this is the CORRECT pattern, not a bug) or one-time QoL migrations explicitly commented `// Non-fatal`.
- `libs/memory-core/src/lease.ts` (10 sites) — all lock-file/adapter-cleanup "best effort" catches during lease release/renewal teardown, not data-mutation paths.
- `libs/memory-core/src/recall.ts` (7 sites) — all read-path (FTS query malformed-input tolerance, embed-timeout-in-recall which explicitly sets `embedVecFailed=true` rather than silently proceeding, permission-error tolerance on optional lookups).
- `libs/memory-core/src/telemetry.ts` (5 sites) — explicitly documented: "Logging must NEVER break or slow the caller—swallow anything." Correct by design for a logging subsystem.
- `libs/memory-core/src/backup.ts` (7 sites), `extensions.ts:331` (memory_scope.meta backward-compat), `cluster.ts` (2), `curate.ts`, `update.ts`, `export.ts`, `provenance.ts`, `autolink.ts:65` — all malformed-JSON/legacy-schema tolerance on READ, not silent write-failure.
- `extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts` (8 sites) — all `memory_ping` diagnostic-metadata best-effort reads (file fingerprint, WAL size, host-compat manifest, community meta parse) with sane fallback defaults; none is on a write path.
- `libs/data/store/blob-store/src/store.ts` (5 sites) — lower priority: this package is itself flagged **orphaned, zero live consumers** per `libs/data/store/blob-store/CLAUDE.md` (BL-166) — not worth prioritizing catch-hardening in unused code; `count()`'s `catch { /* ignore — return 0 */ }` is the closest to concerning but only affects an advisory count, not blob durability itself.
- `libs/data/store/store-adapter/src/{sqlite,turso}-adapter.ts` (2+2 sites) — rollback-error and non-fatal-stamp tolerance, correctly scoped.
- `libs/data/verify/claim-verification/src/{index,prefilter}.ts` (2 sites) — intentional fallback-to-NLI design, logged.
- `libs/data/vectors/vector-store/src/lancedb-worker.ts:246` — documented as an expected-transient training failure on small/skewed tables, self-heals on next upsert.
- `libs/data/embed/embedding-provider/src/embedWorker.ts:416`, `libs/memory-core/src/write-queue.ts:342` — both are "already closed"/idempotent-teardown tolerance, not data-loss risk.

**No silent catches found on the memory_write/memory_recall Phase-A hot path itself, in `write.ts`, or in `WriteQueue`'s main dequeue loop** (`write-queue.ts:814`, the one candidate there, correctly propagates via `item.reject(wrapped)` — confirmed a scanner false positive, not a defect).

---

**Fix sketch (scoped to the HIGH findings only — #1/#2 in `graphifyImport`, #3/#4 aggregate-undercounting):**
1. `graphifyImport`: track a `vecNodeInsertFailures` counter alongside `importedNodes`, increment it in the catch blocks at lines 649 and 687, and surface it in the function's return value (`{ ok: true, imported, edges_imported, shape, vec_insert_failures: N }`) so a caller can tell full success from partial-vector-loss success.
2. `graphifyImport`/`buildCommunities`'s edge-insert catches (lines 1048, 870): similarly track and surface a `skipped_edges`/`skipped_members` count rather than silently discarding the information the catch already has.
3. Do NOT change these to rethrow/abort the whole import on one bad row — per-row tolerance during a bulk import is a reasonable design; the defect is the SILENCE, not the tolerance.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that calls `graphifyImport()` against a fixture where one node's vec_node insert is forced to fail (e.g. a malformed embedding value or a locked table), and asserts (a) TODAY the function's return value shows `ok:true, imported:N` with no indication anything failed (red — demonstrates the silent aggregate lie); (b) after the fix, the return value surfaces a non-zero failure/skip count for the affected row (green). A second test does the same for `buildCommunities`'s MEMBER_OF edge insert.

run-release.mjs's GATE 1 (check-release-ranges) runs before `version` executes, so it checks stale pre-bump disk versions and false-positive-blocks a legitimate same-batch bump

**Discovered:** 2026-07-30, running the real `pnpm release` for this session's full batch.

**What happened:** `pnpm release` (= `run-release.mjs`) failed at GATE 1 with 3 "unresolvable dependency range(s)": `apigen-plugin-cli-output` and `apigen-python-env` declare `@adhd/apigen-core-client`/`@adhd/apigen-engine-runtime` as `^0.2.2`, but the registry (and, at GATE-1-check-time, the ON-DISK source `package.json`) only had `0.2.1` -- GATE 1 correctly flagged this as unresolvable and blocked publish entirely, exactly as designed.

**Root cause:** `run-release.mjs` runs GATE 1 (`check-release-ranges.mjs`) as the very first step, BEFORE `nx run-many -t publish` (which is what actually triggers each project's `version` task, since `publish`'s Nx `dependsOn` chain includes `version`). `range-resolvability.js`'s algorithm reads each package's CURRENT on-disk version to predict "what this release will publish" (its own doc comment: "Discover the release set: every publishable project's CURRENT on-disk {name, version, ...}"). In this case, `apigen-core-client`'s real source had changed (this session's `BUG-APIGEN-CORE-CLIENT-001` fix), so its `version` task -- confirmed via `nx run apigen-core-client:version --dryRun` -- correctly computes a bump to `0.2.2`. But since `version` hadn't run yet when GATE 1 checked, GATE 1 saw the STALE pre-bump `0.2.1` on disk and (correctly, given what it could see) concluded the dependents' `^0.2.2` ranges were unresolvable -- even though the pending, about-to-happen bump would make them resolvable.

**Why this specific case was recoverable but the pattern is fragile:** the two dependent packages happened to have ALREADY had their ranges correctly pre-bumped to `^0.2.2` (presumably by an earlier `sync-deps`/`version` partial run against a different intermediate state), which is exactly what tipped GATE 1 into a false-positive block instead of silently missing the drift. The fix applied this session was a manual workaround: run `nx run-many -t version` for real BEFORE retrying `pnpm release`, so GATE 1's disk-read reflects the real, about-to-be-published versions. This works, but it means a plain `pnpm release` invocation is not actually self-sufficient for a release batch containing this shape of change -- it requires a human/agent to notice the GATE 1 failure, correctly diagnose it as "stale pre-bump state" rather than "a real range bug," and manually pre-run `version` first. A less experienced operator could easily either wrongly "fix" the dependents' ranges DOWN to match the stale 0.2.1 (masking the real available bump and leaving a needlessly conservative range) or give up.

**Fix direction:**
1. Have `run-release.mjs` run `nx run-many -t version` for real (not dry-run) as its own explicit first step, BEFORE GATE 1, so GATE 1 always sees post-bump, accurate disk state. This is the most direct fix and matches what a manual operator now has to do by hand.
2. Alternatively/additionally, have `check-release-ranges.mjs` itself run (or shell out to) a `--dryRun` version pass first to compute the REAL about-to-be-published version per package, rather than reading raw current-disk version, so the gate's prediction is accurate without requiring a separate explicit `version` step in the pipeline.
3. Whichever approach: add a regression test that reproduces this exact shape (a dependent's range correctly anticipates a pending same-batch bump that hasn't been materialized on disk yet) and confirms GATE 1 does NOT false-positive-block it.

**Status:** OPEN.

meta_parsed.title: run-release.mjs's GATE 1 (check-release-ranges) runs before `version` executes, so it checks stale pre-bump disk versions and false-positive-blocks a legitimate same-batch bump
meta_parsed.body:
**Discovered:** 2026-07-30, running the real `pnpm release` for this session's full batch.

**What happened:** `pnpm release` (= `run-release.mjs`) failed at GATE 1 with 3 "unresolvable dependency range(s)": `apigen-plugin-cli-output` and `apigen-python-env` declare `@adhd/apigen-core-client`/`@adhd/apigen-engine-runtime` as `^0.2.2`, but the registry (and, at GATE-1-check-time, the ON-DISK source `package.json`) only had `0.2.1` -- GATE 1 correctly flagged this as unresolvable and blocked publish entirely, exactly as designed.

**Root cause:** `run-release.mjs` runs GATE 1 (`check-release-ranges.mjs`) as the very first step, BEFORE `nx run-many -t publish` (which is what actually triggers each project's `version` task, since `publish`'s Nx `dependsOn` chain includes `version`). `range-resolvability.js`'s algorithm reads each package's CURRENT on-disk version to predict "what this release will publish" (its own doc comment: "Discover the release set: every publishable project's CURRENT on-disk {name, version, ...}"). In this case, `apigen-core-client`'s real source had changed (this session's `BUG-APIGEN-CORE-CLIENT-001` fix), so its `version` task -- confirmed via `nx run apigen-core-client:version --dryRun` -- correctly computes a bump to `0.2.2`. But since `version` hadn't run yet when GATE 1 checked, GATE 1 saw the STALE pre-bump `0.2.1` on disk and (correctly, given what it could see) concluded the dependents' `^0.2.2` ranges were unresolvable -- even though the pending, about-to-happen bump would make them resolvable.

**Why this specific case was recoverable but the pattern is fragile:** the two dependent packages happened to have ALREADY had their ranges correctly pre-bumped to `^0.2.2` (presumably by an earlier `sync-deps`/`version` partial run against a different intermediate state), which is exactly what tipped GATE 1 into a false-positive block instead of silently missing the drift. The fix applied this session was a manual workaround: run `nx run-many -t version` for real BEFORE retrying `pnpm release`, so GATE 1's disk-read reflects the real, about-to-be-published versions. This works, but it means a plain `pnpm release` invocation is not actually self-sufficient for a release batch containing this shape of change -- it requires a human/agent to notice the GATE 1 failure, correctly diagnose it as "stale pre-bump state" rather than "a real range bug," and manually pre-run `version` first. A less experienced operator could easily either wrongly "fix" the dependents' ranges DOWN to match the stale 0.2.1 (masking the real available bump and leaving a needlessly conservative range) or give up.

**Fix direction:**
1. Have `run-release.mjs` run `nx run-many -t version` for real (not dry-run) as its own explicit first step, BEFORE GATE 1, so GATE 1 always sees post-bump, accurate disk state. This is the most direct fix and matches what a manual operator now has to do by hand.
2. Alternatively/additionally, have `check-release-ranges.mjs` itself run (or shell out to) a `--dryRun` version pass first to compute the REAL about-to-be-published version per package, rather than reading raw current-disk version, so the gate's prediction is accurate without requiring a separate explicit `version` step in the pipeline.
3. Whichever approach: add a regression test that reproduces this exact shape (a dependent's range correctly anticipates a pending same-batch bump that hasn't been materialized on disk yet) and confirms GATE 1 does NOT false-positive-block it.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, session-2026-07-30-release, 1: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/smoke-test/run-release.mjs:85-96 (GATE 1 runs before `nx run-many -t publish`, which is the only thing that triggers `version`); 2: tools/nx-plugins/build/lib/range-resolvability.js:32-40 (doc comment confirms the algorithm reads CURRENT on-disk versions, not a simulated post-bump state); 3: real `pnpm release` run this session, GATE 1 failure output citing apigen-plugin-cli-output/apigen-python-env's ^0.2.2 ranges as unresolvable against disk 0.2.1; 4: `nx run apigen-core-client:version --dryRun` output confirming the pending bump to 0.2.2 was real and correct, resolving the apparent conflict once actually applied]

content:
Orphaned communities are never garbage-collected — memory_invalidate only invalidates the episode, never its community/MEMBER_OF edge, so ordinary churn silently decays total_clustered toward 0 while cluster_count stays fixed; SUPERSEDES the 'downstream of vector scarcity' theory for the live 139-communities/0-members signature

Reported by `cluster-proof` (relayed by team-lead), independently verified by this agent reading the exact cited code paths.

`libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:264-296` (`materializeClusters`, read directly) is the ONLY code in the repo that sets `t_invalid` on a `community` node or its `MEMBER_OF` edges (confirmed via the UPDATE statements at lines ~287-291: `UPDATE node SET t_invalid = ? WHERE rowid IN (...)` scoped to `kind = 'community'`, and `UPDATE edge SET t_invalid = ? WHERE rel = 'MEMBER_OF' ... AND dst IN (...)`). This function only runs as part of a genuine full clustering pass — per the companion item `BUG-CLUSTER-INCREMENTAL-PATH-DEAD-STUB-001` (this repo, this triage round), a full pass essentially never happens on ordinary write-driven usage.

**The everyday supersession path never touches community state at all.** `memory_invalidate` (the standard bi-temporal invalidation tool documented in this extension's own CLAUDE.md) sets `t_invalid` on the EPISODE node only — there is no code path from `memory_invalidate` to `materializeClusters` or to any direct `UPDATE edge ... WHERE rel='MEMBER_OF'` cleanup. An episode can be invalidated (superseded, corrected, or aged out) while its stale `MEMBER_OF` edge to a community, and the community node itself, remain fully live.

`libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:650-664` (`clusterStats`, read directly): `total_clustered` is computed via `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge e JOIN node src ON ... src.kind='episode' AND src.t_invalid IS NULL JOIN node dst ON ... dst.kind='community' AND dst.t_invalid IS NULL WHERE e.rel='MEMBER_OF' AND e.t_invalid IS NULL` — this REQUIRES the source episode to be currently live (`t_invalid IS NULL`). Once an episode is invalidated via the everyday path above, it silently drops out of this count — `total_clustered` decays toward 0 with ordinary churn, while `cluster_count` (a separate, simpler `COUNT(*) FROM node WHERE kind='community' AND t_invalid IS NULL`) stays fixed, because nothing ever invalidates the now-empty community node itself.

**Reproduced by cluster-proof (relayed, not independently re-run by this agent):** invalidating 8 episodes drove `total_clustered` 24→16 with `cluster_count` unchanged at 3; the target community remained LIVE with all its members gone. A second repro proved a genuine FULL PASS is self-healing (it correctly invalidates now-empty stale communities via `materializeClusters`) — so vector scarcity alone cannot produce the live incident's observed state; this bug (orphaned communities never GC'd outside a full pass) plus the dead incremental-clustering stub TOGETHER fully explain the live signature.

**This SUPERSEDES any 'downstream of vector scarcity' explanation for the live 139-communities/0-members signature** — team-lead asked this agent to correct any existing tool-side item asserting that theory; **this agent searched all 24 existing tool-side items for 'scarcity'/'downstream of vector'/'139'/'cluster_count' and found none asserting that theory** (the only text matches were unrelated false positives from generic word overlap). If the scarcity theory exists anywhere, it is markdown-only (in the still-split-brained `BACKLOG.md`, e.g. inside BL-322's prose, per `DEBT-BACKLOG-TOOL-MARKDOWN-SPLIT-BRAIN-001`) and this agent cannot correct it in place without a BACKLOG.md hand-edit, which is out of scope per this repo's phase-3 tool-authoritative policy. Flagging this explicitly rather than silently leaving the correction undone.

**Fix sketch:** `memory_invalidate` (or a follow-up hook it triggers) must, when invalidating an episode that holds a live `MEMBER_OF` edge, either (a) invalidate that specific edge immediately (cheap, local, doesn't require a full pass) and check whether the target community now has zero live members — if so, invalidate the community node too; or (b) leave the edge/community alone but make `total_clustered`/`cluster_count` internally consistent (e.g. cluster_count also req a live-member check) so the two metrics can't diverge into a misleading 139/0 shape. Prefer (a): garbage-collecting community state incrementally, not just as an expensive full-pass side effect.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test that (a) builds a small cluster via a full pass, invalidates ALL member episodes via `memory_invalidate`, and asserts TODAY the community node is still live with 0 actual members and `cluster_count` unchanged (red — confirms orphaned-community leak); (b) after the fix, asserts the now-empty community is invalidated (or at minimum `cluster_count` correctly reflects only communities with ≥1 live member) without requiring a full clustering pass to run first.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, BUG-CLUSTER-ORPHANED-COMMUNITIES-NEVER-GC, 1: libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:264-296 (materializeClusters — sole code invalidating community nodes/MEMBER_OF edges, full-pass-only) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:650-664 (clusterStats — total_clustered requires src.t_invalid IS NULL, cluster_count does not check for live members) — read directly; 3: extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/CLAUDE.md (memory_invalidate tool documentation — confirms it operates on the episode/claim node, no community-side-effect documented) — read directly; 4: cluster-proof's repro — 8-episode invalidation driving total_clustered 24→16 with cluster_count fixed at 3, target community live with 0 members; second repro proving a full pass self-heals — relayed by team-lead, not independently re-run by this agent; 5: search of all 24 existing tool-side sox-ecosystem items for 'scarcity'/'139'/'cluster_count'/'downstream of vector' — no item found asserting the scarcity theory; if it exists it is markdown-only in BACKLOG.md, uncorrectable in place per phase-3 policy — run directly this round; 6: BUG-CLUSTER-INCREMENTAL-PATH-DEAD-STUB-001 (this repo, this triage round) — cross-linked companion finding, together fully explaining the live signature]

Default cluster cosine threshold 0.82 appears calibrated for near-duplicate content, not topically-related prose — measured intra-group cosine of 0.67-0.70 on real bge-base-en-v1.5 embeddings yields ZERO clusters at 0.82, full coverage at 0.65

Reported by `cluster-proof` (relayed by team-lead) from the same from-scratch e2e referenced in the companion items `BUG-CLUSTER-INCREMENTAL-PATH-DEAD-STUB-001` and `BUG-CLUSTER-ORPHANED-COMMUNITIES-NEVER-GC-001` filed this round. **Independently confirmed the threshold constant by reading the source**, not just relaying the claim:

`libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:918-920` (read directly):
```ts
function resolveDefaultThreshold(): number {
  return 0.82;
}
```
and `cluster.ts:39` (doc comment): "Cosine threshold τ (default 0.82)." Confirmed this is the actual live default, consumed at `cluster.ts:429` (`const threshold = opts.threshold ?? resolveDefaultThreshold();`).

**cluster-proof's measurement (relayed, not independently re-run by this agent — would require running the real bge-base-en-v1.5 model, out of this agent's investigation-only scope):** on a 24-episode, 3-topic corpus of naturally-worded topical prose (not near-duplicate/paraphrased content), intra-group cosine similarity measured **0.67–0.70**. At the default threshold of 0.82, this corpus produced **zero clusters** — every episode landed as a singleton. At an empirically-derived threshold of **0.65**, the SAME corpus produced `cluster_count=3` (matching the 3 real topics), `coverage=1.0`, **100% purity**, and zero cross-contamination between topics.

**Why this matters:** 0.82 is a reasonable threshold for detecting near-duplicate/paraphrase content (the near-dup detection path elsewhere in this codebase uses a similarly high bar deliberately), but topically-related, differently-worded natural prose — the actual shape of most real agent-memory episodes — sits meaningfully below that bar with this embedding model. **If this measurement generalizes, clustering under-performs across the board even after the incremental-stub and orphaned-community bugs (filed this round) are fixed** — a corrected clustering pipeline still wouldn't cluster much of anything at the current default threshold.

**This is a quality-ceiling finding, not an outage** — ranked MEDIUM per team-lead's own framing ("most interesting" but not a live-breaking bug like the two companion items). Filing to make sure it isn't lost once the dead-stub/orphan-GC fixes land and someone wonders why clustering still barely clusters anything.

**Fix sketch:** (a) re-run cluster-proof's measurement methodology (or an equivalent) against a larger, more representative corpus of REAL production episode content (not a synthetic 24-episode fixture) to confirm 0.65 (or some other value) generalizes rather than being an artifact of the small test corpus; (b) if confirmed, either lower `resolveDefaultThreshold()`'s default, or make it configurable per-store/per-topic rather than a single hardcoded global constant, since the 'right' threshold plausibly depends on the embedding model in use (bge-base-en-v1.5 specifically was measured here) and the nature of the content being clustered; (c) add a calibration note/doc-comment at the threshold's declaration site recording this finding so a future change to 0.82 isn't made blind.

**Acceptance criteria (red→green test naming this item's ID):** a test using a representative multi-topic corpus (ideally sourced from real, not synthetic, episode content) and the real embedding model asserts (a) TODAY at threshold=0.82, cluster_count is significantly below the known topic count for the corpus (red — reproduces the under-clustering); (b) after recalibration, cluster_count/coverage/purity land in an acceptable range for the same corpus (green). This test should be tagged as model-dependent (bge-base-en-v1.5) so it's revisited if the embedding model ever changes.

Citations: [wip/turso-live-metrics, triage, claude, DEBT-CLUSTER-THRESHOLD-MISCALIBRATED, 1: libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:918-920 (resolveDefaultThreshold() returns 0.82) — read directly; 2: libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:39 (doc comment confirming 0.82 as the documented default) — read directly; 3: libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:429 (threshold consumption site, opts.threshold ?? resolveDefaultThreshold()) — read directly; 4: cluster-proof's e2e measurement — 24-episode/3-topic corpus, real bge-base-en-v1.5, intra-group cosine 0.67-0.70 measured, 0.82 yields 0 clusters, 0.65 yields cluster_count=3/coverage=1.0/100% purity — relayed by team-lead, not independently re-run by this agent; 5: BUG-CLUSTER-INCREMENTAL-PATH-DEAD-STUB-001, BUG-CLUSTER-ORPHANED-COMMUNITIES-NEVER-GC-001 (this repo, this triage round) — cross-linked companion findings from the same investigation]

CI's "Publish" job (pull-request.yml) has neither GATE 1 (check-release-ranges) nor GATE 2 (clean-room-smoke); diverges architecturally from the hardened local `pnpm release` pipeline

**Discovered:** 2026-07-31, re-verifying `BUG-CI-PUBLISH-STALE-TARGETS-001` while scoping a release-pipeline redesign.

**Finding:** `.github/workflows/pull-request.yml`'s `Publish` step (lines 127-141, gated on a `publish` PR label or a merged PR) runs:
```
npx nx affected -t build --exclude=$EXCLUDE --parallel=4
npx nx affected -t version --exclude=$EXCLUDE --parallel=4
npx nx affected -t publish --exclude=$EXCLUDE --configuration=production --parallel=4
```
This is a real, working, `nx affected`-based publish path -- NOT the stale/broken thing `BUG-CI-PUBLISH-STALE-TARGETS-001` originally described (that item's specific claims -- legacy targetDefaults, a hardcoded `dist/libs/core` path -- are now stale/fixed, see that item's 2026-07-31 note). But this CI path is a COMPLETELY SEPARATE mechanism from the local `pnpm release` (`tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/smoke-test/run-release.mjs`) that this session's real publish work exercised end-to-end. Confirmed via grep (zero matches for `check-release-ranges`/`clean-room-smoke`/`run-release` anywhere in `pull-request.yml`): CI's publish path has

- **no GATE 1** (`check-release-ranges.mjs` -- the pre-publish check that a package's declared internal `@adhd/*` ranges will actually resolve once published; this session's real publish run was blocked by this gate on its first attempt, correctly catching a real problem before any registry write), and
- **no GATE 2** (`clean-room-smoke.mjs` -- the post-publish real `npm install` smoke test across every published package; this session's run relied on this to confirm 54/54 packages installed cleanly after publishing).

**Impact:** if this CI job ever actually fires (a PR gets the `publish` label, or a PR merges with affected libraries present), it can publish packages with an unresolvable internal dependency range (the exact `ETARGET`-class failure `BUG-RELEASE-UNINSTALLABLE-AGENTMCP-001`/`BUG-RELEASE-UNINSTALLABLE-APIGEN-001` already happened via twice before) with zero pre-publish check, and with zero post-publish verification that what it just shipped actually installs. The two gates that this session's local pipeline proved catch real, recurring failure classes simply don't exist on the CI code path.

**Relationship to the in-progress release-pipeline redesign:** this finding should be folded into that redesign's scope, not fixed in isolation -- the redesign is already unifying the local pipeline around affected-scoping; CI's publish step should end up calling the SAME unified mechanism (including both gates) rather than persisting as a second, independently-evolving, gate-less implementation of "affected publish."

**Fix direction:** once the release-pipeline redesign lands a single canonical publish entrypoint (likely `run-release.mjs` itself, updated to be affected-scoped per the redesign), rewire CI's `Publish` step to call that entrypoint instead of its own raw `nx affected -t build/version/publish` sequence, so there is exactly one publish code path, not two that can silently diverge again.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, release-pipeline-redesign-2026-07-31, 1: .github/workflows/pull-request.yml:127-141 (CI Publish step, no gate references); 2: tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/smoke-test/run-release.mjs (the local pipeline's GATE 1/GATE 2 sequencing, confirmed present and working this session); 3: BUG-CI-PUBLISH-STALE-TARGETS-001 (prior, now largely-stale finding about the same CI step, different specific bug)]

createItem's FTS dedupe scan false-positive-blocks creation on weak token overlap with an unrelated, long candidate document -- no relevance/similarity threshold

**Discovered:** 2026-07-31, live-proving `apigen-plugin-batch`'s `batch_action` MCP tool works end-to-end against the real production backlog store (unrelated task: confirming the batch feature genuinely works live, not just in test suites).

**Reproduction (two independent calls, same result):**
1. `batch_action({operation:'backlog/create-item', items:[{input:{family:'TEST-BATCH-LIVE-PROOF', title:'live batch proof item 1', body:'disposable...', repo:'PseudoSky/adhd'}}, ...]})` -- items at index 0 and 2 both returned `created:false` with `duplicateCandidates:[BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001]`, an existing, completely unrelated ticket about CLI mount-flag wiring.
2. Isolated the batch mechanism as a suspect: called plain (non-batch) `backlog_create_item` with the IDENTICAL single-item input (`family:'TEST-BATCH-LIVE-PROOF', title:'live batch proof item 1', ...`) -- got the exact same false-positive: `created:false`, `duplicateCandidates:[BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001]`. **This proves the bug is in `dedupeScan` itself (entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:30), not specific to the batch feature** -- batch's own concurrency/per-item isolation is unaffected and worked correctly otherwise (confirmed: with `force:true`, the same 3-item batch created 2 real distinct items (nodeIds 614/615) and correctly rejected the 3rd for an unrelated intentional enum violation, `onItemError:continue` honored).

**Root cause (read, not fully traced to the underlying FTS engine -- `store.graph.searchNodes` is implemented in the external `@adhd/sox-graph-store` dependency, not in this repo):** `dedupeScan()` (`entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:30-45`) runs `sanitizeFtsQuery(input.title)` through `store.graph.searchNodes(ftsQuery, {limit:10, filter:{tags:[BACKLOG_ITEM_TAG], namespace:repo}})` with **no relevance/similarity score threshold** -- any hit within the top-10 FTS matches becomes a `duplicateCandidate` regardless of how weak the match is. My test title (`"live batch proof item 1"`) shares only common, generic tokens ("live", "batch") with `BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001`'s body -- an exceptionally long ticket that happens to repeat both words many times (it's literally about `apigen-plugin-batch`'s `--use batch` mount and CLI "live dispatch"). A long document containing common query tokens many times is disproportionately likely to surface as a top FTS match even when a human would immediately see zero real semantic relationship to a short, generic new title.

**Impact:** any new backlog item whose title happens to share a few common words with an existing long/verbose ticket risks being silently blocked from creation (`created:false`, no node written) unless the caller notices `duplicateCandidates` in the response and passes `force:true`. For an agent that doesn't carefully check the response shape, this looks like a successful create (the response still contains an `item` object -- it's just the WRONG, pre-existing item, not a new one) -- a real risk of an agent believing it logged a new finding when it actually got silently redirected to an unrelated ticket.

**Fix direction:** add a minimum relevance/similarity threshold to the FTS dedupe check (e.g., require a BM25/rank score above some cutoff, or require a minimum fraction of the query's tokens to appear in the CANDIDATE's title specifically, not just anywhere in its body, since title-similarity is a much stronger duplicate signal than incidental body-text overlap in a long document). Consider also weighting/limiting matches against the query title vs. the full body text asymmetrically. Add a regression test using a fixture shaped exactly like this real case (a short generic new title vs. a long existing document sharing only common words) asserting NO duplicate candidate is returned.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, session-2026-07-31-batch-live-proof, 1: entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:30-45 (dedupeScan, no relevance threshold on FTS hits); 2: live repro -- batch_action call this session, items 0/2 of 3 both returned duplicateCandidates:[BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001] for unrelated disposable test titles; 3: isolated repro -- plain backlog_create_item with the identical single input reproduced the identical false-positive, proving the bug is in dedupeScan itself, not the batch feature]

meta_parsed.title: createItem's FTS dedupe scan false-positive-blocks creation on weak token overlap with an unrelated, long candidate document -- no relevance/similarity threshold
meta_parsed.body:
**Discovered:** 2026-07-31, live-proving `apigen-plugin-batch`'s `batch_action` MCP tool works end-to-end against the real production backlog store (unrelated task: confirming the batch feature genuinely works live, not just in test suites).

**Reproduction (two independent calls, same result):**
1. `batch_action({operation:'backlog/create-item', items:[{input:{family:'TEST-BATCH-LIVE-PROOF', title:'live batch proof item 1', body:'disposable...', repo:'PseudoSky/adhd'}}, ...]})` -- items at index 0 and 2 both returned `created:false` with `duplicateCandidates:[BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001]`, an existing, completely unrelated ticket about CLI mount-flag wiring.
2. Isolated the batch mechanism as a suspect: called plain (non-batch) `backlog_create_item` with the IDENTICAL single-item input (`family:'TEST-BATCH-LIVE-PROOF', title:'live batch proof item 1', ...`) -- got the exact same false-positive: `created:false`, `duplicateCandidates:[BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001]`. **This proves the bug is in `dedupeScan` itself (entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:30), not specific to the batch feature** -- batch's own concurrency/per-item isolation is unaffected and worked correctly otherwise (confirmed: with `force:true`, the same 3-item batch created 2 real distinct items (nodeIds 614/615) and correctly rejected the 3rd for an unrelated intentional enum violation, `onItemError:continue` honored).

**Root cause (read, not fully traced to the underlying FTS engine -- `store.graph.searchNodes` is implemented in the external `@adhd/sox-graph-store` dependency, not in this repo):** `dedupeScan()` (`entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:30-45`) runs `sanitizeFtsQuery(input.title)` through `store.graph.searchNodes(ftsQuery, {limit:10, filter:{tags:[BACKLOG_ITEM_TAG], namespace:repo}})` with **no relevance/similarity score threshold** -- any hit within the top-10 FTS matches becomes a `duplicateCandidate` regardless of how weak the match is. My test title (`"live batch proof item 1"`) shares only common, generic tokens ("live", "batch") with `BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001`'s body -- an exceptionally long ticket that happens to repeat both words many times (it's literally about `apigen-plugin-batch`'s `--use batch` mount and CLI "live dispatch"). A long document containing common query tokens many times is disproportionately likely to surface as a top FTS match even when a human would immediately see zero real semantic relationship to a short, generic new title.

**Impact:** any new backlog item whose title happens to share a few common words with an existing long/verbose ticket risks being silently blocked from creation (`created:false`, no node written) unless the caller notices `duplicateCandidates` in the response and passes `force:true`. For an agent that doesn't carefully check the response shape, this looks like a successful create (the response still contains an `item` object -- it's just the WRONG, pre-existing item, not a new one) -- a real risk of an agent believing it logged a new finding when it actually got silently redirected to an unrelated ticket.

**Fix direction:** add a minimum relevance/similarity threshold to the FTS dedupe check (e.g., require a BM25/rank score above some cutoff, or require a minimum fraction of the query's tokens to appear in the CANDIDATE's title specifically, not just anywhere in its body, since title-similarity is a much stronger duplicate signal than incidental body-text overlap in a long document). Consider also weighting/limiting matches against the query title vs. the full body text asymmetrically. Add a regression test using a fixture shaped exactly like this real case (a short generic new title vs. a long existing document sharing only common words) asserting NO duplicate candidate is returned.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, session-2026-07-31-batch-live-proof, 1: entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:30-45 (dedupeScan, no relevance threshold on FTS hits); 2: live repro -- batch_action call this session, items 0/2 of 3 both returned duplicateCandidates:[BUG-APIGEN-CLI-OUTPUT-001] for unrelated disposable test titles; 3: isolated repro -- plain backlog_create_item with the identical single input reproduced the identical false-positive, proving the bug is in dedupeScan itself, not the batch feature]

Ran npx nx run backlog:test myself -- 25 files, 187 tests, exit 0 (includes both this fix's 2 new tests in client.spec.ts and a concurrent dispatch's 25 new required-field-validation tests, confirmed coexisting cleanly with no conflict).

[transition to RESOLVED] Root cause was more subtle than initially hypothesized: store.graph.searchNodes() does return a bm25 relevance score, but it doesn't discriminate this case (a short generic title vs. a long unrelated document scored ~0.0000109, a genuine short-vs-short near-duplicate scored ~0.0000113 -- same order of magnitude, no clean threshold, since raw term-frequency in a long document rivals a real duplicate's score). Fixed instead with a title-to-title token-overlap filter (crud.ts:80-142): TITLE_OVERLAP_MIN_FRACTION=0.5, meaningfulTitleTokens()/titleMeaningfullyOverlaps() require an FTS hit's own title (not just its body) to share at least half the new title's meaningful tokens before counting as a duplicate candidate. content:
nx.json production/default inputs conflate code and docs — need a codeOnly named-input group so docs-only edits don't cascade real test/build reruns

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not just README): `nx.json`'s `namedInputs.production` (and `default`, which `production` extends) exclude cypress/eslint/spec/jest/storybook files but nothing doc-related. Every per-package `README.md` (50 pkgs), `CHANGELOG.md` (49), `LICENSE` (9), `BACKLOG.md` (9, stale per repo policy — should be generator-projected), and `docs/marketing/.catalog/*.md` (metrics/capabilities/distribution/doc-conformance/doc-ops/required-tooling/review/consumer, regenerated on every doc-steward run) all match the unexcluded `{projectRoot}/**/*` glob. Since `test`'s targetDefaults inputs are `["default", "^production", ...]` and `build`/`@nx/js:tsc`/`@nx/vite:build` are `["production", "^production"]`, editing ANY of these doc files on a low-in-the-graph package invalidates that package's own test/build cache HASH and cascades via `^production` to every real dependent's test/build hash too — forcing genuine cache-miss (real, non-replayed) test/build reruns across the whole dependent subtree for a pure-docs change. Observed directly: editing 2 package READMEs (apigen-base-logical, apigen-engine-runtime) triggered an 8-minute pre-commit Gate 3 (`nx affected -t test`) rerunning ~20 real apigen-family + backlog test suites.

CLARIFIED MECHANISM (ruled out an alternate theory): NOT caused by the repo's real `assets` target (`@adhd/nx-assets:copy`, attached to every buildable project by `tools/nx-plugins/assets/plugin.js`) or the `copyReadme`/`copyDocFiles` Vite plugin (`tools/vite-plugins/copy-readme.mjs`). Both are correctly scoped only into `nx-release-publish`'s dependency chain (`assets` is not a dependency of `test`/`build` at all) — nothing about them ran or leaked upstream during the incident. The invalidation is purely input-hash glob matching on `test`/`build`'s OWN declared `inputs`, independent of which target actually consumes the file.

IMPORTANT PRECISION (self-corrected): `nx affected -t <target> --files=X` has TWO separate mechanisms that must not be conflated. (1) PROJECT SELECTION — pure git-diff + project-graph topology; a file inside a project's root always makes that project "affected" regardless of any `inputs` config, and this does NOT change under the proposed fix (`nx show projects --affected --files=X` will show the SAME project list before and after). (2) CACHE HIT VS MISS for each selected project's task — this IS governed by named-input groups, and is the actual mechanism causing the slow reruns. The fix makes doc-only changes produce 100% cache HITS (fast replay) for `test`/`build` instead of shrinking the affected-project list. Any verification must key off Nx's own cache-hit/miss reporting per task, never off `nx show projects --affected` list size.

FIX: add a new named-input group `codeOnly` = `production` minus `!{projectRoot}/README.md`, `!{projectRoot}/CHANGELOG.md`, `!{projectRoot}/LICENSE`, `!{projectRoot}/BACKLOG.md`, `!{projectRoot}/docs/marketing/.catalog/**`. Point `test`, `build`, `@nx/js:tsc`, `@nx/vite:build` targetDefaults at `codeOnly`/`^codeOnly`. Leave `assets`/`nx-release-publish` on the current broad `default`/`production` so a real doc change still forces a fresh publish artifact (confirmed via reading `tools/nx-plugins/assets/executors/copy/impl.js`: the `assets` executor unconditionally `fs.copyFileSync`s the LIVE README.md/CHANGELOG.md from source into dist every time it executes, independent of whether `build` cache-hit — so publish correctness is preserved even though the Vite-embedded `copyReadme` plugin becomes dead weight on cache-hit builds, which is fine since `nx-release-publish` depends on `assets` directly, not on the Vite plugin running).

SCOPE NOTE: 24 project.json files locally override `inputs` for `test`/`typecheck`/`assets`/`generate-api` with the same `['default','^production',...]` shape, which SHADOWS targetDefaults — a global nx.json edit alone won't fix these 24 projects; each needs the same edit (or, cleaner, delete the override where it's just duplicating the default so it inherits automatically). `entrypoint/backlog`'s own `assets` target already narrows its inputs to exactly `README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`/`package.json`/`skill/**` — a working precedent for this pattern.

VERIFICATION PROTOCOL (in an isolated `.worktrees/nx-inputs-fix-verify`, pnpm-installed, independent Nx daemon/cache):

Case A (control/baseline) — on UNMODIFIED nx.json: `nx reset`, prime cache via `nx run-many -t test,build` across apigen family + backlog + deps, touch only `apigen-base-logical/README.md`, run `CI=true npx nx affected -t test --files=<path>`. Record Nx's own cache hit/miss summary line and wall-clock — expect mostly/all CACHE MISSES (reproduces the bug).

Case B (fix applied, same edit) — apply the `codeOnly` group + all 24 project.json overrides, `nx reset`, re-prime cache under the new hash scheme, touch the SAME README again, run the identical command. Expect 100% CACHE HITS ("Nx read the output from the cache... for N out of N tasks"), wall-clock drops to seconds. This ratio, not affected-list size, is the pass/fail gate.

Case C (no under-invalidation — the dangerous direction) — with fix applied, make a REAL source edit (e.g. throwaway exported const in apigen-base-logical/src/index.ts), run the same affected-test command. Assert (a) affected PROJECT SET is byte-identical to a pre-fix recording of `nx show projects --affected --files=<same path>` (topological, stable oracle unaffected by inputs either way), and (b) those tasks are CACHE MISSES — they actually ran. Also grep repo-wide for any test reading a real `.md` fixture as actual input (already ruled out README/CHANGELOG string-literal false positives in agent-generator-plugin + apigen-core-client specs — those are just example filenames in filter-logic tests, not content reads) — guards against a future broadened exclusion pattern (`**/*.md` instead of named files) blinding a real markdown-processing test's cache.

Case D (publish correctness, end to end) — edit only a README under the fix, run the real chain: `nx run <pkg>:build` (expect cache hit) → `nx run <pkg>:assets` (expect cache miss, real copy) → `diff dist/<pkg>/README.md <source>/README.md` with exit-code check (not eyeballing) to prove the published artifact still gets fresh docs even though build itself cache-hit.

Case E (real wall-clock, real hook) — stage the same single-README diff, time `.githooks/pre-commit` end-to-end (not the isolated nx command) before/after, same method as the existing Phase 2 before/after measurement in tmp/release-pipeline-audit.md.

Case F (permanent regression guard, not one-time proof) — write a committed structural test (same style as the existing changed-set.spec.mjs/run-release.spec.mjs RED-equivalent tests from Phase 1) parsing nx.json and asserting `codeOnly` exists, excludes each known doc pattern, and that test/build/tsc/vite:build targetDefaults reference it — so a future revert or new doc-file-type addition fails CI instead of silently regressing.

Also confirmed no cross-system divergence risk: the release-pipeline's own `tools/nx-plugins/build/lib/changed-set.js` unions git-diff-affected (topological, unaffected by inputs) with `published-state.json`-cache-staleness (its own independent, already-correct hash) — it does not duplicate or depend on Nx's per-target input-hash logic, so this fix doesn't need to touch it.

meta_parsed.title: nx.json production/default inputs conflate code and docs — need a codeOnly named-input group so docs-only edits don't cascade real test/build reruns
meta_parsed.body:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not just README): `nx.json`'s `namedInputs.production` (and `default`, which `production` extends) exclude cypress/eslint/spec/jest/storybook files but nothing doc-related. Every per-package `README.md` (50 pkgs), `CHANGELOG.md` (49), `LICENSE` (9), `BACKLOG.md` (9, stale per repo policy — should be generator-projected), and `docs/marketing/.catalog/*.md` (metrics/capabilities/distribution/doc-conformance/doc-ops/required-tooling/review/consumer, regenerated on every doc-steward run) all match the unexcluded `{projectRoot}/**/*` glob. Since `test`'s targetDefaults inputs are `["default", "^production", ...]` and `build`/`@nx/js:tsc`/`@nx/vite:build` are `["production", "^production"]`, editing ANY of these doc files on a low-in-the-graph package invalidates that package's own test/build cache HASH and cascades via `^production` to every real dependent's test/build hash too — forcing genuine cache-miss (real, non-replayed) test/build reruns across the whole dependent subtree for a pure-docs change. Observed directly: editing 2 package READMEs (apigen-base-logical, apigen-engine-runtime) triggered an 8-minute pre-commit Gate 3 (`nx affected -t test`) rerunning ~20 real apigen-family + backlog test suites.

CLARIFIED MECHANISM (ruled out an alternate theory): NOT caused by the repo's real `assets` target (`@adhd/nx-assets:copy`, attached to every buildable project by `tools/nx-plugins/assets/plugin.js`) or the `copyReadme`/`copyDocFiles` Vite plugin (`tools/vite-plugins/copy-readme.mjs`). Both are correctly scoped only into `nx-release-publish`'s dependency chain (`assets` is not a dependency of `test`/`build` at all) — nothing about them ran or leaked upstream during the incident. The invalidation is purely input-hash glob matching on `test`/`build`'s OWN declared `inputs`, independent of which target actually consumes the file.

IMPORTANT PRECISION (self-corrected): `nx affected -t <target> --files=X` has TWO separate mechanisms that must not be conflated. (1) PROJECT SELECTION — pure git-diff + project-graph topology; a file inside a project's root always makes that project "affected" regardless of any `inputs` config, and this does NOT change under the proposed fix (`nx show projects --affected --files=X` will show the SAME project list before and after). (2) CACHE HIT VS MISS for each selected project's task — this IS governed by named-input groups, and is the actual mechanism causing the slow reruns. The fix makes doc-only changes produce 100% cache HITS (fast replay) for `test`/`build` instead of shrinking the affected-project list. Any verification must key off Nx's own cache-hit/miss reporting per task, never off `nx show projects --affected` list size.

FIX: add a new named-input group `codeOnly` = `production` minus `!{projectRoot}/README.md`, `!{projectRoot}/CHANGELOG.md`, `!{projectRoot}/LICENSE`, `!{projectRoot}/BACKLOG.md`, `!{projectRoot}/docs/marketing/.catalog/**`. Point `test`, `build`, `@nx/js:tsc`, `@nx/vite:build` targetDefaults at `codeOnly`/`^codeOnly`. Leave `assets`/`nx-release-publish` on the current broad `default`/`production` so a real doc change still forces a fresh publish artifact (confirmed via reading `tools/nx-plugins/assets/executors/copy/impl.js`: the `assets` executor unconditionally `fs.copyFileSync`s the LIVE README.md/CHANGELOG.md from source into dist every time it executes, independent of whether `build` cache-hit — so publish correctness is preserved even though the Vite-embedded `copyReadme` plugin becomes dead weight on cache-hit builds, which is fine since `nx-release-publish` depends on `assets` directly, not on the Vite plugin running).

SCOPE NOTE: 24 project.json files locally override `inputs` for `test`/`typecheck`/`assets`/`generate-api` with the same `['default','^production',...]` shape, which SHADOWS targetDefaults — a global nx.json edit alone won't fix these 24 projects; each needs the same edit (or, cleaner, delete the override where it's just duplicating the default so it inherits automatically). `entrypoint/backlog`'s own `assets` target already narrows its inputs to exactly `README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`/`package.json`/`skill/**` — a working precedent for this pattern.

VERIFICATION PROTOCOL (in an isolated `.worktrees/nx-inputs-fix-verify`, pnpm-installed, independent Nx daemon/cache):

Case A (control/baseline) — on UNMODIFIED nx.json: `nx reset`, prime cache via `nx run-many -t test,build` across apigen family + backlog + deps, touch only `apigen-base-logical/README.md`, run `CI=true npx nx affected -t test --files=<path>`. Record Nx's own cache hit/miss summary line and wall-clock — expect mostly/all CACHE MISSES (reproduces the bug).

Case B (fix applied, same edit) — apply the `codeOnly` group + all 24 project.json overrides, `nx reset`, re-prime cache under the new hash scheme, touch the SAME README again, run the identical command. Expect 100% CACHE HITS ("Nx read the output from the cache... for N out of N tasks"), wall-clock drops to seconds. This ratio, not affected-list size, is the pass/fail gate.

Case C (no under-invalidation — the dangerous direction) — with fix applied, make a REAL source edit (e.g. throwaway exported const in apigen-base-logical/src/index.ts), run the same affected-test command. Assert (a) affected PROJECT SET is byte-identical to a pre-fix recording of `nx show projects --affected --files=<same path>` (topological, stable oracle unaffected by inputs either way), and (b) those tasks are CACHE MISSES — they actually ran. Also grep repo-wide for any test reading a real `.md` fixture as actual input (already ruled out README/CHANGELOG string-literal false positives in agent-generator-plugin + apigen-core-client specs — those are just example filenames in filter-logic tests, not content reads) — guards against a future broadened exclusion pattern (`**/*.md` instead of named files) blinding a real markdown-processing test's cache.

Case D (publish correctness, end to end) — edit only a README under the fix, run the real chain: `nx run <pkg>:build` (expect cache hit) → `nx run <pkg>:assets` (expect cache miss, real copy) → `diff dist/<pkg>/README.md <source>/README.md` with exit-code check (not eyeballing) to prove the published artifact still gets fresh docs even though build itself cache-hit.

Case E (real wall-clock, real hook) — stage the same single-README diff, time `.githooks/pre-commit` end-to-end (not the isolated nx command) before/after, same method as the existing Phase 2 before/after measurement in tmp/release-pipeline-audit.md.

Case F (permanent regression guard, not one-time proof) — write a committed structural test (same style as the existing changed-set.spec.mjs/run-release.spec.mjs RED-equivalent tests from Phase 1) parsing nx.json and asserting `codeOnly` exists, excludes each known doc pattern, and that test/build/tsc/vite:build targetDefaults reference it — so a future revert or new doc-file-type addition fails CI instead of silently regressing.

Also confirmed no cross-system divergence risk: the release-pipeline's own `tools/nx-plugins/build/lib/changed-set.js` unions git-diff-affected (topological, unaffected by inputs) with `published-state.json`-cache-staleness (its own independent, already-correct hash) — it does not duplicate or depend on Nx's per-target input-hash logic, so this fix doesn't need to touch it.

content:
backlog: add a `version` command/tool that reports the running system's installed package version

Related to TASK-003 (INTERFACE_v2 tool consolidation) but distinct: there is currently no way for a caller (human CLI user or an MCP client) to ask the *running* backlog process what version it actually is — which matters because this repo runs multiple backlog surfaces side by side: the local dev build at `entrypoint/backlog/dist/index.js` (wired via `.mcp.json`, currently the source for `mcp__backlog__*` tools in this session) and a *completely unrelated* globally pnpm-installed package also named `backlog` (`/Users/nix/Library/pnpm/backlog`, v1.4.56 — a different orchestrator product with `board`/`daemon`/`orchestrator`/`worktree` commands, registered as the `backlog` MCP server in the user's global `~/.claude.json`). Confirmed live: `npx --no-install backlog --version` prints `1.4.56` and `--help` shows none of this repo's CRUD-style surface — proving the naming collision is real, not hypothetical.

Requirements:
- CLI: `backlog version` (or `--version`) prints the resolved `@adhd/backlog` package.json version + build metadata (git sha / build timestamp if available) from the actually-running dist, not a hardcoded string.
- MCP: expose the same as a callable operation (e.g. `backlog_version`) so an MCP client can distinguish which `backlog` server it's actually talking to at runtime, without shelling out.
- Must read the version from the running system (resolve own `package.json` relative to the loaded module, mirroring the existing `backlogDistDir()` probe pattern in `entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts` that already handles the published/dev-built/vitest three-layout problem), never a value baked in at a different build time.
- Verify: prove it returns the correct version both when run from `entrypoint/backlog/dist/index.js` (dev-built) and from an npm-installed tarball layout, per AGENTS.md §7's real-component verification standard.

This would have let us immediately detect the `/Users/nix/Library/pnpm/backlog` vs `entrypoint/backlog` collision from inside a session instead of via manual `--help` diffing.
