content:
apigen: CLI/MCP help text collapses nested/$ref params to bare "object" — add a configurable usage(op) full-schema command

Confirmed by reading source, not guessed. apigen does NOT auto-build full help text today — what exists is a flat one-line-per-param summary, and it genuinely oversimplifies:

`@adhd/apigen-engine-runtime`'s `describe-params.ts` (`typeName()`) collapses:
- any nested object property to the literal string `'object'` (no properties, no nested field names, no depth at all)
- any `$ref` to just the ref's bare name (e.g. `BacklogItem`), never the referenced shape
- any `oneOf`/`anyOf` to the literal string `'union'`

This is exactly the CLI-visible surface: `apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/run.ts` builds its `--help` text from this same `name?: type` summary (comment at run.ts:254 says it "mirrors the former `describeParams(schema).text`"). Live proof from this session: `mcp__backlog__backlog_create_item`'s own auto-generated MCP tool description reads `"apigen calling convention: all domain parameters go inside a \"data\" envelope"` with a flat property/type list — no nested shape for e.g. `dedupeScan: object`.

By contrast, the MCP tool *description* path (`apigen-engine-runtime`'s `buildToolDescription`, via `apigen-base-logical`'s `synthesizeExample`/`renderExampleNote`) already walks the FULL schema (resolves `$ref`, picks `oneOf` branches, merges `allOf`) to produce one concrete worked example — so the full-shape information already exists and is already schema-driven; it's just never exposed as an on-demand, per-operation "show me the whole shape" surface, and the CLI help path doesn't use it at all.

Proposed fix (as discussed with user, not yet designed in detail): a configurable usage plugin analogous to `@adhd/apigen-plugin-batch`'s design —
- A build-time option: **minimal** (today's default — list operations, and for each suggest `<client> usage <op>` / an MCP `usage` tool call to get details) vs **full** (expose the complete JSON-Schema-derived shape per op directly in the standard usage/help call, no second round-trip).
- A callable `usage(operation?)` operation/tool: with no arg, lists operations (today's minimal behavior); with an operation id, returns the FULL input schema for that op (not the collapsed `name: type` line) — reusing `synthesizeExample`/`renderExampleNote` plus the raw resolved schema (post `$ref`/`oneOf`/`allOf` resolution), not just the worked example.
- CLI: `usage` becomes a real command; MCP: a `usage` tool alongside the mounted operations.

Open design questions for whoever picks this up: where does `usage` live architecturally (apigen-engine-runtime alongside `buildToolDescription`, or a new `apigen-plugin-usage` mirroring `apigen-plugin-batch`'s mount-plugin shape)? Does "full" mode change every tool description's default verbosity, or only the dedicated `usage` call? How does full-schema resolution behave for the batch mount's root-level `oneOf`+`discriminator` union (see `apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/mount-cli-flags.ts`'s existing per-branch merge logic — likely the same resolution shape usage(op) needs for batch ops).

Scope note: this is a real gap in the core value proposition (discoverability of the actual call shape), not a batch-spec detail — filed as its own FEAT rather than folded into TASK-003 (backlog's own MCP interface consolidation), since it's an apigen-wide capability that would benefit every apigen-mounted package, backlog included.

- A callable `usage(operation?)` operation/tool: with no arg, lists operations (today's minimal behavior); with an operation id, returns the FULL input schema for that op (not the collapsed `name: type` line) — reusing `synthesizeExample`/`renderExampleNote` plus the raw resolved schema (post `$ref`/`oneOf`/`allOf` resolution), not just the worked example.
- CLI: `usage` becomes a real command; MCP: a `usage` tool alongside the mounted operations.

Open design questions for whoever picks this up: where does `usage` live architecturally (apigen-engine-runtime alongside `buildToolDescription`, or a new `apigen-plugin-usage` mirroring `apigen-plugin-batch`'s mount-plugin shape)? Does "full" mode change every tool description's default verbosity, or only the dedicated `usage` call? How does full-schema resolution behave for the batch mount's root-level `oneOf`+`discriminator` union (see `apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/mount-cli-flags.ts`'s existing per-branch merge logic — likely the same resolution shape usage(op) needs for batch ops).

Scope note: this is a real gap in the core value proposition (discoverability of the actual call shape), not a batch-spec detail — filed as its own FEAT rather than folded into TASK-003 (backlog's own MCP interface consolidation), since it's an apigen-wide capability that would benefit every apigen-mounted package, backlog included.

detail.reason: Refuted by direct measurement 2026-08-08, and the owner confirms the Turso conversion data loss was fully fixed. Three-way comparison run read-only per the warning on this item (sqlite3 file:...?mode=ro on the backups; live read via memory_stats/memory_ping integrity probe, never via db_path through openDb): backup memory.db.20260728-121524.turso-migration = 9216 node rows / 45846 edge rows; backup memory.db.20260728-153052.pre-swap = 9216 / 45846 -- byte-identical counts, so there was no 12:15->15:30 write delta to discard and the rollback hypothesis does not apply either. Live store now reports ix_node_kind fully populated at 10337/10337 rows, i.e. 1121 MORE nodes than either backup. The store did not lose 716 nodes; it has grown past both forensic snapshots. Live integrity is ok across all six probes with zero damaged objects. Closing INVALID rather than RESOLVED because no fix was applied -- the premise was wrong, most likely by measuring an already-restored store against the wrong baseline.

detail.reason: Fixed in e6e9453e. CORRECTION to the filed mechanism: a build cache-hit does NOT wipe the copied assets — measured directly, they survive it. The actual defect is that the inferred assets target was declared cache:true with NO outputs, and an nx cacheable task with no declared outputs restores nothing on a cache hit while still reporting success. So once assets was cached, a dist missing README.md/CHANGELOG.md/llms.txt stayed missing and a publish shipped a package with no README. The prescribed fix was right even though the mechanism was not. assetOutputs() now enumerates the asset files that actually exist for the project and declares each as an individual {projectRoot}/dist/<basename> output. Per-file, deliberately not the whole dist directory: BUG-026 established that a whole-directory output makes nx do a destructive remove(dir);copy(cachedDir,dir) swap that would wipe the build compiled output; per-file outputs merge. Generalizes BUG-026 single-project fix to every inferred assets target. Regression pin bug-017-assets-outputs.spec.mjs: 5/5 green with the fix, 5/5 RED with the plugin reverted, plugin restored and md5-verified. Repro before the fix: rm dist/README.md; nx run backlog:assets -> reads from cache -> README still absent. NOT fixed and filed separately: the executor chmod of pkg.bin targets is still lost on an assets cache hit, since claiming build outputs here would reintroduce BUG-026.

Implemented the lifetime operational control plane for the embed/enrich pipeline so it can surface and recover from any root cause that wedges it, plus a live-outage fix and the user-reviewed poison correction.

1) LIVE OUTAGE (2026-08-30): memory_ping/write path failed with 'no such table: enrich_poison'. Root cause: the enrich_poison DDL comment contained a semicolon which DDL_BASE.split(';') broke into an invalid SQL statement; db.ts per-statement catch swallowed the syntax error at log.debug (dropped at the default info level). Fix: removed the semicolon (also fixed the identical pre-existing promotion_queue comment semicolon) and made db.ts distinguish 'already exists' (debug) from genuine DDL failures (WARN/ERROR). Rebuilt + restarted the launchd unit; verified memory_ping status:ok, store_ok:true, integrity.healthy:true, and a real memory_write probe succeeded.

2) POISON CORRECTION (user review): converted enrich_poison from a permanent parking lot into a bounded, alarm-visible, honest-progress circuit breaker — (a) poisonReentryMs config field so poisoned rows auto re-enter the heal scan after the cool-down (no operator); reinitEmbedProvider/reset_pipeline clear the poison table (cause-cleared re-entry); (b) poison count feeds checkAndEscalateEnrichAlarm (non-zero -> at least warn, toward crit with the tick/negative-drain rules) and persists on EnrichAlarmRecord; (c) poisoned_skipped tracked separately from healed; the verdict never reads ok while poisoned_rows>0 (net_drained does not credit parked rows).

RED->GREEN (BL-225): 7 new spec files naming the item. memory-core 731 passed / memory-server 278 / memory-cli 15 / embedding-provider 94 (2 pre-existing write-queue.spec.ts BL-586 failures are the store-adapter agent's fe7c19f3 regression, filed as BL-625). Smoke test summary.failed===0. Commits 9d3e0430 (impl+correction) and b1dbf405 (registry).

Verified via plugin.spec.mjs real-file-reading test + manual negative control (revert-to-pre-fix-shape goes red, restore goes green, diff confirmed byte-identical after restore).
